# Power analysis for testing H0: R² = 0 in linear regression
# Model: y = β₀ + β₁x₁ + β₂x₂ + β₃x₃ + ε
# Parameters:
#   p = 4 (intercept + 3 predictors)
#   k = 3 (numerator df for the F-test)
#   ρ = 0.30 (anticipated multiple correlation)
#   ρ² = 0.09 (squared multiple correlation, the effect size)
#   α = 0.05 (two-sided)
#   Target power = 0.90

library(jsonlite)

# Define parameters
p <- 4  # Number of parameters (intercept + 3 predictors)
k <- p - 1  # Numerator df for F-test
rho <- 0.30  # Multiple correlation
rho_sq <- rho^2  # R² = 0.09
alpha <- 0.05  # Significance level (two-sided)
target_power <- 0.90

# Function to compute power for a given sample size n
compute_power_linear_regression <- function(n, p, rho_sq, alpha) {
  # Denominator df
  df2 <- n - p
  
  # Numerator df
  df1 <- p - 1
  
  # Noncentrality parameter
  lambda <- (rho_sq * (n - p)) / ((1 - rho_sq) * (p - 1))
  
  # Critical value from central F distribution
  f_crit <- qf(1 - alpha, df1, df2)
  
  # Power: P(F > f_crit) under noncentral F distribution
  power <- 1 - pf(f_crit, df1, df2, ncp = lambda)
  
  return(power)
}

# Find minimum sample size by iterating
n_min <- p + 1  # Start with minimum possible sample size
n_max <- 500  # Upper bound for search

sample_sizes <- n_min:n_max
powers <- sapply(sample_sizes, function(n) {
  compute_power_linear_regression(n, p, rho_sq, alpha)
})

# Find the smallest n where power >= target_power
idx <- which(powers >= target_power)[1]
n_optimal <- sample_sizes[idx]
power_achieved <- powers[idx]

# Also report power at n-1 for context
if (idx > 1) {
  n_prev <- sample_sizes[idx - 1]
  power_prev <- powers[idx - 1]
} else {
  n_prev <- NA
  power_prev <- NA
}

# Print results
cat("Minimum sample size for 90% power:\n")
cat("Sample size (n):", n_optimal, "\n")
cat("Achieved power:", round(power_achieved, 6), "\n")
if (!is.na(n_prev)) {
  cat("Power at n =", n_prev, ":", round(power_prev, 6), "\n")
}

# Detailed calculations at optimal n
cat("\n--- Detailed Calculations at n =", n_optimal, "---\n")
df1 <- p - 1
df2 <- n_optimal - p
lambda <- (rho_sq * (n_optimal - p)) / ((1 - rho_sq) * (p - 1))
f_crit <- qf(1 - alpha, df1, df2)

cat("Model: y = β₀ + β₁x₁ + β₂x₂ + β₃x₃ + ε\n")
cat("Total parameters (p):", p, "\n")
cat("Numerator df (p-1):", df1, "\n")
cat("Denominator df (n-p):", df2, "\n")
cat("Multiple correlation (ρ):", rho, "\n")
cat("Squared correlation (R²):", rho_sq, "\n")
cat("Noncentrality parameter (λ):", round(lambda, 6), "\n")
cat("Critical F-value (α=0.05, df1=3, df2=", df2, "):", round(f_crit, 6), "\n")
cat("Power = P(F >", round(f_crit, 6), " | λ =", round(lambda, 6), "):", round(power_achieved, 6), "\n")

# Return result as JSON
result <- list(
  sample_size = n_optimal,
  achieved_power = power_achieved,
  previous_sample_size = n_prev,
  previous_power = power_prev,
  noncentrality_parameter = lambda,
  critical_f_value = f_crit,
  numerator_df = df1,
  denominator_df = df2,
  effect_size_r_squared = rho_sq,
  multiple_correlation = rho,
  alpha = alpha
)

cat("\n")
cat(toJSON(result, auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15))

# Power analysis for testing H0: R² = 0 in linear regression
# Model: y = β₀ + β₁x₁ + β₂x₂ + β₃x₃ + ε
# Parameters:
#   p = 4 (intercept + 3 predictors)
#   k = 3 (numerator df for the F-test)
#   ρ = 0.30 (anticipated multiple correlation)
#   ρ² = 0.09 (squared multiple correlation, the effect size)
#   α = 0.05 (two-sided)
#   Target power = 0.90

library(jsonlite)

# Define parameters
p <- 4  # Number of parameters (intercept + 3 predictors)
k <- p - 1  # Numerator df for F-test
rho <- 0.30  # Multiple correlation
rho_sq <- rho^2  # R² = 0.09
alpha <- 0.05  # Significance level (two-sided)
target_power <- 0.90

# Function to compute power for a given sample size n
compute_power_linear_regression <- function(n, p, rho_sq, alpha) {
  # Denominator df
  df2 <- n - p
  
  # Numerator df
  df1 <- p - 1
  
  # Noncentrality parameter
  lambda <- (rho_sq * (n - p)) / ((1 - rho_sq) * (p - 1))
  
  # Critical value from central F distribution
  f_crit <- qf(1 - alpha, df1, df2)
  
  # Power: P(F > f_crit) under noncentral F distribution
  power <- 1 - pf(f_crit, df1, df2, ncp = lambda)
  
  return(power)
}

# Find minimum sample size by iterating
n_min <- p + 1  # Start with minimum possible sample size
n_max <- 500  # Upper bound for search

sample_sizes <- n_min:n_max
powers <- sapply(sample_sizes, function(n) {
  compute_power_linear_regression(n, p, rho_sq, alpha)
})

# Find the smallest n where power >= target_power
idx <- which(powers >= target_power)[1]
n_optimal <- sample_sizes[idx]
power_achieved <- powers[idx]

# Also report power at n-1 for context
if (idx > 1) {
  n_prev <- sample_sizes[idx - 1]
  power_prev <- powers[idx - 1]
} else {
  n_prev <- NA
  power_prev <- NA
}

# Print results
cat("Minimum sample size for 90% power:\n")
cat("Sample size (n):", n_optimal, "\n")
cat("Achieved power:", round(power_achieved, 6), "\n")
if (!is.na(n_prev)) {
  cat("Power at n =", n_prev, ":", round(power_prev, 6), "\n")
}

# Detailed calculations at optimal n
cat("\n--- Detailed Calculations at n =", n_optimal, "---\n")
df1 <- p - 1
df2 <- n_optimal - p
lambda <- (rho_sq * (n_optimal - p)) / ((1 - rho_sq) * (p - 1))
f_crit <- qf(1 - alpha, df1, df2)

cat("Model: y = β₀ + β₁x₁ + β₂x₂ + β₃x₃ + ε\n")
cat("Total parameters (p):", p, "\n")
cat("Numerator df (p-1):", df1, "\n")
cat("Denominator df (n-p):", df2, "\n")
cat("Multiple correlation (ρ):", rho, "\n")
cat("Squared correlation (R²):", rho_sq, "\n")
cat("Noncentrality parameter (λ):", round(lambda, 6), "\n")
cat("Critical F-value (α=0.05, df1=3, df2=", df2, "):", round(f_crit, 6), "\n")
cat("Power = P(F >", round(f_crit, 6), " | λ =", round(lambda, 6), "):", round(power_achieved, 6), "\n")

# Return result as JSON
result <- list(
  sample_size = n_optimal,
  achieved_power = power_achieved,
  previous_sample_size = n_prev,
  previous_power = power_prev,
  noncentrality_parameter = lambda,
  critical_f_value = f_crit,
  numerator_df = df1,
  denominator_df = df2,
  effect_size_r_squared = rho_sq,
  multiple_correlation = rho,
  alpha = alpha
)

# Balanced 3-by-2 factorial ANOVA design
# Testing main effect of 3-level factor (Factor A)
# Effect size: partial eta-squared = 0.06
# Alpha = 0.05, target power = 0.80
# Balanced design: n participants per cell, 6 cells total

# Step 1: Convert partial eta-squared to non-centrality parameter (lambda)
# For ANOVA F-test: lambda = (f^2 * df_error) / (1 - f^2)
# Or using partial eta-squared: partial_eta^2 = lambda / (lambda + df_error)
# Therefore: lambda = partial_eta^2 * df_error / (1 - partial_eta^2)

partial_eta_sq <- 0.06
alpha <- 0.05
target_power <- 0.80
df_numerator <- 2  # 3 levels - 1 for main effect of Factor A

# Function to compute power given n per cell
compute_power <- function(n_per_cell, partial_eta_sq, df_num, alpha) {
  # Total N = 6 cells * n per cell
  total_N <- 6 * n_per_cell
  # Denominator df in full factorial model: 6(n-1)
  df_denom <- 6 * (n_per_cell - 1)
  
  # Convert partial eta-squared to non-centrality parameter
  # partial_eta^2 = lambda / (lambda + df_denom)
  # Solving for lambda: lambda = partial_eta^2 * df_denom / (1 - partial_eta^2)
  lambda <- (partial_eta_sq * df_denom) / (1 - partial_eta_sq)
  
  # Critical value from central F distribution
  f_crit <- qf(1 - alpha, df_num, df_denom)
  
  # Power is P(F > f_crit) under non-central F with non-centrality lambda
  power <- 1 - pf(f_crit, df_num, df_denom, ncp = lambda)
  
  return(list(
    n_per_cell = n_per_cell,
    total_N = total_N,
    df_numerator = df_num,
    df_denominator = df_denom,
    lambda = lambda,
    f_critical = f_crit,
    power = power
  ))
}

# Search for minimum n that achieves >= 0.80 power
power_results <- list()
for (n in 1:200) {
  result <- compute_power(n, partial_eta_sq, df_numerator, alpha)
  power_results[[n]] <- result
  
  if (n <= 50 || n %% 10 == 0 || (n >= 30 && n <= 60)) {
    cat(sprintf("n=%3d: power=%.6f, df_denom=%3d, lambda=%.4f\n",
                n, result$power, result$df_denominator, result$lambda))
  }
}

# Find minimum n achieving target power
min_n <- NA
for (n in 1:200) {
  if (power_results[[n]]$power >= target_power) {
    min_n <- n
    break
  }
}

cat("\n=== RESULT ===\n")
cat(sprintf("Minimum n per cell for 80%% power: %d\n", min_n))

# Display results for selected sample sizes around minimum
min_result <- power_results[[min_n]]
cat("\nAchieved design (minimum n):\n")
cat(sprintf("  n per cell: %d\n", min_result$n_per_cell))
cat(sprintf("  Total N: %d\n", min_result$total_N))
cat(sprintf("  df_numerator: %d\n", min_result$df_numerator))
cat(sprintf("  df_denominator: %d\n", min_result$df_denominator))
cat(sprintf("  Non-centrality parameter (lambda): %.6f\n", min_result$lambda))
cat(sprintf("  F-critical (alpha=0.05): %.6f\n", min_result$f_critical))
cat(sprintf("  Achieved Power: %.6f\n", min_result$power))

# Check preceding design
if (min_n > 1) {
  prev_result <- power_results[[min_n - 1]]
  cat("\nPreceding admissible design (n-1):\n")
  cat(sprintf("  n per cell: %d\n", prev_result$n_per_cell))
  cat(sprintf("  Total N: %d\n", prev_result$total_N))
  cat(sprintf("  df_denominator: %d\n", prev_result$df_denominator))
  cat(sprintf("  Non-centrality parameter (lambda): %.6f\n", prev_result$lambda))
  cat(sprintf("  F-critical (alpha=0.05): %.6f\n", prev_result$f_critical))
  cat(sprintf("  Power: %.6f\n", prev_result$power))
}

# Store results for final output
final_result <- list(
  min_n_per_cell = min_n,
  achieved_power = min_result$power,
  achieved_df_denom = min_result$df_denominator,
  achieved_lambda = min_result$lambda,
  preceding_power = if (min_n > 1) prev_result$power else NA,
  partial_eta_squared = partial_eta_sq,
  alpha = alpha,
  target_power = target_power
)

# Verification and detailed documentation of the calculation

library(jsonlite)

# Parameters
partial_eta_sq <- 0.06
alpha <- 0.05
target_power <- 0.80
df_numerator <- 2
n_per_cell_minimum <- 27

# Verify the calculation for n=27
n <- n_per_cell_minimum
total_N <- 6 * n
df_denom <- 6 * (n - 1)

# Step 1: Convert partial eta-squared to non-centrality parameter
# Formula: partial_eta^2 = lambda / (lambda + df_denom)
# Rearranged: lambda = partial_eta^2 * df_denom / (1 - partial_eta^2)

lambda <- (partial_eta_sq * df_denom) / (1 - partial_eta_sq)

# Step 2: Get critical F-value at alpha=0.05
f_crit <- qf(1 - alpha, df_numerator, df_denom)

# Step 3: Calculate power using non-central F distribution
power <- 1 - pf(f_crit, df_numerator, df_denom, ncp = lambda)

cat("DETAILED CALCULATION VERIFICATION\n")
cat("===================================\n\n")

cat("Study Parameters:\n")
cat(sprintf("  Factorial design: 3 × 2 (6 cells total)\n"))
cat(sprintf("  Factor A levels: 3\n"))
cat(sprintf("  Factor B levels: 2\n"))
cat(sprintf("  Test hypothesis: Main effect of Factor A (3 levels)\n"))
cat(sprintf("  Effect size (partial η²): %.2f\n", partial_eta_sq))
cat(sprintf("  Significance level (α): %.2f\n", alpha))
cat(sprintf("  Target power: %.2f\n", target_power))
cat(sprintf("  Allocation: Balanced (equal n per cell)\n\n")

cat("Minimum Sample Size Calculation:\n")
cat(sprintf("  n per cell: %d\n", n))
cat(sprintf("  Total N: %d (6 cells × %d per cell)\n", total_N, n))
cat(sprintf("  Numerator df (for Factor A main effect): %d\n", df_numerator))
cat(sprintf("  Denominator df = 6(n-1) = 6(%d-1) = %d\n", n, df_denom))

cat("\nNon-centrality Parameter Conversion:\n")
cat(sprintf("  partial η² = λ / (λ + df_denom)\n"))
cat(sprintf("  %.4f = λ / (λ + %d)\n", partial_eta_sq, df_denom))
cat(sprintf("  λ = %.4f × %d / (1 - %.4f)\n", partial_eta_sq, df_denom, partial_eta_sq))
cat(sprintf("  λ = %.6f\n", lambda))

cat("\nCritical Value and Power:\n")
cat(sprintf("  F-critical = F_{1-α}(%d, %d) = F_{0.95}(%d, %d)\n", 
            df_numerator, df_denom, df_numerator, df_denom))
cat(sprintf("  F-critical = %.6f\n", f_crit))
cat(sprintf("  Power = P(F > %.6f | λ = %.6f) = %.6f\n", f_crit, lambda, power))
cat(sprintf("  Power = %.2f%% (meets 80%% target)\n\n", 100*power))

# Contrast with n-1
n_prev <- n - 1
df_denom_prev <- 6 * (n_prev - 1)
lambda_prev <- (partial_eta_sq * df_denom_prev) / (1 - partial_eta_sq)
f_crit_prev <- qf(1 - alpha, df_numerator, df_denom_prev)
power_prev <- 1 - pf(f_crit_prev, df_numerator, df_denom_prev, ncp = lambda_prev)

cat("Preceding Design (n=26):\n")
cat(sprintf("  Total N: %d\n", 6 * n_prev))
cat(sprintf("  Denominator df: %d\n", df_denom_prev))
cat(sprintf("  λ: %.6f\n", lambda_prev))
cat(sprintf("  Power: %.6f (%.2f%%) — falls short of 80%% target\n", power_prev, 100*power_prev))

cat("\n=== FINAL RESULT ===\n")
cat(sprintf("Minimum integer participants per cell: %d\n", n_per_cell_minimum))

# Prepare JSON output for POWER_AGENT_RESULT
result_data <- list(
  results = list(
    list(
      metric = "sample_size",
      value = as.numeric(n_per_cell_minimum),
      unit = "participants_per_cell"
    ),
    list(
      metric = "achieved_power",
      value = power,
      unit = "proportion"
    ),
    list(
      metric = "total_N",
      value = as.numeric(total_N),
      unit = "participants"
    ),
    list(
      metric = "preceding_power",
      value = power_prev,
      unit = "proportion"
    ),
    list(
      metric = "numerator_degrees_of_freedom",
      value = as.numeric(df_numerator),
      unit = "df"
    ),
    list(
      metric = "denominator_degrees_of_freedom",
      value = as.numeric(df_denom),
      unit = "df"
    ),
    list(
      metric = "non_centrality_parameter",
      value = lambda,
      unit = "lambda"
    ),
    list(
      metric = "f_critical",
      value = f_crit,
      unit = "F-value"
    )
  )
)

cat("\n")
cat("POWER_AGENT_RESULT=", toJSON(result_data, auto_unbox=TRUE, digits=15), "\n", sep="")

cat("  lambda = eta^2 * df_error / (1 - eta^2)\n\n")

scientific_notes: Partial eta-squared is used as the standardized effect-size measure for the main effect in factorial ANOVA

# Balanced 3-by-2 factorial ANOVA design
# Testing main effect of 3-level factor (Factor A)
# Effect size: partial eta-squared = 0.06
# Alpha = 0.05, target power = 0.80
# Balanced design: n participants per cell, 6 cells total

# Step 1: Convert partial eta-squared to non-centrality parameter (lambda)
# For ANOVA F-test: lambda = (f^2 * df_error) / (1 - f^2)
# Or using partial eta-squared: partial_eta^2 = lambda / (lambda + df_error)
# Therefore: lambda = partial_eta^2 * df_error / (1 - partial_eta^2)

partial_eta_sq <- 0.06
alpha <- 0.05
target_power <- 0.80
df_numerator <- 2  # 3 levels - 1 for main effect of Factor A

# Function to compute power given n per cell
compute_power <- function(n_per_cell, partial_eta_sq, df_num, alpha) {
  # Total N = 6 cells * n per cell
  total_N <- 6 * n_per_cell
  # Denominator df in full factorial model: 6(n-1)
  df_denom <- 6 * (n_per_cell - 1)
  
  # Convert partial eta-squared to non-centrality parameter
  # partial_eta^2 = lambda / (lambda + df_denom)
  # Solving for lambda: lambda = partial_eta^2 * df_denom / (1 - partial_eta^2)
  lambda <- (partial_eta_sq * df_denom) / (1 - partial_eta_sq)
  
  # Critical value from central F distribution
  f_crit <- qf(1 - alpha, df_num, df_denom)
  
  # Power is P(F > f_crit) under non-central F with non-centrality lambda
  power <- 1 - pf(f_crit, df_num, df_denom, ncp = lambda)
  
  return(list(
    n_per_cell = n_per_cell,
    total_N = total_N,
    df_numerator = df_num,
    df_denominator = df_denom,
    lambda = lambda,
    f_critical = f_crit,
    power = power
  ))
}

# Search for minimum n that achieves >= 0.80 power
power_results <- list()
for (n in 1:200) {
  result <- compute_power(n, partial_eta_sq, df_numerator, alpha)
  power_results[[n]] <- result
  
  if (n <= 50 || n %% 10 == 0 || (n >= 30 && n <= 60)) {
    cat(sprintf("n=%3d: power=%.6f, df_denom=%3d, lambda=%.4f\n",
                n, result$power, result$df_denominator, result$lambda))
  }
}

# Find minimum n achieving target power
min_n <- NA
for (n in 1:200) {
  if (power_results[[n]]$power >= target_power) {
    min_n <- n
    break
  }
}

cat("\n=== RESULT ===\n")
cat(sprintf("Minimum n per cell for 80%% power: %d\n", min_n))

# Display results for selected sample sizes around minimum
min_result <- power_results[[min_n]]
cat("\nAchieved design (minimum n):\n")
cat(sprintf("  n per cell: %d\n", min_result$n_per_cell))
cat(sprintf("  Total N: %d\n", min_result$total_N))
cat(sprintf("  df_numerator: %d\n", min_result$df_numerator))
cat(sprintf("  df_denominator: %d\n", min_result$df_denominator))
cat(sprintf("  Non-centrality parameter (lambda): %.6f\n", min_result$lambda))
cat(sprintf("  F-critical (alpha=0.05): %.6f\n", min_result$f_critical))
cat(sprintf("  Achieved Power: %.6f\n", min_result$power))

# Check preceding design
if (min_n > 1) {
  prev_result <- power_results[[min_n - 1]]
  cat("\nPreceding admissible design (n-1):\n")
  cat(sprintf("  n per cell: %d\n", prev_result$n_per_cell))
  cat(sprintf("  Total N: %d\n", prev_result$total_N))
  cat(sprintf("  df_denominator: %d\n", prev_result$df_denominator))
  cat(sprintf("  Non-centrality parameter (lambda): %.6f\n", prev_result$lambda))
  cat(sprintf("  F-critical (alpha=0.05): %.6f\n", prev_result$f_critical))
  cat(sprintf("  Power: %.6f\n", prev_result$power))
}

# Store results for final output
final_result <- list(
  min_n_per_cell = min_n,
  achieved_power = min_result$power,
  achieved_df_denom = min_result$df_denominator,
  achieved_lambda = min_result$lambda,
  preceding_power = if (min_n > 1) prev_result$power else NA,
  partial_eta_squared = partial_eta_sq,
  alpha = alpha,
  target_power = target_power
)

# Balanced 3-by-2 factorial ANOVA design
# Testing main effect of 3-level factor (Factor A)
# Effect size: partial eta-squared = 0.06
# Alpha = 0.05, target power = 0.80

partial_eta_sq <- 0.06
alpha <- 0.05
target_power <- 0.80
df_numerator <- 2  # 3 levels - 1 for main effect of Factor A

# Function to compute power given n per cell
compute_power <- function(n_per_cell, partial_eta_sq, df_num, alpha) {
  if (n_per_cell < 2) return(NA)  # Need at least 2 per cell
  
  # Total N = 6 cells * n per cell
  total_N <- 6 * n_per_cell
  # Denominator df in full factorial model: 6(n-1)
  df_denom <- 6 * (n_per_cell - 1)
  
  # Convert partial eta-squared to non-centrality parameter
  # partial_eta^2 = lambda / (lambda + df_denom)
  # Solving for lambda: lambda = partial_eta^2 * df_denom / (1 - partial_eta^2)
  lambda <- (partial_eta_sq * df_denom) / (1 - partial_eta_sq)
  
  # Critical value from central F distribution
  f_crit <- qf(1 - alpha, df_num, df_denom)
  
  # Power is P(F > f_crit) under non-central F with non-centrality lambda
  power <- 1 - pf(f_crit, df_num, df_denom, ncp = lambda)
  
  return(list(
    n_per_cell = n_per_cell,
    total_N = total_N,
    df_numerator = df_num,
    df_denominator = df_denom,
    lambda = lambda,
    f_critical = f_crit,
    power = power
  ))
}

# Search for minimum n that achieves >= 0.80 power
cat("Power analysis by sample size per cell:\n")
cat("n | power\n")
cat("--|-------\n")

min_n <- NA
for (n in 2:100) {
  result <- compute_power(n, partial_eta_sq, df_numerator, alpha)
  
  # Print selected values
  if (n <= 30 || n %% 5 == 0) {
    cat(sprintf("%2d | %.6f\n", n, result$power))
  }
  
  # Check for minimum n achieving target power
  if (is.na(min_n) && result$power >= target_power) {
    min_n <- n
  }
}

# Get results for minimum n and preceding n
min_result <- compute_power(min_n, partial_eta_sq, df_numerator, alpha)
prev_result <- compute_power(min_n - 1, partial_eta_sq, df_numerator, alpha)

cat("\n=== SAMPLE SIZE CALCULATION RESULTS ===\n\n")
cat("Study Design: Balanced 3×2 Factorial ANOVA\n")
cat("Testing: Main effect of 3-level Factor A\n")
cat("Effect size (partial η²): 0.06\n")
cat("Alpha: 0.05 (one-sided)\n")
cat("Target Power: 0.80\n\n")

cat("MINIMUM SAMPLE SIZE (achieves target power):\n")
cat(sprintf("  Participants per cell: %d\n", min_result$n_per_cell))
cat(sprintf("  Total N across 6 cells: %d\n", min_result$total_N))
cat(sprintf("  Numerator df: %d\n", min_result$df_numerator))
cat(sprintf("  Denominator df: %d\n", min_result$df_denominator))
cat(sprintf("  Non-centrality (λ): %.6f\n", min_result$lambda))
cat(sprintf("  F-critical (α=0.05): %.6f\n", min_result$f_critical))
cat(sprintf("  Achieved Power: %.6f (%.2f%%)\n", min_result$power, 100*min_result$power))

cat("\nPRECEDING DESIGN (n-1):\n")
cat(sprintf("  Participants per cell: %d\n", prev_result$n_per_cell))
cat(sprintf("  Total N across 6 cells: %d\n", prev_result$total_N))
cat(sprintf("  Denominator df: %d\n", prev_result$df_denominator))
cat(sprintf("  Non-centrality (λ): %.6f\n", prev_result$lambda))
cat(sprintf("  Power: %.6f (%.2f%%)\n", prev_result$power, 100*prev_result$power))

cat("\n=== VERIFICATION ===\n")
cat(sprintf("Achieved power (%.2f%%) >= Target (%.2f%%): %s\n", 
            100*min_result$power, 100*target_power, 
            min_result$power >= target_power))

# Evidence e1; success=false

# Balanced 3-by-2 factorial ANOVA design
# Testing main effect of 3-level factor (Factor A)
# Effect size: partial eta-squared = 0.06
# Alpha = 0.05, target power = 0.80
# Balanced design: n participants per cell, 6 cells total

# Step 1: Convert partial eta-squared to non-centrality parameter (lambda)
# For ANOVA F-test: lambda = (f^2 * df_error) / (1 - f^2)
# Or using partial eta-squared: partial_eta^2 = lambda / (lambda + df_error)
# Therefore: lambda = partial_eta^2 * df_error / (1 - partial_eta^2)

partial_eta_sq <- 0.06
alpha <- 0.05
target_power <- 0.80
df_numerator <- 2  # 3 levels - 1 for main effect of Factor A

# Function to compute power given n per cell
compute_power <- function(n_per_cell, partial_eta_sq, df_num, alpha) {
  # Total N = 6 cells * n per cell
  total_N <- 6 * n_per_cell
  # Denominator df in full factorial model: 6(n-1)
  df_denom <- 6 * (n_per_cell - 1)
  
  # Convert partial eta-squared to non-centrality parameter
  # partial_eta^2 = lambda / (lambda + df_denom)
  # Solving for lambda: lambda = partial_eta^2 * df_denom / (1 - partial_eta^2)
  lambda <- (partial_eta_sq * df_denom) / (1 - partial_eta_sq)

# Two-sample t-test sample size calculation
# H0: μ_treatment = μ_control vs H1: μ_treatment ≠ μ_control (one-sided)
# Parameters:
# - Expected difference: 4.3 dBA
# - Common SD: 7.8 dBA
# - Alpha: 0.05 (one-sided)
# - Target power: 0.8
# - Allocation: 1:1

# Load power package for sample size calculation
library(pwr)

delta <- 4.3  # effect size (difference in means)
sd_common <- 7.8  # common standard deviation
alpha <- 0.05
target_power <- 0.8
allocation_ratio <- 1  # 1:1 allocation

# Standardized effect size for t-test (Cohen's d)
# d = delta / sd
cohens_d <- delta / sd_common

cat("Study Design Parameters:\n")
cat("Expected difference (delta):", delta, "dBA\n")
cat("Common standard deviation:", sd_common, "dBA\n")
cat("Standardized effect size (Cohen's d):", round(cohens_d, 4), "\n")
cat("Alpha:", alpha, "(one-sided)\n")
cat("Target power:", target_power, "\n")
cat("Allocation ratio:", allocation_ratio, ":1\n\n")

# Use pwr.t.test for two-sample t-test
# For one-sided test, use 'one.sided' specification
# Note: pwr.t.test with alternative='one.sided' uses one-sided alternative
result <- pwr.t.test(
  d = cohens_d,
  n = NULL,  # Calculate n
  sig.level = alpha,
  power = target_power,
  type = "two.sample",
  alternative = "one.sided"
)

cat("Power Calculation Results:\n")
cat("Sample size per group (continuous solution):", round(result$n, 3), "\n")

# Round up to next integer
n_per_group <- ceiling(result$n)
cat("Sample size per group (integer, rounded up):", n_per_group, "\n")
cat("Total sample size:", n_per_group * 2, "\n\n")

# Verify achieved power at this sample size
power_achieved <- pwr.t.test(
  d = cohens_d,
  n = n_per_group,
  sig.level = alpha,
  type = "two.sample",
  alternative = "one.sided"
)$power

cat("Achieved power at n =", n_per_group, "per group:", round(power_achieved, 4), "\n")

# Check power at n-1 to confirm this is the minimum
power_preceding <- pwr.t.test(
  d = cohens_d,
  n = n_per_group - 1,
  sig.level = alpha,
  type = "two.sample",
  alternative = "one.sided"
)$power

cat("Power at n =", n_per_group - 1, "per group:", round(power_preceding, 4), "\n\n")

# Additional validation using base R t-distribution
# Non-centrality parameter for one-sided test
lambda <- cohens_d * sqrt(n_per_group / 2)  # sqrt(n1*n2/(n1+n2)) * d = sqrt(n/2) * d for equal n
t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha, df = 2 * n_per_group - 2)
power_base_r <- 1 - pt(t_crit, df = 2 * n_per_group - 2, ncp = lambda)

cat("Verification using base R t-distribution:\n")
cat("Non-centrality parameter (lambda):", round(lambda, 4), "\n")
cat("Critical t-value:", round(t_crit, 4), "\n")
cat("Power (1 - Type II error):", round(power_base_r, 4), "\n\n")

# Output in structured format
cat("FINAL ANSWER:\n")
cat("Minimum sample size per group:", n_per_group, "participants\n")
cat("Total sample size:", n_per_group * 2, "participants\n")
cat("Achieved power:", round(power_achieved, 4), "\n")

# Prepare JSON output
results <- list(
  sample_size_per_group = n_per_group,
  total_sample_size = n_per_group * 2,
  achieved_power = round(power_achieved, 4),
  power_preceding_design = round(power_preceding, 4),
  continuous_solution = round(result$n, 3),
  cohens_d = round(cohens_d, 4),
  lambda = round(lambda, 4),
  verification_power = round(power_base_r, 4)
)

cat("\n")
cat("POWER_AGENT_RESULT=", jsonlite::toJSON(list(results = list(
  list(metric = "sample_size", value = n_per_group, unit = "participants_per_group"),
  list(metric = "total_sample_size", value = n_per_group * 2, unit = "participants"),
  list(metric = "achieved_power", value = round(power_achieved, 4), unit = "proportion"),
  list(metric = "power_at_preceding_design", value = round(power_preceding, 4), unit = "proportion"),
  list(metric = "continuous_solution", value = round(result$n, 3), unit = "participants_per_group"),
  list(metric = "cohens_d", value = round(cohens_d, 4), unit = "standardized_effect_size")
)), auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15), sep = "")

# Independent verification of two-sample t-test sample size calculation
# Design: One-sided test, H0: μ1 = μ2 vs H1: μ1 > μ2 (or similar directional)
# Given: delta = 4.3 dBA, sd_common = 7.8 dBA, alpha = 0.05, target power = 0.8

library(pwr)

# Input parameters
delta <- 4.3
sd_common <- 7.8
alpha <- 0.05
target_power <- 0.8
cohens_d <- delta / sd_common

cat("=== INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION ===\n\n")
cat("Input Parameters:\n")
cat("Effect size (delta):", delta, "dBA\n")
cat("Common SD:", sd_common, "dBA\n")
cat("Cohen's d:", round(cohens_d, 6), "\n")
cat("Alpha (one-sided):", alpha, "\n")
cat("Target power:", target_power, "\n")
cat("Allocation: 1:1\n\n")

# Method 1: Using pwr.t.test with alternative='greater'
result_greater <- pwr.t.test(
  d = cohens_d,
  n = NULL,
  sig.level = alpha,
  power = target_power,
  type = "two.sample",
  alternative = "greater"
)

cat("Method 1 - pwr.t.test(alternative='greater'):\n")
cat("Continuous solution (n per group):", round(result_greater$n, 6), "\n")
cat("Minimum integer (ceiling):", ceiling(result_greater$n), "\n\n")

# Method 2: Manual calculation using non-centrality parameter
# For two-sample t-test with equal n per group:
# Non-centrality = d * sqrt(n_total / 2) = d * sqrt(n_per_group)
# df = n_total - 2 = 2*n - 2
# Critical value: t_alpha = qt(1 - alpha, df)
# Power = 1 - P(T < t_alpha | ncp = non_centrality)

cat("Method 2 - Manual NCP approach:\n")

# Function to compute power given n per group
compute_power_manual <- function(n_per_group, d, alpha) {
  n_total <- 2 * n_per_group
  df <- n_total - 2
  t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha, df)
  ncp <- d * sqrt(n_per_group)  # sqrt(n_per_group) because sqrt(n1*n2/(n1+n2)) = sqrt(n/2)*sqrt(2) = sqrt(n)
  # Actually, ncp = d * sqrt((n1*n2)/(n1+n2)) = d * sqrt(n^2/(2n)) = d * sqrt(n/2)
  ncp_correct <- d * sqrt(n_per_group / 2)
  power <- 1 - pt(t_crit, df, ncp = ncp_correct)
  return(power)
}

# Verify power at n=42
power_at_42 <- compute_power_manual(42, cohens_d, alpha)
cat("Power at n=42 per group:", round(power_at_42, 6), "\n")

# Verify power at n=41
power_at_41 <- compute_power_manual(41, cohens_d, alpha)
cat("Power at n=41 per group:", round(power_at_41, 6), "\n\n")

# Method 3: Using pwr.t.test to verify power at specific n values
verify_42 <- pwr.t.test(d = cohens_d, n = 42, sig.level = alpha, 
                        type = "two.sample", alternative = "greater")
verify_41 <- pwr.t.test(d = cohens_d, n = 41, sig.level = alpha, 
                        type = "two.sample", alternative = "greater")

cat("Method 3 - pwr.t.test verification:\n")
cat("Power at n=42:", round(verify_42$power, 6), "\n")
cat("Power at n=41:", round(verify_41$power, 6), "\n\n")

# Cross-check with uniroot to find exact minimum n for target power
find_min_n <- function(target_power_val, d, alpha) {
  lower_n <- 1
  upper_n <- 200
  
  # Binary search
  while (upper_n - lower_n > 0.01) {
    mid_n <- (lower_n + upper_n) / 2
    power_mid <- compute_power_manual(mid_n, d, alpha)
    
    if (power_mid < target_power_val) {
      lower_n <- mid_n
    } else {
      upper_n <- mid_n
    }
  }
  return((lower_n + upper_n) / 2)
}

continuous_sol <- find_min_n(target_power, cohens_d, alpha)
cat("Binary search for continuous minimum n:", round(continuous_sol, 6), "\n")
cat("Ceiling to integer:", ceiling(continuous_sol), "\n\n")

# Final summary
min_n_integer <- ceiling(continuous_sol)
power_achieved <- compute_power_manual(min_n_integer, cohens_d, alpha)
power_preceding <- compute_power_manual(min_n_integer - 1, cohens_d, alpha)

cat("=== FINAL VERIFICATION RESULTS ===\n")
cat("Minimum sample size (per group):", min_n_integer, "\n")
cat("Total sample size:", min_n_integer * 2, "\n")
cat("Achieved power at n =", min_n_integer, ":", round(power_achieved, 4), "\n")
cat("Power at preceding design (n =", min_n_integer - 1, "):", round(power_preceding, 4), "\n")
cat("Continuous solution:", round(continuous_sol, 3), "\n")
cat("Cohen's d:", round(cohens_d, 4), "\n\n")

# Check assumptions and test specification
cat("=== ASSUMPTIONS AND SPECIFICATION CHECKS ===\n")

cat("✓ 1:1 allocation ratio\n")
cat("✓ One-sided test (directional alternative, 'greater')\n")
cat("✓ Alpha = 0.05 (one-sided)\n")
cat("✓ Target power = 0.80\n")
cat("✓ Effect size = 4.3 / 7.8 = Cohen's d =", round(cohens_d, 4), "\n")
cat("✓ Test statistic follows non-central t with df = 82 and ncp = 2.526\n\n")

# Output structured results
cat("POWER_AGENT_RESULT=", jsonlite::toJSON(
  list(
    results = list(
      list(metric = "sample_size", value = min_n_integer, unit = "participants_per_group"),
      list(metric = "total_sample_size", value = min_n_integer * 2, unit = "participants"),
      list(metric = "achieved_power", value = round(power_achieved, 4), unit = "proportion"),
      list(metric = "power_at_preceding_design", value = round(power_preceding, 4), unit = "proportion"),
      list(metric = "continuous_solution", value = round(continuous_sol, 3), unit = "participants_per_group"),
      list(metric = "cohens_d", value = round(cohens_d, 4), unit = "standardized_effect_size"),
      list(metric = "test_specification", value = "one-sided t-test, df=82", unit = "string")
    )
  ),

  digits = 15
), sep = "")

# Monte Carlo simulation to validate power calculation
# Simulate:
# 1. Type I error rate under H0 (delta = 0)
# 2. Power under H1 (delta = 4.3)
# Both at n = 42 per group, one-sided t-test, alpha = 0.05

set.seed(12345)

n_per_group <- 42
delta <- 4.3
sd_common <- 7.8
alpha <- 0.05
nsim <- 10000

cat("=== MONTE CARLO VALIDATION ===\n\n")
cat("Simulation parameters:\n")
cat("n per group:", n_per_group, "\n")
cat("Total n:", n_per_group * 2, "\n")
cat("Expected effect (delta):", delta, "dBA\n")
cat("Common SD:", sd_common, "dBA\n")
cat("Replications:", nsim, "\n")
cat("Random seed: 12345\n\n")

# Test 1: Type I error under H0 (both groups from N(0, sd_common))
cat("TEST 1: Type I Error (H0 true: delta = 0)\n")
cat("-------------------------------------------\n")

reject_h0_count <- 0

for (i in 1:nsim) {
  group1 <- rnorm(n_per_group, mean = 0, sd = sd_common)
  group2 <- rnorm(n_per_group, mean = 0, sd = sd_common)
  
  # Conduct one-sided t-test (H1: group1 > group2)
  t_stat <- t.test(group1, group2, alternative = "greater", 
                   var.equal = TRUE)$statistic
  
  # One-sided critical value at alpha = 0.05
  df <- 2 * n_per_group - 2
  t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha, df)
  
  if (t_stat > t_crit) {
    reject_h0_count <- reject_h0_count + 1
  }
}

type1_error_simulated <- reject_h0_count / nsim
type1_error_se <- sqrt(type1_error_simulated * (1 - type1_error_simulated) / nsim)

cat("Simulated Type I error rate:", round(type1_error_simulated, 4), "\n")
cat("95% CI:", round(type1_error_simulated - 1.96 * type1_error_se, 4), "to", 
    round(type1_error_simulated + 1.96 * type1_error_se, 4), "\n")
cat("Expected (nominal alpha): 0.05\n")
cat("Status: ", ifelse(abs(type1_error_simulated - 0.05) < 2.5 * type1_error_se, 
                         "✓ PASS (within 2.5 SE)", "✗ FAIL"), "\n\n")

# Test 2: Power under H1 (group1 ~ N(4.3, 7.8), group2 ~ N(0, 7.8))
cat("TEST 2: Power (H1 true: delta = 4.3)\n")
cat("------------------------------------\n")

reject_h1_count <- 0

for (i in 1:nsim) {
  group1 <- rnorm(n_per_group, mean = delta, sd = sd_common)
  group2 <- rnorm(n_per_group, mean = 0, sd = sd_common)
  
  # Conduct one-sided t-test (H1: group1 > group2)
  t_stat <- t.test(group1, group2, alternative = "greater", 
                   var.equal = TRUE)$statistic
  
  # One-sided critical value at alpha = 0.05
  df <- 2 * n_per_group - 2
  t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha, df)
  
  if (t_stat > t_crit) {
    reject_h1_count <- reject_h1_count + 1
  }
}

power_simulated <- reject_h1_count / nsim
power_se <- sqrt(power_simulated * (1 - power_simulated) / nsim)

cat("Simulated power:", round(power_simulated, 4), "\n")
cat("95% CI:", round(power_simulated - 1.96 * power_se, 4), "to", 
    round(power_simulated + 1.96 * power_se, 4), "\n")
cat("Theoretical power (from pwr package): 0.8052\n")
cat("Difference:", round(power_simulated - 0.8052, 4), "\n")
cat("Status: ", ifelse(abs(power_simulated - 0.8052) < 2.5 * power_se, 
                         "✓ PASS (within 2.5 SE)", "✗ FAIL"), "\n\n")

cat("=== SUMMARY ===\n")
cat("Type I error rate (nominal 0.05):", round(type1_error_simulated, 4), "\n")
cat("Power under H1 (target 0.80):", round(power_simulated, 4), "\n")
cat("Theoretical power (pwr::pwr.t.test):", 0.8052, "\n")
cat("Simulation matches theory: ", 
    ifelse(abs(power_simulated - 0.8052) < 0.015, "YES ✓", "QUESTIONABLE"), "\n\n")

# Output JSON
cat("POWER_AGENT_RESULT=", jsonlite::toJSON(
  list(
    simulation = list(
      seed = 12345,
      trials = nsim,
      type1_error = round(type1_error_simulated, 4),
      type1_error_se = round(type1_error_se, 4),
      power = round(power_simulated, 4),
      power_se = round(power_se, 4),
      theoretical_power = 0.8052,
      difference_from_theory = round(power_simulated - 0.8052, 4)
    )
  ),
  auto_unbox = TRUE,
  digits = 15
), sep = "")

# Two-sample t-test sample size calculation
# H0: μ_treatment = μ_control vs H1: μ_treatment ≠ μ_control (one-sided)
# Parameters:
# - Expected difference: 4.3 dBA
# - Common SD: 7.8 dBA
# - Alpha: 0.05 (one-sided)
# - Target power: 0.8
# - Allocation: 1:1

# Load power package for sample size calculation
library(pwr)

delta <- 4.3  # effect size (difference in means)
sd_common <- 7.8  # common standard deviation
alpha <- 0.05
target_power <- 0.8
allocation_ratio <- 1  # 1:1 allocation

# Standardized effect size for t-test (Cohen's d)
# d = delta / sd
cohens_d <- delta / sd_common

cat("Study Design Parameters:\n")
cat("Expected difference (delta):", delta, "dBA\n")
cat("Common standard deviation:", sd_common, "dBA\n")
cat("Standardized effect size (Cohen's d):", round(cohens_d, 4), "\n")
cat("Alpha:", alpha, "(one-sided)\n")
cat("Target power:", target_power, "\n")
cat("Allocation ratio:", allocation_ratio, ":1\n\n")

# Use pwr.t.test for two-sample t-test
# For one-sided test, use 'one.sided' specification
# Note: pwr.t.test with alternative='one.sided' uses one-sided alternative
result <- pwr.t.test(
  d = cohens_d,
  n = NULL,  # Calculate n
  sig.level = alpha,
  power = target_power,
  type = "two.sample",
  alternative = "one.sided"
)

cat("Power Calculation Results:\n")
cat("Sample size per group (continuous solution):", round(result$n, 3), "\n")

# Round up to next integer
n_per_group <- ceiling(result$n)
cat("Sample size per group (integer, rounded up):", n_per_group, "\n")
cat("Total sample size:", n_per_group * 2, "\n\n")

# Verify achieved power at this sample size
power_achieved <- pwr.t.test(
  d = cohens_d,
  n = n_per_group,
  sig.level = alpha,
  type = "two.sample",
  alternative = "one.sided"
)$power

cat("Achieved power at n =", n_per_group, "per group:", round(power_achieved, 4), "\n")

# Check power at n-1 to confirm this is the minimum
power_preceding <- pwr.t.test(
  d = cohens_d,
  n = n_per_group - 1,
  sig.level = alpha,
  type = "two.sample",
  alternative = "one.sided"
)$power

cat("Power at n =", n_per_group - 1, "per group:", round(power_preceding, 4), "\n\n")

# Additional validation using base R t-distribution
# Non-centrality parameter for one-sided test
lambda <- cohens_d * sqrt(n_per_group / 2)  # sqrt(n1*n2/(n1+n2)) * d = sqrt(n/2) * d for equal n
t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha, df = 2 * n_per_group - 2)
power_base_r <- 1 - pt(t_crit, df = 2 * n_per_group - 2, ncp = lambda)

cat("Verification using base R t-distribution:\n")
cat("Non-centrality parameter (lambda):", round(lambda, 4), "\n")
cat("Critical t-value:", round(t_crit, 4), "\n")
cat("Power (1 - Type II error):", round(power_base_r, 4), "\n\n")

# Output in structured format
cat("FINAL ANSWER:\n")
cat("Minimum sample size per group:", n_per_group, "participants\n")
cat("Total sample size:", n_per_group * 2, "participants\n")
cat("Achieved power:", round(power_achieved, 4), "\n")

# Prepare JSON output
results <- list(
  sample_size_per_group = n_per_group,
  total_sample_size = n_per_group * 2,
  achieved_power = round(power_achieved, 4),
  power_preceding_design = round(power_preceding, 4),
  continuous_solution = round(result$n, 3),
  cohens_d = round(cohens_d, 4),
  lambda = round(lambda, 4),
  verification_power = round(power_base_r, 4)
)

cat("\n")
cat("POWER_AGENT_RESULT=", jsonlite::toJSON(list(results = list(
  list(metric = "sample_size", value = n_per_group, unit = "participants_per_group"),
  list(metric = "total_sample_size", value = n_per_group * 2, unit = "participants"),
  list(metric = "achieved_power", value = round(power_achieved, 4), unit = "proportion"),

)), auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15), sep = "")

# Independent verification of two-sample t-test sample size calculation
# Design: One-sided test, H0: μ1 = μ2 vs H1: μ1 > μ2 (or similar directional)
# Given: delta = 4.3 dBA, sd_common = 7.8 dBA, alpha = 0.05, target power = 0.8

library(pwr)

# Input parameters
delta <- 4.3
sd_common <- 7.8
alpha <- 0.05
target_power <- 0.8
cohens_d <- delta / sd_common

cat("=== INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION ===\n\n")
cat("Input Parameters:\n")
cat("Effect size (delta):", delta, "dBA\n")
cat("Common SD:", sd_common, "dBA\n")
cat("Cohen's d:", round(cohens_d, 6), "\n")
cat("Alpha (one-sided):", alpha, "\n")
cat("Target power:", target_power, "\n")
cat("Allocation: 1:1\n\n")

# Method 1: Using pwr.t.test with alternative='greater'
result_greater <- pwr.t.test(
  d = cohens_d,
  n = NULL,
  sig.level = alpha,
  power = target_power,
  type = "two.sample",
  alternative = "greater"
)

cat("Method 1 - pwr.t.test(alternative='greater'):\n")
cat("Continuous solution (n per group):", round(result_greater$n, 6), "\n")
cat("Minimum integer (ceiling):", ceiling(result_greater$n), "\n\n")

# Method 2: Manual calculation using non-centrality parameter
# For two-sample t-test with equal n per group:
# Non-centrality = d * sqrt(n_total / 2) = d * sqrt(n_per_group)
# df = n_total - 2 = 2*n - 2
# Critical value: t_alpha = qt(1 - alpha, df)
# Power = 1 - P(T < t_alpha | ncp = non_centrality)

cat("Method 2 - Manual NCP approach:\n")

# Function to compute power given n per group
compute_power_manual <- function(n_per_group, d, alpha) {
  n_total <- 2 * n_per_group
  df <- n_total - 2
  t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha, df)
  ncp <- d * sqrt(n_per_group)  # sqrt(n_per_group) because sqrt(n1*n2/(n1+n2)) = sqrt(n/2)*sqrt(2) = sqrt(n)
  # Actually, ncp = d * sqrt((n1*n2)/(n1+n2)) = d * sqrt(n^2/(2n)) = d * sqrt(n/2)
  ncp_correct <- d * sqrt(n_per_group / 2)
  power <- 1 - pt(t_crit, df, ncp = ncp_correct)
  return(power)
}

# Verify power at n=42
power_at_42 <- compute_power_manual(42, cohens_d, alpha)
cat("Power at n=42 per group:", round(power_at_42, 6), "\n")

# Verify power at n=41
power_at_41 <- compute_power_manual(41, cohens_d, alpha)
cat("Power at n=41 per group:", round(power_at_41, 6), "\n\n")

# Method 3: Using pwr.t.test to verify power at specific n values
verify_42 <- pwr.t.test(d = cohens_d, n = 42, sig.level = alpha, 
                        type = "two.sample", alternative = "greater")
verify_41 <- pwr.t.test(d = cohens_d, n = 41, sig.level = alpha, 
                        type = "two.sample", alternative = "greater")

cat("Method 3 - pwr.t.test verification:\n")
cat("Power at n=42:", round(verify_42$power, 6), "\n")
cat("Power at n=41:", round(verify_41$power, 6), "\n\n")

# Cross-check with uniroot to find exact minimum n for target power
find_min_n <- function(target_power_val, d, alpha) {
  lower_n <- 1
  upper_n <- 200
  
  # Binary search
  while (upper_n - lower_n > 0.01) {
    mid_n <- (lower_n + upper_n) / 2
    power_mid <- compute_power_manual(mid_n, d, alpha)
    
    if (power_mid < target_power_val) {
      lower_n <- mid_n
    } else {
      upper_n <- mid_n
    }
  }
  return((lower_n + upper_n) / 2)
}

continuous_sol <- find_min_n(target_power, cohens_d, alpha)
cat("Binary search for continuous minimum n:", round(continuous_sol, 6), "\n")
cat("Ceiling to integer:", ceiling(continuous_sol), "\n\n")

# Final summary
min_n_integer <- ceiling(continuous_sol)
power_achieved <- compute_power_manual(min_n_integer, cohens_d, alpha)
power_preceding <- compute_power_manual(min_n_integer - 1, cohens_d, alpha)

cat("=== FINAL VERIFICATION RESULTS ===\n")
cat("Minimum sample size (per group):", min_n_integer, "\n")
cat("Total sample size:", min_n_integer * 2, "\n")
cat("Achieved power at n =", min_n_integer, ":", round(power_achieved, 4), "\n")
cat("Power at preceding design (n =", min_n_integer - 1, "):", round(power_preceding, 4), "\n")
cat("Continuous solution:", round(continuous_sol, 3), "\n")
cat("Cohen's d:", round(cohens_d, 4), "\n\n")

# Check assumptions and test specification
cat("=== ASSUMPTIONS AND SPECIFICATION CHECKS ===\n")
cat("✓ Two independent normal groups\n")
cat("✓ Equal variances (pooled t-test)\n")
cat("✓ 1:1 allocation ratio\n")
cat("✓ One-sided test (directional alternative, 'greater')\n")
cat("✓ Alpha = 0.05 (one-sided)\n")
cat("✓ Target power = 0.80\n")
cat("✓ Effect size = 4.3 / 7.8 = Cohen's d =", round(cohens_d, 4), "\n")
cat("✓ Test statistic follows non-central t with df = 82 and ncp = 2.526\n\n")

# Output structured results
cat("POWER_AGENT_RESULT=", jsonlite::toJSON(
  list(
    results = list(
      list(metric = "sample_size", value = min_n_integer, unit = "participants_per_group"),
      list(metric = "total_sample_size", value = min_n_integer * 2, unit = "participants"),
      list(metric = "achieved_power", value = round(power_achieved, 4), unit = "proportion"),
      list(metric = "power_at_preceding_design", value = round(power_preceding, 4), unit = "proportion"),
      list(metric = "continuous_solution", value = round(continuous_sol, 3), unit = "participants_per_group"),
      list(metric = "cohens_d", value = round(cohens_d, 4), unit = "standardized_effect_size"),
      list(metric = "test_specification", value = "one-sided t-test, df=82", unit = "string")
    )
  ),

# Monte Carlo simulation to validate power calculation
# Simulate:
# 1. Type I error rate under H0 (delta = 0)
# 2. Power under H1 (delta = 4.3)
# Both at n = 42 per group, one-sided t-test, alpha = 0.05

set.seed(12345)

n_per_group <- 42
delta <- 4.3
sd_common <- 7.8
alpha <- 0.05
nsim <- 10000

cat("=== MONTE CARLO VALIDATION ===\n\n")
cat("Simulation parameters:\n")
cat("n per group:", n_per_group, "\n")
cat("Total n:", n_per_group * 2, "\n")
cat("Expected effect (delta):", delta, "dBA\n")
cat("Common SD:", sd_common, "dBA\n")
cat("Replications:", nsim, "\n")
cat("Random seed: 12345\n\n")

# Test 1: Type I error under H0 (both groups from N(0, sd_common))
cat("TEST 1: Type I Error (H0 true: delta = 0)\n")
cat("-------------------------------------------\n")

reject_h0_count <- 0

for (i in 1:nsim) {
  group1 <- rnorm(n_per_group, mean = 0, sd = sd_common)
  group2 <- rnorm(n_per_group, mean = 0, sd = sd_common)
  
  # Conduct one-sided t-test (H1: group1 > group2)
  t_stat <- t.test(group1, group2, alternative = "greater", 
                   var.equal = TRUE)$statistic
  
  # One-sided critical value at alpha = 0.05
  df <- 2 * n_per_group - 2
  t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha, df)
  
  if (t_stat > t_crit) {
    reject_h0_count <- reject_h0_count + 1
  }
}

type1_error_simulated <- reject_h0_count / nsim
type1_error_se <- sqrt(type1_error_simulated * (1 - type1_error_simulated) / nsim)

cat("Simulated Type I error rate:", round(type1_error_simulated, 4), "\n")
cat("95% CI:", round(type1_error_simulated - 1.96 * type1_error_se, 4), "to", 
    round(type1_error_simulated + 1.96 * type1_error_se, 4), "\n")
cat("Expected (nominal alpha): 0.05\n")
cat("Status: ", ifelse(abs(type1_error_simulated - 0.05) < 2.5 * type1_error_se, 
                         "✓ PASS (within 2.5 SE)", "✗ FAIL"), "\n\n")

# Test 2: Power under H1 (group1 ~ N(4.3, 7.8), group2 ~ N(0, 7.8))
cat("TEST 2: Power (H1 true: delta = 4.3)\n")
cat("------------------------------------\n")

reject_h1_count <- 0

for (i in 1:nsim) {
  group1 <- rnorm(n_per_group, mean = delta, sd = sd_common)
  group2 <- rnorm(n_per_group, mean = 0, sd = sd_common)
  
  # Conduct one-sided t-test (H1: group1 > group2)
  t_stat <- t.test(group1, group2, alternative = "greater", 
                   var.equal = TRUE)$statistic
  
  # One-sided critical value at alpha = 0.05
  df <- 2 * n_per_group - 2
  t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha, df)
  
  if (t_stat > t_crit) {
    reject_h1_count <- reject_h1_count + 1
  }
}

power_simulated <- reject_h1_count / nsim

# Evidence e1; success=false

# Two-sample t-test sample size calculation
# H0: μ_treatment = μ_control vs H1: μ_treatment ≠ μ_control (one-sided)
# Parameters:
# - Expected difference: 4.3 dBA
# - Common SD: 7.8 dBA
# - Alpha: 0.05 (one-sided)
# - Target power: 0.8
# - Allocation: 1:1

# Load power package for sample size calculation
library(pwr)

delta <- 4.3  # effect size (difference in means)
sd_common <- 7.8  # common standard deviation
alpha <- 0.05
target_power <- 0.8
allocation_ratio <- 1  # 1:1 allocation

# Standardized effect size for t-test (Cohen's d)
# d = delta / sd
cohens_d <- delta / sd_common

cat("Study Design Parameters:\n")
cat("Expected difference (delta):", delta, "dBA\n")
cat("Common standard deviation:", sd_common, "dBA\n")
cat("Standardized effect size (Cohen's d):", round(cohens_d, 4), "\n")
cat("Alpha:", alpha, "(one-sided)\n")
cat("Target power:", target_power, "\n")
cat("Allocation ratio:", allocation_ratio, ":1\n\n")

# Use pwr.t.test for two-sample t-test
# For one-sided test, use 'one.sided' specification
# Note: pwr.t.test with alternative='one.sided' uses one-sided alternative
result <- pwr.t.test(
  d = cohens_d,
  n = NULL,  # Calculate n
  sig.level = alpha,
  power = target_power,
  type = "two.sample",
  alternative = "one.sided"
)

cat("Power Calculation Results:\n")
cat("Sample size per group (continuous solution):", round(result$n, 3), "\n")

# Round up to next integer
n_per_group <- ceiling(result$n)
cat("Sample size per group (integer, rounded up):", n_per_group, "\n")
cat("Total sample size:", n_per_group * 2, "\n\n")

# Verify achieved power at this sample size
power_achieved <- pwr.t.test(
  d = cohens_d,
  n = n_per_group,
  sig.level = alpha,
  type = "two.sample",
  alternative = "one.sided"
)$power

cat("Achieved power at n =", n_per_group, "per group:", round(power_achieved, 4), "\n")

# Check power at n-1 to confirm this is the minimum
power_preceding <- pwr.t.test(
  d = cohens_d,
  n = n_per_group - 1,
  sig.level = alpha,
  type = "two.sample",
  alternative = "one.sided"
)$power

cat("Power at n =", n_per_group - 1, "per group:", round(power_preceding, 4), "\n\n")

# Additional validation using base R t-distribution
# Non-centrality parameter for one-sided test
lambda <- cohens_d * sqrt(n_per_group / 2)  # sqrt(n1*n2/(n1+n2)) * d = sqrt(n/2) * d for equal n
t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha, df = 2 * n_per_group - 2)
power_base_r <- 1 - pt(t_crit, df = 2 * n_per_group - 2, ncp = lambda)

cat("Verification using base R t-distribution:\n")
cat("Non-centrality parameter (lambda):", round(lambda, 4), "\n")
cat("Critical t-value:", round(t_crit, 4), "\n")
cat("Power (1 - Type II error):", round(power_base_r, 4), "\n\n")

# Output in structured format
cat("FINAL ANSWER:\n")
cat("Minimum sample size per group:", n_per_group, "participants\n")
cat("Total sample size:", n_per_group * 2, "participants\n")
cat("Achieved power:", round(power_achieved, 4), "\n")

# Prepare JSON output
results <- list(
  sample_size_per_group = n_per_group,
  total_sample_size = n_per_group * 2,
  achieved_power = round(power_achieved, 4),
  power_preceding_design = round(power_preceding, 4),
  continuous_solution = round(result$n, 3),
  cohens_d = round(cohens_d, 4),
  lambda = round(lambda, 4),
  verification_power = round(power_base_r, 4)
)

cat("\n")
cat("POWER_AGENT_RESULT=", jsonlite::toJSON(list(results = list(
  list(metric = "sample_size", value = n_per_group, unit = "participants_per_group"),
  list(metric = "total_sample_size", value = n_per_group * 2, unit = "participants"),
  list(metric = "achieved_power", value = round(power_achieved, 4), unit = "proportion"),
  list(metric = "power_at_preceding_design", value = round(power_preceding, 4), unit = "proportion"),
  list(metric = "continuous_solution", value = round(result$n, 3), unit = "participants_per_group"),
  list(metric = "cohens_d", value = round(cohens_d, 4), unit = "standardized_effect_size")
)), auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15), sep = "")

# One-sample t-test power calculation
# H0: μ = 0 vs H1: μ > 0 (one-sided)
# Parameters
n <- 25                    # sample size (participants)
mean_diff <- 0.2          # hypothesized mean increase
sd <- 0.5                 # standard deviation
alpha <- 0.05             # significance level (one-sided)

# Calculate Cohen's d (effect size)
cohens_d <- mean_diff / sd

# Non-centrality parameter for t-distribution
# ncp = (mean_diff / (sd / sqrt(n))) = (mean_diff * sqrt(n)) / sd
ncp <- (mean_diff * sqrt(n)) / sd

# Degrees of freedom
df <- n - 1

# Critical t-value for one-sided test at alpha = 0.05
critical_t <- qt(1 - alpha, df)

# Power is the probability of rejecting H0 when H1 is true
# P(t > critical_t | ncp) under the non-central t-distribution
power <- 1 - pt(critical_t, df, ncp = ncp)

# Summary
cat("One-Sample t-test Power Calculation\n")
cat("=" , rep("=", 40), "\n")
cat("Hypothesis: H0: μ = 0 vs H1: μ > 0 (one-sided)\n")
cat("Significance level (α): ", alpha, "\n")
cat("Sample size (n): ", n, " participants\n")
cat("Mean difference: ", mean_diff, " units\n")
cat("Standard deviation (SD): ", sd, " units\n")
cat("Cohen's d: ", round(cohens_d, 4), "\n")
cat("Degrees of freedom: ", df, "\n")
cat("Non-centrality parameter: ", round(ncp, 4), "\n")
cat("Critical t-value: ", round(critical_t, 4), "\n")
cat("Power: ", round(power, 4), "\n")

# Output result in required format
POWER_AGENT_RESULT <- list(
  results = list(
    list(metric = "power", value = round(power, 15), unit = "probability")
  ),
  simulation = NULL
)

cat("\nPOWER_AGENT_RESULT=", jsonlite::toJSON(POWER_AGENT_RESULT, auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15))

# Monte Carlo simulation verification
set.seed(42)

n <- 25
mean_diff <- 0.2
sd <- 0.5
alpha <- 0.05
nsim <- 100000

# Simulate data under the alternative hypothesis
# H1: true mean = mean_diff
reject_count <- 0

for (i in 1:nsim) {
  # Generate sample from normal distribution with mean = mean_diff
  sample <- rnorm(n, mean = mean_diff, sd = sd)
  
  # Perform one-sample t-test: H0: μ = 0
  t_stat <- (mean(sample) - 0) / (sd(sample) / sqrt(n))
  
  # One-sided critical value
  crit_t <- qt(1 - alpha, n - 1)
  
  # Reject if t_stat > critical value (upper tail)
  if (t_stat > crit_t) {
    reject_count <- reject_count + 1
  }
}

# Empirical power
empirical_power <- reject_count / nsim

# Standard error
se <- sqrt(empirical_power * (1 - empirical_power) / nsim)

cat("Monte Carlo Simulation Verification\n")
cat("=" , rep("=", 50), "\n")
cat("Simulations: ", nsim, "\n")
cat("Seed: 42\n")
cat("Rejections: ", reject_count, "\n")
cat("Empirical power: ", round(empirical_power, 15), "\n")
cat("Standard error: ", round(se, 6), "\n")
cat("95% CI: [", round(empirical_power - 1.96*se, 6), ", ", 
    round(empirical_power + 1.96*se, 6), "]\n\n")

# Compare to theoretical power
df <- n - 1
ncp <- (mean_diff * sqrt(n)) / sd
critical_t <- qt(1 - alpha, df)
theoretical_power <- 1 - pt(critical_t, df, ncp = ncp)

cat("Theoretical power: ", round(theoretical_power, 15), "\n")
cat("Difference: ", round(abs(empirical_power - theoretical_power), 6), "\n")

# Output
POWER_AGENT_RESULT <- list(
  results = list(
    list(metric = "power", value = round(theoretical_power, 15), unit = "probability")
  ),
  simulation = list(
    seed = 42,

    confidence_interval = list(
      round(empirical_power - 1.96*se, 15),

    )
  )
)

# One-sample t-test power calculation
# H0: μ = 0 vs H1: μ > 0 (one-sided)
# Parameters
n <- 25                    # sample size (participants)
mean_diff <- 0.2          # hypothesized mean increase
sd <- 0.5                 # standard deviation
alpha <- 0.05             # significance level (one-sided)

# Calculate Cohen's d (effect size)
cohens_d <- mean_diff / sd

# Non-centrality parameter for t-distribution
# ncp = (mean_diff / (sd / sqrt(n))) = (mean_diff * sqrt(n)) / sd
ncp <- (mean_diff * sqrt(n)) / sd

# Degrees of freedom
df <- n - 1

# Critical t-value for one-sided test at alpha = 0.05
critical_t <- qt(1 - alpha, df)

# Power is the probability of rejecting H0 when H1 is true
# P(t > critical_t | ncp) under the non-central t-distribution
power <- 1 - pt(critical_t, df, ncp = ncp)

# Summary
cat("One-Sample t-test Power Calculation\n")
cat("=" , rep("=", 40), "\n")
cat("Hypothesis: H0: μ = 0 vs H1: μ > 0 (one-sided)\n")
cat("Significance level (α): ", alpha, "\n")
cat("Sample size (n): ", n, " participants\n")
cat("Mean difference: ", mean_diff, " units\n")
cat("Standard deviation (SD): ", sd, " units\n")
cat("Cohen's d: ", round(cohens_d, 4), "\n")
cat("Degrees of freedom: ", df, "\n")
cat("Non-centrality parameter: ", round(ncp, 4), "\n")
cat("Critical t-value: ", round(critical_t, 4), "\n")
cat("Power: ", round(power, 4), "\n")

# Output result in required format
POWER_AGENT_RESULT <- list(
  results = list(
    list(metric = "power", value = round(power, 15), unit = "probability")
  ),
  simulation = NULL
)

cat("\nPOWER_AGENT_RESULT=", jsonlite::toJSON(POWER_AGENT_RESULT, auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15))

# Monte Carlo simulation verification
set.seed(42)

n <- 25
mean_diff <- 0.2
sd <- 0.5
alpha <- 0.05
nsim <- 100000

# Simulate data under the alternative hypothesis
# H1: true mean = mean_diff
reject_count <- 0

for (i in 1:nsim) {
  # Generate sample from normal distribution with mean = mean_diff
  sample <- rnorm(n, mean = mean_diff, sd = sd)
  
  # Perform one-sample t-test: H0: μ = 0
  t_stat <- (mean(sample) - 0) / (sd(sample) / sqrt(n))
  
  # One-sided critical value
  crit_t <- qt(1 - alpha, n - 1)
  
  # Reject if t_stat > critical value (upper tail)
  if (t_stat > crit_t) {
    reject_count <- reject_count + 1
  }
}

# Empirical power
empirical_power <- reject_count / nsim

# Standard error
se <- sqrt(empirical_power * (1 - empirical_power) / nsim)

cat("Monte Carlo Simulation Verification\n")
cat("=" , rep("=", 50), "\n")
cat("Simulations: ", nsim, "\n")
cat("Seed: 42\n")
cat("Rejections: ", reject_count, "\n")
cat("Empirical power: ", round(empirical_power, 15), "\n")
cat("Standard error: ", round(se, 6), "\n")
cat("95% CI: [", round(empirical_power - 1.96*se, 6), ", ", 
    round(empirical_power + 1.96*se, 6), "]\n\n")

# Compare to theoretical power
df <- n - 1
ncp <- (mean_diff * sqrt(n)) / sd
critical_t <- qt(1 - alpha, df)
theoretical_power <- 1 - pt(critical_t, df, ncp = ncp)

cat("Theoretical power: ", round(theoretical_power, 15), "\n")
cat("Difference: ", round(abs(empirical_power - theoretical_power), 6), "\n")

# Output
POWER_AGENT_RESULT <- list(
  results = list(
    list(metric = "power", value = round(theoretical_power, 15), unit = "probability")
  ),
  simulation = list(
    seed = 42,
    trials = nsim,
    failures = 0,
    mcse = round(se, 15),
    confidence_interval = list(
      round(empirical_power - 1.96*se, 15),
      round(empirical_power + 1.96*se, 15)
    )
  )
)

cat("\nPOWER_AGENT_RESULT=", jsonlite::toJSON(POWER_AGENT_RESULT, auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15))

# Independent analytical verification
# H0: μ = 0 vs H1: μ > 0 (one-sided, upper-tail test)
# Parameters from request
n <- 25
mean_diff <- 0.2
sd <- 0.5
alpha <- 0.05

# Step 1: Effect size (Cohen's d)
d <- mean_diff / sd
cat("Effect size (Cohen's d):", d, "\n")

# Step 2: Non-centrality parameter
# For one-sample t-test: ncp = (μ1 - μ0) / (σ / √n) = d × √n
ncp <- d * sqrt(n)
cat("Non-centrality parameter ncp:", ncp, "\n")

# Step 3: Critical t-value for one-sided test
df <- n - 1
t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha, df)
cat("Critical t-value (df=24, α=0.05 one-sided):", t_crit, "\n")

# Step 4: Power calculation
# Power = P(T > t_crit | H1 true) = 1 - F_nct(t_crit; df, ncp)
power_analytical <- 1 - pt(t_crit, df, ncp = ncp)
cat("\nAnalytical power (non-central t-distribution):", power_analytical, "\n")

# Verify formula consistency
cat("\n--- Formula Verification ---\n")
cat("t-statistic under H1: t = (ȳ - 0) / (s/√n) ~ t(df=24, ncp=2)\n")
cat("Rejection region: t > ", round(t_crit, 4), "\n")
cat("Power = P(t > ", round(t_crit, 4), " | ncp=", ncp, ") = ", 
    round(power_analytical, 6), "\n")

# Double-check with alternative formulation
# Using the property that if X ~ N(μ, σ²), then Z = (X - 0)/(σ/√n) ~ N(ncp, 1)
# But for small samples, we use the t-distribution with ncp parameter
power_check <- 1 - pt(t_crit, df, ncp = ncp)
cat("\nPower (double-check):", power_check, "\n")

# Output in required format
POWER_AGENT_RESULT <- list(
  results = list(
    list(metric = "power", value = power_analytical, unit = "probability")
  )
)

cat("\nFinal Result:\n")
cat("POWER_AGENT_RESULT=", jsonlite::toJSON(POWER_AGENT_RESULT, auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15))

# Independent Monte Carlo verification
set.seed(42)

n <- 25
mean_diff <- 0.2
sd <- 0.5
alpha <- 0.05
nsim <- 100000

# Critical t-value
crit_t <- qt(1 - alpha, n - 1)

# Simulate rejections
rejections <- 0

for (i in 1:nsim) {
  # Generate sample under H1: μ = mean_diff
  sample_data <- rnorm(n, mean = mean_diff, sd = sd)
  
  # Calculate t-statistic
  sample_mean <- mean(sample_data)
  sample_sd <- sd(sample_data)
  t_stat <- (sample_mean - 0) / (sample_sd / sqrt(n))
  
  # Count rejections (one-sided, upper tail)
  if (t_stat > crit_t) {
    rejections <- rejections + 1
  }
}

empirical_power <- rejections / nsim
se_binomial <- sqrt(empirical_power * (1 - empirical_power) / nsim)

cat("Monte Carlo Verification (Independent)\n")
cat("=====================================\n")
cat("Simulations: ", nsim, "\n")
cat("Seed: 42\n")
cat("Rejections: ", rejections, "\n")
cat("Empirical Power: ", round(empirical_power, 15), "\n")
cat("Standard Error (Binomial): ", round(se_binomial, 15), "\n")

# 95% CI
ci_lower <- empirical_power - 1.96 * se_binomial
ci_upper <- empirical_power + 1.96 * se_binomial
cat("95% CI: [", round(ci_lower, 15), ", ", round(ci_upper, 15), "]\n\n")

# Theoretical power
df <- n - 1
ncp <- (mean_diff * sqrt(n)) / sd
crit_t_check <- qt(1 - alpha, df)
theoretical_power <- 1 - pt(crit_t_check, df, ncp = ncp)

cat("Theoretical power: ", round(theoretical_power, 15), "\n")
cat("Difference (empirical - theoretical): ", round(empirical_power - theoretical_power, 6), "\n")
cat("Within 95% CI? ", (ci_lower <= theoretical_power) & (theoretical_power <= ci_upper), "\n")

# Evidence e1; success=true

# One-sample t-test power calculation
# H0: μ = 0 vs H1: μ > 0 (one-sided)
# Parameters
n <- 25                    # sample size (participants)
mean_diff <- 0.2          # hypothesized mean increase
sd <- 0.5                 # standard deviation
alpha <- 0.05             # significance level (one-sided)

# Calculate Cohen's d (effect size)
cohens_d <- mean_diff / sd

# Non-centrality parameter for t-distribution
# ncp = (mean_diff / (sd / sqrt(n))) = (mean_diff * sqrt(n)) / sd
ncp <- (mean_diff * sqrt(n)) / sd

# Degrees of freedom
df <- n - 1

# Critical t-value for one-sided test at alpha = 0.05
critical_t <- qt(1 - alpha, df)

# Power is the probability of rejecting H0 when H1 is true
# P(t > critical_t | ncp) under the non-central t-distribution
power <- 1 - pt(critical_t, df, ncp = ncp)

# Summary
cat("One-Sample t-test Power Calculation\n")
cat("=" , rep("=", 40), "\n")
cat("Hypothesis: H0: μ = 0 vs H1: μ > 0 (one-sided)\n")
cat("Significance level (α): ", alpha, "\n")
cat("Sample size (n): ", n, " participants\n")
cat("Mean difference: ", mean_diff, " units\n")
cat("Standard deviation (SD): ", sd, " units\n")
cat("Cohen's d: ", round(cohens_d, 4), "\n")
cat("Degrees of freedom: ", df, "\n")
cat("Non-centrality parameter: ", round(ncp, 4), "\n")
cat("Critical t-value: ", round(critical_t, 4), "\n")
cat("Power: ", round(power, 4), "\n")

# Output result in required format
POWER_AGENT_RESULT <- list(
  results = list(
    list(metric = "power", value = round(power, 15), unit = "probability")
  ),
  simulation = NULL
)

cat("\nPOWER_AGENT_RESULT=", jsonlite::toJSON(POWER_AGENT_RESULT, auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15))

# Verify using pwr package (widely used for power analysis)
library(pwr)

# Parameters
n <- 25
mean_diff <- 0.2
sd <- 0.5
alpha <- 0.05

# Calculate effect size (Cohen's d)
cohens_d <- mean_diff / sd

# Use pwr.t.test for one-sample t-test
# type = "one.sample", alternative = "greater" for one-sided upper-tail test
result_pwr <- pwr.t.test(n = n, d = cohens_d, sig.level = alpha, 
                          type = "one.sample", alternative = "greater")

cat("Verification using pwr package:\n")
cat("=" , rep("=", 40), "\n")
cat("Cohen's d: ", cohens_d, "\n")
cat("Sample size: ", n, "\n")
cat("Alpha: ", alpha, "\n")
cat("One-sided test (greater)\n")
cat("Power from pwr: ", round(result_pwr$power, 15), "\n")

# Also verify manually with pt function
df <- n - 1
ncp <- cohens_d * sqrt(n)
critical_t <- qt(1 - alpha, df)
power_manual <- 1 - pt(critical_t, df, ncp = ncp)

cat("\nManual verification:\n")
cat("Non-centrality parameter: ", ncp, "\n")
cat("Critical t-value: ", critical_t, "\n")
cat("Power (manual): ", round(power_manual, 15), "\n")

# Output in required format

  results = list(
    list(metric = "power", value = round(result_pwr$power, 15), unit = "probability")
  ),
  simulation = NULL
)

cat("\nPOWER_AGENT_RESULT=", jsonlite::toJSON(POWER_AGENT_RESULT, auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15))


# Evidence e3; success=true

# Monte Carlo simulation verification
set.seed(42)

n <- 25
mean_diff <- 0.2
sd <- 0.5
alpha <- 0.05
nsim <- 100000

# Simulate data under the alternative hypothesis
# H1: true mean = mean_diff
reject_count <- 0

for (i in 1:nsim) {
  # Generate sample from normal distribution with mean = mean_diff
  sample <- rnorm(n, mean = mean_diff, sd = sd)
  
  # Perform one-sample t-test: H0: μ = 0
  t_stat <- (mean(sample) - 0) / (sd(sample) / sqrt(n))
  
  # One-sided critical value
  crit_t <- qt(1 - alpha, n - 1)
  
  # Reject if t_stat > critical value (upper tail)
  if (t_stat > crit_t) {
    reject_count <- reject_count + 1
  }
}

# Empirical power
empirical_power <- reject_count / nsim

# Standard error
se <- sqrt(empirical_power * (1 - empirical_power) / nsim)

cat("Monte Carlo Simulation Verification\n")
cat("=" , rep("=", 50), "\n")
cat("Simulations: ", nsim, "\n")
cat("Seed: 42\n")
cat("Rejections: ", reject_count, "\n")
cat("Empirical power: ", round(empirical_power, 15), "\n")
cat("Standard error: ", round(se, 6), "\n")
cat("95% CI: [", round(empirical_power - 1.96*se, 6), ", ", 
    round(empirical_power + 1.96*se, 6), "]\n\n")

# Compare to theoretical power
df <- n - 1
ncp <- (mean_diff * sqrt(n)) / sd
critical_t <- qt(1 - alpha, df)
theoretical_power <- 1 - pt(critical_t, df, ncp = ncp)

cat("Theoretical power: ", round(theoretical_power, 15), "\n")
cat("Difference: ", round(abs(empirical_power - theoretical_power), 6), "\n")

# Output
POWER_AGENT_RESULT <- list(
  results = list(
    list(metric = "power", value = round(theoretical_power, 15), unit = "probability")
  ),
  simulation = list(
    seed = 42,
    trials = nsim,
    failures = 0,
    mcse = round(se, 15),
    confidence_interval = list(
      round(empirical_power - 1.96*se, 15),
      round(empirical_power + 1.96*se, 15)
    )
  )
)

cat("\nPOWER_AGENT_RESULT=", jsonlite::toJSON(POWER_AGENT_RESULT, auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15))

answer.summary: For a paired t-test with one-sided α = 0.05 testing for a mean weight reduction of 3 kg, baseline SD = 5 kg, follow-up SD = 5.5 kg, and within-person correlation r = 0.5, the minimum number of participants required to achieve 80% power is **21 participants**. This design achieves 80.92% power; the preceding design (n = 20) provides 79.09% power, falling below the 80% target.
answer.method: Paired t-test sample size inversion using the non-central t-distribution. The standard deviation of paired differences was calculated as SD(diff) = √[SD_baseline² + SD_followup² - 2·r·SD_baseline·SD_followup] = √27.75 = 5.268 kg. The effect size (Cohen's d for paired samples) is d = mean_diff / SD(diff) = 3 / 5.268 = 0.5695. For each candidate sample size n, power is calculated as P(t > t_{α,n-1} | λ = d√n) using the non-central t-distribution with df = n−1. The minimum integer n where achieved power ≥ 0.80 is identified by iterative evaluation.

# Paired t-test sample size calculation
# Parameters
mean_diff <- 3  # kg - expected weight reduction
sd_baseline <- 5  # kg
sd_followup <- 5.5  # kg
r <- 0.5  # within-person correlation
alpha <- 0.05  # one-sided test
target_power <- 0.80

# Calculate SD of the difference
# SD_diff = sqrt(SD_baseline^2 + SD_followup^2 - 2*r*SD_baseline*SD_followup)
sd_diff <- sqrt(sd_baseline^2 + sd_followup^2 - 2*r*sd_baseline*sd_followup)
cat("SD of paired differences:", sd_diff, "kg\n")

# Calculate effect size (Cohen's d for paired data)
cohens_d <- mean_diff / sd_diff
cat("Cohen's d (paired):", cohens_d, "\n")

# Critical value for one-sided test at alpha=0.05
# We'll use iterative approach to find n where achieved power = 0.80
# For paired t-test: t_crit = qt(1 - alpha, df = n-1)
# Non-centrality parameter: lambda = d * sqrt(n)
# Power = 1 - pt(t_crit, df=n-1, ncp=lambda)

library(stats)

# Function to calculate power for given sample size (paired t-test)
power_paired_t <- function(n, effect_size, alpha = 0.05, one_sided = TRUE) {
  df <- n - 1
  
  # Critical value (one-sided)
  if (one_sided) {
    t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha, df = df)
  } else {
    t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha/2, df = df)
  }
  
  # Non-centrality parameter
  ncp <- effect_size * sqrt(n)
  
  # Power calculation
  power <- 1 - pt(t_crit, df = df, ncp = ncp)
  
  return(power)
}

# Find minimum sample size for target power = 0.80
sample_sizes <- 2:500
powers <- sapply(sample_sizes, function(n) power_paired_t(n, cohens_d, alpha, one_sided = TRUE))

# Find minimum n where power >= 0.80
min_n <- sample_sizes[which(powers >= target_power)[1]]
achieved_power_min_n <- powers[which(sample_sizes == min_n)[1]]

cat("\n--- Sample Size Calculation ---\n")
cat("Minimum sample size for 80% power:", min_n, "participants\n")
cat("Achieved power at n =", min_n, ":", round(achieved_power_min_n, 4), "\n")

# Also report power at n-1 to show the crossing
if (min_n > 2) {
  prev_n <- min_n - 1
  prev_power <- power_paired_t(prev_n, cohens_d, alpha, one_sided = TRUE)
  cat("Power at n =", prev_n, ":", round(prev_power, 4), "\n")
  cat("Power improvement from n =", prev_n, "to n =", min_n, ":",
      round(achieved_power_min_n - prev_power, 4), "\n")
}

# Display a range for verification
cat("\n--- Power by Sample Size ---\n")
verification_ns <- c(15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40, 45, 50)
for (n in verification_ns) {
  pw <- power_paired_t(n, cohens_d, alpha, one_sided = TRUE)
  cat(sprintf("n = %3d: Power = %.4f %s\n", n, pw, if (pw >= 0.80) "[✓ meets target]" else ""))
}

# Emit result
result <- data.frame(
  metric = "sample_size",
  value = min_n,
  unit = "participants_total"
)

cat("\n--- Final Result ---\n")
print(result)

# Independent verification of paired t-test sample size
# Using the pwr package and manual calculation

library(pwr)
library(stats)

# Input parameters
mean_diff <- 3  # kg
sd_baseline <- 5  # kg
sd_followup <- 5.5  # kg
r <- 0.5  # within-person correlation
alpha <- 0.05  # one-sided
target_power <- 0.80

cat("=== INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION ===\n\n")

# Step 1: Verify SD of differences calculation
cat("1. SD OF PAIRED DIFFERENCES\n")
cat("   Formula: SD_diff = sqrt(SD_b^2 + SD_f^2 - 2*r*SD_b*SD_f)\n")
sd_diff_manual <- sqrt(sd_baseline^2 + sd_followup^2 - 2*r*sd_baseline*sd_followup)
cat("   Calculation: sqrt(5^2 + 5.5^2 - 2*0.5*5*5.5)\n")
cat("   = sqrt(25 + 30.25 - 27.5)\n")
cat("   = sqrt(27.75)\n")
cat("   = ", sd_diff_manual, "\n\n")

# Step 2: Calculate effect size
cat("2. EFFECT SIZE (Cohen's d for paired data)\n")
cohens_d <- mean_diff / sd_diff_manual
cat("   d = mean_diff / SD_diff\n")
cat("   d = 3 / ", sd_diff_manual, "\n")
cat("   d = ", cohens_d, "\n\n")

# Step 3: Use pwr package to calculate sample size
# Note: pwr.t.test for paired samples uses d and type="paired"
cat("3. SAMPLE SIZE USING pwr PACKAGE\n")
result_pwr <- pwr.t.test(d = cohens_d, sig.level = alpha, power = target_power, 
                         type = "paired", alternative = "greater")
cat("   pwr.t.test result:\n")
print(result_pwr)
cat("\n")

# Step 4: Manual verification using non-central t-distribution
cat("4. MANUAL VERIFICATION USING NON-CENTRAL T-DISTRIBUTION\n")

power_at_n <- function(n, d, alpha) {
  df <- n - 1
  t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha, df = df)  # one-sided critical value
  ncp <- d * sqrt(n)  # non-centrality parameter
  power <- 1 - pt(t_crit, df = df, ncp = ncp)
  return(power)
}

# Test a range of sample sizes
test_ns <- c(19, 20, 21, 22, 23, 24, 25)
cat("   Sample Size | Power\n")
cat("   -----------|--------\n")
for (n in test_ns) {
  pw <- power_at_n(n, cohens_d, alpha)
  marker <- ifelse(pw >= 0.80, "✓", "")
  cat(sprintf("   %3d         | %.4f %s\n", n, pw, marker))
}

cat("\n")

# Step 5: Identify minimum sample size
min_n_manual <- NA
for (n in 2:1000) {
  if (power_at_n(n, cohens_d, alpha) >= 0.80) {
    min_n_manual <- n
    break
  }
}

cat("5. MINIMUM SAMPLE SIZE FOR 80% POWER\n")
cat("   Minimum n (manual): ", min_n_manual, "\n")
cat("   Power at n=", min_n_manual, ": ", power_at_n(min_n_manual, cohens_d, alpha), "\n")
cat("   Power at n=", min_n_manual-1, ": ", power_at_n(min_n_manual-1, cohens_d, alpha), "\n\n")

# Step 6: Comparison
cat("6. COMPARISON OF RESULTS\n")
cat("   Candidate answer: n = 21\n")
cat("   Manual calculation: n = ", min_n_manual, "\n")
cat("   pwr package result: n = ", ceiling(result_pwr$n), "\n")

if (min_n_manual == 21) {
  cat("   ✓ All methods agree\n")
} else {
  cat("   ⚠ Methods disagree\n")
}

cat("\n")

# Step 7: Detailed power calculation at n=21 to show the mathematics
cat("7. DETAILED CALCULATION AT n=21\n")
n <- 21
df <- n - 1
t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha, df = df)
ncp <- cohens_d * sqrt(n)
power_n21 <- 1 - pt(t_crit, df = df, ncp = ncp)

cat("   Degrees of freedom df = n-1 = ", df, "\n")
cat("   Critical value t_{0.05,", df, "} = ", t_crit, "\n")
cat("   Non-centrality parameter λ = d*sqrt(n) = ", cohens_d, " * sqrt(", n, ") = ", ncp, "\n")
cat("   Power = 1 - P(T_{", df, "} ≤ ", t_crit, " | λ=", ncp, ")\n")
cat("   Power = 1 - pt(", t_crit, ", df=", df, ", ncp=", ncp, ")\n")
cat("   Power = ", power_n21, "\n\n")

# Emit results
POWER_AGENT_RESULT <- list(
  results = list(
    list(metric = "minimum_sample_size", value = min_n_manual, unit = "participants_total"),
    list(metric = "achieved_power_at_minimum_n", value = round(power_at_n(min_n_manual, cohens_d, alpha), 4), unit = "proportion"),
    list(metric = "power_at_n_minus_1", value = round(power_at_n(min_n_manual - 1, cohens_d, alpha), 4), unit = "proportion"),
    list(metric = "verification_status", value = ifelse(min_n_manual == 21, "pass", "fail"), unit = "text")
  )
)

cat("  SD_followup = ", sd_f, "\n")
cat("  r (correlation) = ", r, "\n\n")

cat("FORMULA 1: SD_diff = sqrt(SD_b^2 + SD_f^2 - 2*r*SD_b*SD_f)\n")
cat("This is the standard formula for the SD of a difference of two correlated variables.\n")
cat("Derivation: Var(X - Y) = Var(X) + Var(Y) - 2*Cov(X,Y)\n")
cat("           = SD_X^2 + SD_Y^2 - 2*r*SD_X*SD_Y\n")
cat("SD_diff = sqrt(Var(X-Y))\n\n")

sd_diff_formula1 <- sqrt(sd_b^2 + sd_f^2 - 2*r*sd_b*sd_f)
cat("Calculation: sqrt(5^2 + 5.5^2 - 2*0.5*5*5.5)\n")
cat("           = sqrt(25 + 30.25 - 27.5)\n")
cat("           = sqrt(27.75)\n")
cat("           = ", sd_diff_formula1, "\n\n")

cat("FORMULA 2: Alternative - if independent (no correlation)\n")
sd_diff_formula2 <- sqrt(sd_b^2 + sd_f^2)
cat("SD_diff = sqrt(SD_b^2 + SD_f^2)\n")
cat("        = sqrt(25 + 30.25)\n")
cat("        = sqrt(55.25)\n")
cat("        = ", sd_diff_formula2, "\n")
cat("(NOT appropriate here since r=0.5)\n\n")

cat("VERIFICATION: The candidate used Formula 1, which is CORRECT.\n\n")

# Verify this is consistent with the pwr package interpretation
cat("=== CONSISTENCY WITH pwr PACKAGE ===\n\n")

cat("                            = 3 / ", sd_diff_formula1, "\n")
cat("                            = ", cohens_d, "\n\n")

cat("  Required sample size = ", result_pwr$n, "\n")
cat("  Ceiling (integer) = ", ceiling(result_pwr$n), "\n")
cat("  This confirms n = 21 is the minimum integer sample size.\n\n")

# Paired t-test sample size calculation
# Parameters
mean_diff <- 3  # kg - expected weight reduction
sd_baseline <- 5  # kg
sd_followup <- 5.5  # kg
r <- 0.5  # within-person correlation
alpha <- 0.05  # one-sided test
target_power <- 0.80

# Calculate SD of the difference
# SD_diff = sqrt(SD_baseline^2 + SD_followup^2 - 2*r*SD_baseline*SD_followup)
sd_diff <- sqrt(sd_baseline^2 + sd_followup^2 - 2*r*sd_baseline*sd_followup)
cat("SD of paired differences:", sd_diff, "kg\n")

# Calculate effect size (Cohen's d for paired data)
cohens_d <- mean_diff / sd_diff
cat("Cohen's d (paired):", cohens_d, "\n")

# Critical value for one-sided test at alpha=0.05
# We'll use iterative approach to find n where achieved power = 0.80
# For paired t-test: t_crit = qt(1 - alpha, df = n-1)
# Non-centrality parameter: lambda = d * sqrt(n)
# Power = 1 - pt(t_crit, df=n-1, ncp=lambda)

library(stats)

# Function to calculate power for given sample size (paired t-test)
power_paired_t <- function(n, effect_size, alpha = 0.05, one_sided = TRUE) {
  df <- n - 1
  
  # Critical value (one-sided)
  if (one_sided) {
    t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha, df = df)
  } else {
    t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha/2, df = df)
  }
  
  # Non-centrality parameter
  ncp <- effect_size * sqrt(n)
  
  # Power calculation
  power <- 1 - pt(t_crit, df = df, ncp = ncp)
  
  return(power)
}

# Find minimum sample size for target power = 0.80
sample_sizes <- 2:500
powers <- sapply(sample_sizes, function(n) power_paired_t(n, cohens_d, alpha, one_sided = TRUE))

# Find minimum n where power >= 0.80
min_n <- sample_sizes[which(powers >= target_power)[1]]
achieved_power_min_n <- powers[which(sample_sizes == min_n)[1]]

cat("\n--- Sample Size Calculation ---\n")
cat("Minimum sample size for 80% power:", min_n, "participants\n")
cat("Achieved power at n =", min_n, ":", round(achieved_power_min_n, 4), "\n")

# Also report power at n-1 to show the crossing
if (min_n > 2) {
  prev_n <- min_n - 1
  prev_power <- power_paired_t(prev_n, cohens_d, alpha, one_sided = TRUE)
  cat("Power at n =", prev_n, ":", round(prev_power, 4), "\n")
  cat("Power improvement from n =", prev_n, "to n =", min_n, ":",
      round(achieved_power_min_n - prev_power, 4), "\n")
}

# Display a range for verification
cat("\n--- Power by Sample Size ---\n")
verification_ns <- c(15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40, 45, 50)
for (n in verification_ns) {
  pw <- power_paired_t(n, cohens_d, alpha, one_sided = TRUE)
  cat(sprintf("n = %3d: Power = %.4f %s\n", n, pw, if (pw >= 0.80) "[✓ meets target]" else ""))
}

# Emit result
result <- data.frame(
  metric = "sample_size",
  value = min_n,
  unit = "participants_total"
)

cat("\n--- Final Result ---\n")
print(result)

cat("This is the standard formula for the SD of a difference of two correlated variables.\n")
cat("Derivation: Var(X - Y) = Var(X) + Var(Y) - 2*Cov(X,Y)\n")
cat("           = SD_X^2 + SD_Y^2 - 2*r*SD_X*SD_Y\n")
cat("SD_diff = sqrt(Var(X-Y))\n\n")

cat("Calculation: sqrt(5^2 + 5.5^2 - 2*0.5*5*5.5)\n")

cat("           = sqrt(27.75)\n")
cat("           = ", sd_diff_formula1, "\n\n")

cat("FORMULA 2: Alternative - if independent (no correlation)\n")
sd_diff_formula2 <- sqrt(sd_b^2 + sd_f^2)
