_ A_ r_ g_ u_ m_ e_ n_ t_ s:

    type: specifies the type of analysis for which sample size is being
          calculated

            • ‘"c"’ specifies sample size calculation for a prediction
              model with a continuous outcome

            • ‘"b"’ specifies sample size calculation for a prediction
              model with a binary outcome

            • ‘"s"’ specifies sample size calculation for a prediction
              model with a survival (time-to-event) outcome

nagrsquared: for ‘type="b" or type="s"’ this specifies the expected
          value of the Nagelkerke's R-squared of the new model, which
          is the Cox-Snell R-squared scaled to lie in the [0,1] range.
          It is interpretable in the same way as the standard
          R-squared, i.e. the percentage of variation in outcome values
          explained by the model. Please read the description of
          ‘rsquared’ for additional details about specifying the
          expected R-squared performance

csrsquared: for ‘type="b" or type="s"’ this specifies the expected
          value of the Cox-Snell R-squared of the new model. The
          Cox-Snell R-squared is the generalised version of the
          well-known R-squared for continuous outcomes, based on the
          likelihood. Please read the description of ‘rsquared’ for
          additional details about specifying the expected R-squared
          performance. The papers by Riley et al. (see references)
          outline how to obtain the Cox-Snell R-squared value from
          published studies if they are not reported, using other
          information (such as the C-statistic [see ‘cstatistic()’
          option below]).

rsquared: for ‘type="c"’ this specifies the expected value of the
          R-squared of the new model, where R-squared is the percentage
          of variation in outcome values explained by the model. For
          example, the user may input the value of the R-squared
          reported for a previous prediction model study in the same
          field.  If taking a value from a previous prediction model
          development study, users should input the model's adjusted
          R-squared value, not the apparent R-squared value, as the
          latter is optimistic (biased).  However, if taking the
          R-squared value from an external validation of a previous
          model, the apparent R-squared can be used (as the validation
          data was not used for development, and so R-squared apparent
          is then unbiased). Users should be conservative with their
          chosen R-squared value; for example, by taking the R-squared
          value from a previous model, even if they hope their new
          model will improve performance.

parameters: specifies the number of candidate predictor parameters for
          potential inclusion in the new prediction model.  Note that
          this may be larger than the number of candidate predictors,
          as categorical and continuous predictors often require two or
          more parameters to be estimated.

shrinkage: specifies the level of shrinkage desired at internal
          validation after developing the new model. Shrinkage is a
          measure of overfitting, and can range from 0 to 1, with
          higher values denoting less overfitting. We recommend a
          shrinkage = 0.9 (the default in ‘pmsampsize’), which
          indicates that the predictor effect (beta coefficients) in
          the model would need to be shrunk by 10% to adjust for
          overfitting. See references below for further information.

prevalence: (‘type="b"’ option) specifies the overall outcome
          proportion (for a prognostic model) or overall prevalence
          (for a diagnostic model) expected within the model
          development dataset. This should be derived based on previous
          studies in the same population.

cstatistic: (‘type="b"’ option) specifies the C-statistic reported in
          an existing prediction model study to be used in conjunction
          with the expected prevalence to approximate the Cox-Snell
          R-squared using the approach of Riley et al. 2020. Ideally,
          this should be an optimism-adjusted C-statistic. The
          approximate Cox-Snell R-squared value is used as described
          above for the ‘csrsquared()’ option, and so is treated as a
          baseline for the expected performance of the new model.

    seed: (‘type="b"’ option) specifies the initial value of the
          random-number seed used by the random-number functions when
          simulating data to approximate the Cox-Snell R-squared based
          on reported C-statistic and expect prevalence as described by
          Riley et al. 2020

    rate: (‘type="s"’ option) specifies the overall event rate in the
          population of interest, for example as obtained from a
          previous study, for the survival outcome of interest. NB:
          rate must be given in time units used for meanfup and
          timepoint options.

timepoint: (‘type="s"’ option) specifies the timepoint of interest for
          prediction. NB: time units must be the same as given for
          meanfup option (e.g. years, months).

 meanfup: (‘type="s"’ option) specifies the average (mean) follow-up
          time anticipated for individuals in the model development
          dataset, for example as taken from a previous study in the
          population of interest. NB: time units must be the same as
          given for timepoint option.

intercept: (‘type="c"’ options) specifies the average outcome value in
          the population of interest e.g. the average blood pressure,
          or average pain score. This could be based on a previous
          study, or on clinical knowledge.

      sd: (‘type="c"’ options) specifies the standard deviation (SD) of
          outcome values in the population e.g. the SD for blood
          pressure in patients with all other predictors set to the
          average. This could again be based on a previous study, or on
          clinical knowledge.

    mmoe: (‘type="c"’ options) multiplicative margin of error (MMOE)
          acceptable for calculation of the intercept. The default is a
          MMOE of 10%. Confidence interval for the intercept will be
          displayed in the output for reference. See references below
          for further information.

_ D_ e_ t_ a_ i_ l_ s:

     ‘pmsampsize’ can be used to calculate the minimum sample size for
     the development of models with continuous, binary or survival
     (time-to-event) outcomes. Riley _et al_. lay out a series of
     criteria the sample size should meet. These aim to minimise the
     overfitting and to ensure precise estimation of key parameters in
     the prediction model.

     For continuous outcomes, there are four criteria:
     i) small overfitting defined by an expected shrinkage of predictor
     effects by 10% or less,
     ii) small absolute difference of 0.05 in the model's apparent and
     adjusted R-squared value,
     iii) precise estimation of the residual standard deviation, and
     iv) precise estimation of the average outcome value.

     The sample size calculation requires the user to pre-specify (e.g.
     based on previous evidence) the anticipated R-squared of the
     model, and the average outcome value and standard deviation of
     outcome values in the population of interest.

     For binary or survival (time-to-event) outcomes, there are three
     criteria:
     i) small overfitting defined by an expected shrinkage of predictor
     effects by 10% or less,
     ii) small absolute difference of 0.05 in the model's apparent and
     adjusted Nagelkerke's R-squared value, and
     iii) precise estimation (within +/- 0.05) of the average outcome
     risk in the population for a key timepoint of interest for
     prediction.

     With thanks to Richard D. Riley, Emma C Martin, Gary Collins, Glen
     Martin & Kym Snell for helpful input & feedback

     ## Examples based on those included in two papers by Riley et al.
     ## published in Statistics in Medicine (2018).
     ## NB: Survival example based on Riley et al. BMJ paper (2020).
     
     ## Binary outcomes (Logistic prediction models)
     # Use pmsampsize to calculate the minimum sample size required to develop a
     # multivariable prediction model for a binary outcome using 24 candidate
     # predictor parameters. Based on previous evidence, the outcome prevalence is
     # anticipated to be 0.174 (17.4%) and a lower bound (taken from the adjusted
     # Cox-Snell R-squared of an existing prediction model) for the new model's
     # R-squared value is 0.288
     
     pmsampsize(type = "b", csrsquared = 0.288, parameters = 24, prevalence = 0.174)
     
     # Now lets assume we could not obtain a Cox-Snell R-squared estimate from an existing
     # prediction model, but instead had a C-statistic (0.89) reported for the existing prediction
     # model. We can use this C-statistic along with the prevalence to approximate the Cox-Snell
     # R-squared using the approach of Riley et al. (2020). Use pmsampsize with the cstatistic()
     # option instead of rsquared() option.
     
     pmsampsize(type = "b", cstatistic = 0.89, parameters = 24, prevalence = 0.174)
     
     ## Survial outcomes (Cox prediction models)
     # Use pmsampsize to calculate the minimum sample size required for developing
     # a multivariable prediction model with a survival outcome using 30 candidate
     # predictors. We know an existing prediction model in the same field has an
     # R-squared adjusted of 0.051. Further, in the previous study the mean
     # follow-up was 2.07 years, and overall event rate was 0.065. We select a
     # timepoint of interest for prediction using the newly developed model of 2
     # years
     
     pmsampsize(type = "s", csrsquared = 0.051, parameters = 30, rate = 0.065,
                timepoint = 2, meanfup = 2.07)
     
     ## Continuous outcomes (Linear prediction models)
     # Use pmsampsize to calculate the minimum sample size required for developing
     # a multivariable prediction model for a continuous outcome (here, FEV1 say),
     # using 25 candidate predictors.  We know an existing prediction model in the
     # same field has an R-squared adjusted of 0.2, and that FEV1 values in the
     # population have a mean of 1.9 and SD of 0.6
     
     pmsampsize(type = "c", rsquared = 0.2, parameters = 25, intercept = 1.9, sd = 0.6)

plan.estimand: Minimum participants per group achieving 90% power for detecting a constant mean group difference of 0.45 under a two-group random-intercept Gaussian model with repeated observations
plan.hypothesis: H₀: μ₂ - μ₁ = 0 vs. H₁: μ₂ - μ₁ ≠ 0, where μ₁ and μ₂ are group means, tested via pooled two-sample t-test on participant averages
assumptions: Random-intercept model: observations within a participant share a common random intercept drawn from N(0, σ²ᵢ), inducing correlation structure
Marginal model: each observation is N(μ_g, σ²_marginal) with common marginal SD across groups
Intraclass correlation (ICC) = σ²ᵢ / σ²_marginal = 0.4, implying σ²ᵢ = 0.4 and σ²_within = 0.6
Constant treatment effect: group difference is 0.45 on the original scale
Participant averages computed as (y₁ + y₂ + y₃ + y₄) / 4 per participant
SD of participant average under null: SD_avg = σ_marginal * √(ICC + (1 - ICC) / m) = 1 * √(0.4 + 0.6 / 4) = √0.55
Two-sample pooled t-test on participant averages with m-1 = 3 degrees of freedom per group collapsed into error term
No missing data; all 4 observations collected per participant
Equal group allocation (1:1 ratio)
scientific_notes: Design combines repeated measures (within-participant correlation via ICC) with between-group comparison
Power is driven by effective sample size (number of participant averages) and SD of those averages
The SD of participant averages under this model is √(0.4 + 0.6/4) = √0.55 ≈ 0.7416
Effective standardized difference = 0.45 / √0.55 ≈ 0.607
Analytical power calculation uses two-sample t-test with total n = 2N (N per group) and df = 2N - 2
Will verify achieved power at the selected minimum integer design

answer.summary: For a two-group random-intercept Gaussian study with 4 observations per participant, marginal SD = 1, ICC = 0.4, and constant group difference = 0.45, analyzed via pooled two-sample t-test on participant averages at α = 0.05 (two-sided), the minimum integer sample size achieving 90% power is 59 participants per group (118 total, 472 total observations). The preceding design (58 per group) achieves 89.97% power, confirming that 59 is the smallest admissible integer meeting the target.
answer.method: Analytical power calculation for two-sample t-test on participant averages. Under the random-intercept model, the marginal variance of each observation is σ²_marginal = 1. The variance of each participant's average (from m = 4 observations) is Var(ȳᵢ) = σ²_marginal × (ICC + (1−ICC)/m) = 1 × (0.4 + 0.6/4) = 0.55, giving SD_avg = √0.55 ≈ 0.7416. The effective standardized difference is d = 0.45 / 0.7416 ≈ 0.6068. Power is computed from the non-central t-distribution with non-centrality parameter λ = d × √(n/2), df = 2n − 2, and two-sided critical value at α = 0.05. The minimum n achieving power ≥ 0.90 is identified by search over integer candidate values.
assumptions: Random-intercept model: observations within a participant share a common random intercept ∼ N(0, σ²ᵢ), inducing within-participant correlation
Marginal model: each observation ∼ N(μ_g, σ²_marginal) with constant marginal SD = 1 across groups
Intraclass correlation ICC = σ²ᵢ / σ²_marginal = 0.4 throughout
Constant treatment effect: group mean difference = 0.45 on the original scale
Participant averages computed as (y₁ + y₂ + y₃ + y₄)/4 for analysis
Two-sample pooled t-test applied to participant averages, treating each average as an independent observation
No missing data; all 4 observations collected per participant
Equal group allocation (1:1 ratio)
Analysis uses theoretical t-distribution; asymptotic normality holds with n = 59 per group
limitations: Calculation assumes random-intercept structure correctly captures within-participant correlation; violations (e.g., compound symmetry, heterogeneous correlation) may affect actual power

Power computation relies on participant averages being approximately normally distributed; with n = 59 per group and m = 4 observations each, normality is a reasonable working assumption but may not hold exactly for non-normal error distributions
No adjustment for multiple comparisons, sequential testing, or interim analyses; power is based on a single fixed design
No attrition modeled; power is nominal under the assumption of 100% data completion
Rounding to integer sample size follows standard practice; continuous solution would require approximately 58.7 participants per group

# Two-group random-intercept Gaussian study
# 4 observations per participant, marginal SD = 1, ICC = 0.4
# Constant mean group difference = 0.45
# Equal allocation, no missing data
# Analyze participant averages with two-sided pooled t-test at alpha = 0.05
# Target: 90% power

# Parameters
m <- 4  # observations per participant
sigma_marginal <- 1  # marginal SD
rho <- 0.4  # intraclass correlation
delta <- 0.45  # group difference
alpha <- 0.05  # significance level
target_power <- 0.90

# Calculate variance components
# From ICC = sigma_i^2 / sigma_marginal^2
sigma_i_sq <- rho * sigma_marginal^2  # between-participant variance
sigma_within_sq <- (1 - rho) * sigma_marginal^2  # within-participant variance

cat("Variance components:\n")
cat("  Between-participant variance (σ²ᵢ):", sigma_i_sq, "\n")
cat("  Within-participant variance (σ²_within):", sigma_within_sq, "\n")
cat("  Marginal variance (σ²_marginal):", sigma_marginal^2, "\n\n")

# SD of participant average
# Var(avg) = Var((y1+y2+y3+y4)/4)
#          = [σ²ᵢ + σ²_within] / 4  (averaging m observations under random intercept model)
# Under random intercept: Var(y_ij) = σ²ᵢ + σ²_within = σ²_marginal
# More precisely: Var(avg_i) = σ²ᵢ + σ²_within/m = σ²_marginal * (ICC + (1-ICC)/m)

sd_avg <- sigma_marginal * sqrt(rho + (1 - rho) / m)

cat("SD of participant average:\n")
cat("  SD_avg = σ_marginal * √(ICC + (1-ICC)/m)\n")
cat("  SD_avg = 1 * √(0.4 + 0.6/4)\n")
cat("  SD_avg = √0.55 =", sd_avg, "\n\n")

# Effective standardized difference (Cohen's d scale)
effective_d <- delta / sd_avg

cat("Effective standardized difference:\n")
cat("  d = Δ / SD_avg =", delta, "/", sd_avg, "=", effective_d, "\n\n")

# For a two-sample t-test with equal allocation (n per group, total N = 2n):
# Non-centrality parameter: λ = d * √(n/2) where n is per group
# df = 2n - 2

# Function to compute power for given n (per group)
compute_power <- function(n_per_group, d, alpha_level) {
  df <- 2 * n_per_group - 2
  lambda <- d * sqrt(n_per_group / 2)
  # Non-central t critical value
  t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha_level / 2, df)
  # Power is P(|t| > t_crit | H1)
  power <- pt(t_crit, df, ncp = lambda, lower.tail = FALSE) +
           pt(-t_crit, df, ncp = lambda, lower.tail = TRUE)
  return(power)
}

# Search for minimum n achieving target power
# Start with a reasonable range
n_candidates <- seq(10, 80, by = 1)
powers <- sapply(n_candidates, function(n) compute_power(n, effective_d, alpha))

# Find minimum n where power >= target_power
min_idx <- which(powers >= target_power)[1]
min_n <- n_candidates[min_idx]
achieved_power <- powers[min_idx]

# Also check the preceding design
if (min_idx > 1) {
  preceding_n <- n_candidates[min_idx - 1]
  preceding_power <- powers[min_idx - 1]
} else {
  preceding_n <- NA
  preceding_power <- NA
}

cat("Power calculation results:\n")
cat("=========================================\n")
cat("Minimum integer n per group:", min_n, "\n")
cat("Achieved power at n =", min_n, ":", achieved_power, "\n")
if (!is.na(preceding_n)) {
  cat("Power at preceding design (n =", preceding_n, "):", preceding_power, "\n")
}
cat("Target power:", target_power, "\n")
cat("Significance level (α):", alpha, "\n\n")

# Show a table around the minimum
n_table <- max(min_n - 3, 1):min(min_n + 3, 80)
power_table <- sapply(n_table, function(n) compute_power(n, effective_d, alpha))

cat("Power curve around minimum:\n")
for (i in seq_along(n_table)) {
  marker <- if (n_table[i] == min_n) " ← SELECTED" else ""
  cat(sprintf("  n = %3d: power = %.6f%s\n", n_table[i], power_table[i], marker))
}

cat("\n")
cat("Study design summary:\n")
cat("=========================================\n")
cat("Sample size: ", min_n, "participants per group\n")
cat("Total participants: ", 2 * min_n, "\n")
cat("Total observations: ", 2 * min_n * m, "\n")
cat("Observations per participant: ", m, "\n")
cat("Marginal SD: ", sigma_marginal, "\n")
cat("ICC: ", rho, "\n")
cat("Group difference: ", delta, "\n")
cat("SD of participant average: ", sd_avg, "\n")
cat("Effective d: ", effective_d, "\n")
cat("Two-sided α: ", alpha, "\n")
cat("Achieved power: ", achieved_power, "\n")

# Independent verification using different computational pathway
# Study design:
# - Two groups (equal allocation)
# - 4 observations per participant
# - Marginal SD = 1, ICC = 0.4
# - Group difference = 0.45
# - Analyzed via pooled two-sample t-test on participant averages
# - Target: 90% power, α = 0.05 (two-sided)

library(stats)

# Step 1: Verify variance decomposition
m <- 4
sigma_marginal <- 1
rho <- 0.4  # ICC

# Under random-intercept model:
# Var(y_ij) = sigma_i^2 + sigma_within^2 = sigma_marginal^2
# ICC = sigma_i^2 / sigma_marginal^2

sigma_i_sq <- rho * sigma_marginal^2
sigma_within_sq <- (1 - rho) * sigma_marginal^2

cat("Variance decomposition verification:\n")
cat("  σ²_i (between) =", sigma_i_sq, "\n")
cat("  σ²_within =", sigma_within_sq, "\n")
cat("  Sum (marginal) =", sigma_i_sq + sigma_within_sq, "\n")
cat("  ICC = σ²_i / σ²_marginal =", sigma_i_sq / sigma_marginal^2, "\n\n")

# Step 2: Variance of participant average
# When averaging m observations from random-intercept model:
# Var(ȳ_i) = Var((1/m) * Σ_j y_ij)
#          = (1/m^2) * Σ_j Cov(y_ij, y_ij) + (1/m^2) * Σ_{j≠k} Cov(y_ij, y_ik)
#          = (1/m^2) * m * (σ²_i + σ²_within) + (1/m^2) * m(m-1) * σ²_i
#          = (1/m) * (σ²_i + σ²_within) + ((m-1)/m) * σ²_i
#          = (1/m) * σ²_marginal + ((m-1)/m) * σ²_i
#          = σ²_marginal * (1/m + ((m-1)/m) * ICC)
#          = σ²_marginal * (1/m + (m-1)*ICC/m)
#          = σ²_marginal * (1 + (m-1)*ICC) / m

var_avg_formula1 <- sigma_marginal^2 * (1 + (m - 1) * rho) / m
sd_avg_formula1 <- sqrt(var_avg_formula1)

# Alternative formulation:
# Var(ȳ_i) = σ²_marginal * (ICC + (1-ICC)/m)
var_avg_formula2 <- sigma_marginal^2 * (rho + (1 - rho) / m)
sd_avg_formula2 <- sqrt(var_avg_formula2)

cat("Variance of participant average (two equivalent formulas):\n")
cat("  Formula 1: σ²_avg = σ²_marginal * (1 + (m-1)*ICC) / m\n")
cat("    Var(ȳ_i) =", var_avg_formula1, "\n")
cat("    SD(ȳ_i) =", sd_avg_formula1, "\n")
cat("  Formula 2: σ²_avg = σ²_marginal * (ICC + (1-ICC)/m)\n")
cat("    Var(ȳ_i) =", var_avg_formula2, "\n")
cat("    SD(ȳ_i) =", sd_avg_formula2, "\n")
cat("  Match:", isTRUE(all.equal(var_avg_formula1, var_avg_formula2)), "\n\n")

sd_avg <- sd_avg_formula1

# Step 3: Effective standardized difference (Cohen's d for t-test)
delta <- 0.45
effective_d <- delta / sd_avg

cat("Effective standardized difference:\n")
cat("  d = Δ / SD(ȳ_i) =", delta, "/", round(sd_avg, 10), "=", effective_d, "\n\n")

# Step 4: Power calculation for two-sample t-test
# For two groups with n per group, total N = 2n
# H0: μ_1 = μ_2, H1: μ_1 ≠ μ_2
# Under H1 with effect d and equal n:
# t ~ t(df = 2n-2, λ) where λ = d * sqrt(n/2)
# Power = P(|t| > t_crit | H1)

alpha <- 0.05
target_power <- 0.90

compute_power_v2 <- function(n_per_group, d, alpha_sig) {
  df <- 2 * n_per_group - 2
  lambda <- d * sqrt(n_per_group / 2)
  
  # Two-tailed critical value
  t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha_sig / 2, df)
  
  # Power: probability that |t| exceeds critical value under H1
  # This is equivalent to P(t > t_crit | NCP=λ) + P(t < -t_crit | NCP=λ)
  power <- pt(-t_crit, df, ncp = lambda, lower.tail = TRUE) +
           pt(t_crit, df, ncp = lambda, lower.tail = FALSE)
  
  return(power)
}

# Test at candidate values around expected minimum
candidates <- 55:65
powers <- sapply(candidates, function(n) compute_power_v2(n, effective_d, alpha))

cat("Power curve (independent calculation):\n")
for (i in seq_along(candidates)) {
  n <- candidates[i]
  p <- powers[i]
  meets <- ifelse(p >= target_power, "✓ MEETS", "  ")
  cat(sprintf("  n = %d: power = %.8f  %s\n", n, p, meets))
}

# Find minimum
min_idx <- which(powers >= target_power)[1]
min_n_verified <- candidates[min_idx]
power_at_min <- powers[min_idx]
power_at_pred <- powers[min_idx - 1]

cat("\n")
cat("VERIFICATION RESULTS:\n")
cat("====================\n")
cat("Minimum n per group:", min_n_verified, "\n")
cat("Achieved power:", round(power_at_min, 10), "\n")
cat("Power at n-1:", round(power_at_pred, 10), "\n")
cat("Meets 90% target:", power_at_min >= target_power, "\n")
cat("Preceding design below target:", power_at_pred < target_power, "\n\n")

# Calculate total design size
total_part <- 2 * min_n_verified
total_obs <- total_part * m

cat("DESIGN SUMMARY:\n")
cat("================\n")
cat("Sample size per group:", min_n_verified, "\n")
cat("Total participants:", total_part, "\n")
cat("Total observations:", total_obs, "\n")
cat("SD of participant average:", round(sd_avg, 10), "\n")
cat("Effective d:", round(effective_d, 10), "\n")
cat("Degrees of freedom (at min n):", 2*min_n_verified - 2, "\n")

# Monte Carlo verification of power calculation
# Generate data under the random-intercept model and test via two-sample t-test on averages

set.seed(20240515)

m <- 4  # observations per participant
sigma_marginal <- 1
rho <- 0.4
delta <- 0.45
alpha <- 0.05

# Variance components
sigma_i_sq <- rho * sigma_marginal^2
sigma_within_sq <- (1 - rho) * sigma_marginal^2

cat("Monte Carlo Simulation for Power Validation\n")
cat("===========================================\n")
cat("Data-generating process: random-intercept Gaussian model\n")
cat("  σ²_i (between) =", sigma_i_sq, "\n")
cat("  σ²_within =", sigma_within_sq, "\n")
cat("  Group 1 mean: 0, Group 2 mean:", delta, "\n\n")

# Test for n = 58 and n = 59
test_designs <- c(58, 59)
n_sims <- 10000

results_mc <- data.frame()

for (n_per_group in test_designs) {
  cat("Testing n =", n_per_group, "per group (", n_sims, "simulations)...\n")
  
  rejections <- 0
  
  for (sim in 1:n_sims) {
    # Generate data for group 1
    b_1 <- rnorm(n_per_group, 0, sqrt(sigma_i_sq))  # random intercepts
    y_1 <- matrix(NA, n_per_group, m)
    for (i in 1:n_per_group) {
      y_1[i, ] <- b_1[i] + rnorm(m, 0, sqrt(sigma_within_sq))
    }
    avg_1 <- rowMeans(y_1)
    
    # Generate data for group 2
    b_2 <- rnorm(n_per_group, 0, sqrt(sigma_i_sq))  # random intercepts
    y_2 <- matrix(NA, n_per_group, m)
    for (i in 1:n_per_group) {
      y_2[i, ] <- delta + b_2[i] + rnorm(m, 0, sqrt(sigma_within_sq))
    }
    avg_2 <- rowMeans(y_2)
    
    # Pooled two-sample t-test on participant averages
    t_test <- t.test(avg_1, avg_2, var.equal = TRUE)
    
    if (t_test$p.value < alpha) {
      rejections <- rejections + 1
    }
  }
  
  power_mc <- rejections / n_sims
  se_mc <- sqrt(power_mc * (1 - power_mc) / n_sims)
  ci_lower <- power_mc - 1.96 * se_mc
  ci_upper <- power_mc + 1.96 * se_mc
  
  # Analytical power from previous calculation
  sd_avg <- sigma_marginal * sqrt(rho + (1 - rho) / m)
  effective_d <- delta / sd_avg
  
  df <- 2 * n_per_group - 2
  lambda <- effective_d * sqrt(n_per_group / 2)
  t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha / 2, df)
  power_analytical <- pt(-t_crit, df, ncp = lambda, lower.tail = TRUE) +
                      pt(t_crit, df, ncp = lambda, lower.tail = FALSE)
  
  results_mc <- rbind(results_mc, data.frame(
    n_per_group = n_per_group,
    power_mc = power_mc,
    se_mc = se_mc,
    ci_lower = ci_lower,
    ci_upper = ci_upper,
    power_analytical = power_analytical,
    difference = power_mc - power_analytical
  ))
  
  cat(sprintf("  MC power: %.6f (SE: %.6f, 95%% CI: [%.6f, %.6f])\n",
              power_mc, se_mc, ci_lower, ci_upper))
  cat(sprintf("  Analytical: %.6f\n", power_analytical))
  cat(sprintf("  Difference: %.6f\n\n", power_mc - power_analytical))
}

# Summary table
cat("\nSUMMARY: Monte Carlo vs Analytical Power\n")
cat("=========================================\n")
print(results_mc)

# Check calibration
cat("\nCALIBRATION CHECK:\n")
cat("At n=58: MC power", results_mc$power_mc[1], "vs target 0.90 -",
    ifelse(results_mc$ci_lower[1] < 0.90 & results_mc$ci_upper[1] > 0.90,

cat("At n=59: MC power", results_mc$power_mc[2], "vs target 0.90 -",

# Summary
cat("\nCONCLUSION:\n")
cat("The analytical power calculation is ", 
    if(all(abs(results_mc$difference) < 0.01)) "well-calibrated" else "poorly calibrated",
    " to the Monte Carlo simulation.\n", sep="")
cat("Minimum design n=59 per group has MC power ≈", round(results_mc$power_mc[2], 4),
    "and analytical power =", round(results_mc$power_analytical[2], 4), "\n")

# For two-sample t-test: power = F(t_crit | ncp, df) where F is survival function of non-central t
# Power as function of n:
# P(n) = P(|t| > t_crit(n) | λ(n)), with t_crit(n) = qt(1-α/2, 2n-2), λ(n) = d*√(n/2)

# Solve numerically for the continuous solution
solve_for_power <- function(target_p, d, alpha_sig) {
  f <- function(n) {
    df <- 2 * n - 2
    lambda <- d * sqrt(n / 2)
    t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha_sig / 2, df)
    power <- pt(-t_crit, df, ncp = lambda, lower.tail = TRUE) +
             pt(t_crit, df, ncp = lambda, lower.tail = FALSE)
    return(power - target_p)
  }
  
  # Use uniroot to find n such that power(n) = target_p
  sol <- uniroot(f, interval = c(1, 200), tol = 1e-8)
  return(sol$root)
}

  t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha / 2, df)
  power <- pt(-t_crit, df, ncp = lambda, lower.tail = TRUE) +
           pt(t_crit, df, ncp = lambda, lower.tail = FALSE)
  return(power)
}

# Two-group random-intercept Gaussian study
# 4 observations per participant, marginal SD = 1, ICC = 0.4
# Constant mean group difference = 0.45
# Equal allocation, no missing data
# Analyze participant averages with two-sided pooled t-test at alpha = 0.05
# Target: 90% power

# Parameters
m <- 4  # observations per participant
sigma_marginal <- 1  # marginal SD
rho <- 0.4  # intraclass correlation
delta <- 0.45  # group difference
alpha <- 0.05  # significance level
target_power <- 0.90

# Calculate variance components
# From ICC = sigma_i^2 / sigma_marginal^2
sigma_i_sq <- rho * sigma_marginal^2  # between-participant variance
sigma_within_sq <- (1 - rho) * sigma_marginal^2  # within-participant variance

cat("Variance components:\n")
cat("  Between-participant variance (σ²ᵢ):", sigma_i_sq, "\n")
cat("  Within-participant variance (σ²_within):", sigma_within_sq, "\n")
cat("  Marginal variance (σ²_marginal):", sigma_marginal^2, "\n\n")

# SD of participant average
# Var(avg) = Var((y1+y2+y3+y4)/4)
#          = [σ²ᵢ + σ²_within] / 4  (averaging m observations under random intercept model)
# Under random intercept: Var(y_ij) = σ²ᵢ + σ²_within = σ²_marginal
# More precisely: Var(avg_i) = σ²ᵢ + σ²_within/m = σ²_marginal * (ICC + (1-ICC)/m)

sd_avg <- sigma_marginal * sqrt(rho + (1 - rho) / m)

cat("SD of participant average:\n")
cat("  SD_avg = σ_marginal * √(ICC + (1-ICC)/m)\n")
cat("  SD_avg = 1 * √(0.4 + 0.6/4)\n")
cat("  SD_avg = √0.55 =", sd_avg, "\n\n")

# Effective standardized difference (Cohen's d scale)
effective_d <- delta / sd_avg

cat("Effective standardized difference:\n")
cat("  d = Δ / SD_avg =", delta, "/", sd_avg, "=", effective_d, "\n\n")

# For a two-sample t-test with equal allocation (n per group, total N = 2n):
# Non-centrality parameter: λ = d * √(n/2) where n is per group
# df = 2n - 2

# Function to compute power for given n (per group)
compute_power <- function(n_per_group, d, alpha_level) {
  df <- 2 * n_per_group - 2
  lambda <- d * sqrt(n_per_group / 2)
  # Non-central t critical value
  t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha_level / 2, df)
  # Power is P(|t| > t_crit | H1)
  power <- pt(t_crit, df, ncp = lambda, lower.tail = FALSE) +
           pt(-t_crit, df, ncp = lambda, lower.tail = TRUE)
  return(power)
}

# Search for minimum n achieving target power
# Start with a reasonable range
n_candidates <- seq(10, 80, by = 1)
powers <- sapply(n_candidates, function(n) compute_power(n, effective_d, alpha))

# Find minimum n where power >= target_power
min_idx <- which(powers >= target_power)[1]
min_n <- n_candidates[min_idx]
achieved_power <- powers[min_idx]

# Also check the preceding design
if (min_idx > 1) {
  preceding_n <- n_candidates[min_idx - 1]
  preceding_power <- powers[min_idx - 1]
} else {
  preceding_n <- NA
  preceding_power <- NA
}

cat("Power calculation results:\n")
cat("=========================================\n")
cat("Minimum integer n per group:", min_n, "\n")
cat("Achieved power at n =", min_n, ":", achieved_power, "\n")
if (!is.na(preceding_n)) {
  cat("Power at preceding design (n =", preceding_n, "):", preceding_power, "\n")
}
cat("Target power:", target_power, "\n")
cat("Significance level (α):", alpha, "\n\n")

# Show a table around the minimum
n_table <- max(min_n - 3, 1):min(min_n + 3, 80)
power_table <- sapply(n_table, function(n) compute_power(n, effective_d, alpha))

cat("Power curve around minimum:\n")
for (i in seq_along(n_table)) {
  marker <- if (n_table[i] == min_n) " ← SELECTED" else ""
  cat(sprintf("  n = %3d: power = %.6f%s\n", n_table[i], power_table[i], marker))
}

cat("\n")
cat("Study design summary:\n")
cat("=========================================\n")
cat("Sample size: ", min_n, "participants per group\n")
cat("Total participants: ", 2 * min_n, "\n")
cat("Total observations: ", 2 * min_n * m, "\n")
cat("Observations per participant: ", m, "\n")
cat("Marginal SD: ", sigma_marginal, "\n")
cat("ICC: ", rho, "\n")
cat("Group difference: ", delta, "\n")
cat("SD of participant average: ", sd_avg, "\n")
cat("Effective d: ", effective_d, "\n")
cat("Two-sided α: ", alpha, "\n")
cat("Achieved power: ", achieved_power, "\n")

# Independent verification using different computational pathway
# Study design:
# - Two groups (equal allocation)
# - 4 observations per participant
# - Marginal SD = 1, ICC = 0.4
# - Group difference = 0.45
# - Analyzed via pooled two-sample t-test on participant averages
# - Target: 90% power, α = 0.05 (two-sided)

library(stats)

# Step 1: Verify variance decomposition
m <- 4
sigma_marginal <- 1
rho <- 0.4  # ICC

# Under random-intercept model:
# Var(y_ij) = sigma_i^2 + sigma_within^2 = sigma_marginal^2
# ICC = sigma_i^2 / sigma_marginal^2

sigma_i_sq <- rho * sigma_marginal^2
sigma_within_sq <- (1 - rho) * sigma_marginal^2

cat("Variance decomposition verification:\n")
cat("  σ²_i (between) =", sigma_i_sq, "\n")
cat("  σ²_within =", sigma_within_sq, "\n")
cat("  Sum (marginal) =", sigma_i_sq + sigma_within_sq, "\n")
cat("  ICC = σ²_i / σ²_marginal =", sigma_i_sq / sigma_marginal^2, "\n\n")

# Step 2: Variance of participant average
# When averaging m observations from random-intercept model:
# Var(ȳ_i) = Var((1/m) * Σ_j y_ij)
#          = (1/m^2) * Σ_j Cov(y_ij, y_ij) + (1/m^2) * Σ_{j≠k} Cov(y_ij, y_ik)
#          = (1/m^2) * m * (σ²_i + σ²_within) + (1/m^2) * m(m-1) * σ²_i
#          = (1/m) * (σ²_i + σ²_within) + ((m-1)/m) * σ²_i
#          = (1/m) * σ²_marginal + ((m-1)/m) * σ²_i
#          = σ²_marginal * (1/m + ((m-1)/m) * ICC)
#          = σ²_marginal * (1/m + (m-1)*ICC/m)
#          = σ²_marginal * (1 + (m-1)*ICC) / m

var_avg_formula1 <- sigma_marginal^2 * (1 + (m - 1) * rho) / m
sd_avg_formula1 <- sqrt(var_avg_formula1)

# Alternative formulation:
# Var(ȳ_i) = σ²_marginal * (ICC + (1-ICC)/m)
var_avg_formula2 <- sigma_marginal^2 * (rho + (1 - rho) / m)
sd_avg_formula2 <- sqrt(var_avg_formula2)

cat("Variance of participant average (two equivalent formulas):\n")
cat("  Formula 1: σ²_avg = σ²_marginal * (1 + (m-1)*ICC) / m\n")
cat("    Var(ȳ_i) =", var_avg_formula1, "\n")
cat("    SD(ȳ_i) =", sd_avg_formula1, "\n")
cat("  Formula 2: σ²_avg = σ²_marginal * (ICC + (1-ICC)/m)\n")
cat("    Var(ȳ_i) =", var_avg_formula2, "\n")
cat("    SD(ȳ_i) =", sd_avg_formula2, "\n")
cat("  Match:", isTRUE(all.equal(var_avg_formula1, var_avg_formula2)), "\n\n")

sd_avg <- sd_avg_formula1

# Step 3: Effective standardized difference (Cohen's d for t-test)
delta <- 0.45
effective_d <- delta / sd_avg

cat("Effective standardized difference:\n")
cat("  d = Δ / SD(ȳ_i) =", delta, "/", round(sd_avg, 10), "=", effective_d, "\n\n")

# Step 4: Power calculation for two-sample t-test
# For two groups with n per group, total N = 2n
# H0: μ_1 = μ_2, H1: μ_1 ≠ μ_2
# Under H1 with effect d and equal n:
# t ~ t(df = 2n-2, λ) where λ = d * sqrt(n/2)
# Power = P(|t| > t_crit | H1)

alpha <- 0.05
target_power <- 0.90

compute_power_v2 <- function(n_per_group, d, alpha_sig) {
  df <- 2 * n_per_group - 2
  lambda <- d * sqrt(n_per_group / 2)
  
  # Two-tailed critical value
  t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha_sig / 2, df)
  
  # Power: probability that |t| exceeds critical value under H1
  # This is equivalent to P(t > t_crit | NCP=λ) + P(t < -t_crit | NCP=λ)
  power <- pt(-t_crit, df, ncp = lambda, lower.tail = TRUE) +
           pt(t_crit, df, ncp = lambda, lower.tail = FALSE)
  
  return(power)
}

# Test at candidate values around expected minimum
candidates <- 55:65
powers <- sapply(candidates, function(n) compute_power_v2(n, effective_d, alpha))

cat("Power curve (independent calculation):\n")
for (i in seq_along(candidates)) {
  n <- candidates[i]
  p <- powers[i]
  meets <- ifelse(p >= target_power, "✓ MEETS", "  ")
  cat(sprintf("  n = %d: power = %.8f  %s\n", n, p, meets))
}

# Find minimum
min_idx <- which(powers >= target_power)[1]
min_n_verified <- candidates[min_idx]
power_at_min <- powers[min_idx]
power_at_pred <- powers[min_idx - 1]

cat("\n")
cat("VERIFICATION RESULTS:\n")
cat("====================\n")
cat("Minimum n per group:", min_n_verified, "\n")
cat("Achieved power:", round(power_at_min, 10), "\n")
cat("Power at n-1:", round(power_at_pred, 10), "\n")
cat("Meets 90% target:", power_at_min >= target_power, "\n")
cat("Preceding design below target:", power_at_pred < target_power, "\n\n")

# Calculate total design size
total_part <- 2 * min_n_verified
total_obs <- total_part * m

cat("DESIGN SUMMARY:\n")
cat("================\n")
cat("Sample size per group:", min_n_verified, "\n")
cat("Total participants:", total_part, "\n")
cat("Total observations:", total_obs, "\n")
cat("SD of participant average:", round(sd_avg, 10), "\n")
cat("Effective d:", round(effective_d, 10), "\n")
cat("Degrees of freedom (at min n):", 2*min_n_verified - 2, "\n")

# Monte Carlo verification of power calculation
# Generate data under the random-intercept model and test via two-sample t-test on averages

set.seed(20240515)

m <- 4  # observations per participant
sigma_marginal <- 1
rho <- 0.4
delta <- 0.45
alpha <- 0.05

# Variance components
sigma_i_sq <- rho * sigma_marginal^2
sigma_within_sq <- (1 - rho) * sigma_marginal^2

cat("Monte Carlo Simulation for Power Validation\n")
cat("===========================================\n")
cat("Data-generating process: random-intercept Gaussian model\n")
cat("  σ²_i (between) =", sigma_i_sq, "\n")
cat("  σ²_within =", sigma_within_sq, "\n")
cat("  Group 1 mean: 0, Group 2 mean:", delta, "\n\n")

# Test for n = 58 and n = 59
test_designs <- c(58, 59)
n_sims <- 10000

results_mc <- data.frame()

for (n_per_group in test_designs) {
  cat("Testing n =", n_per_group, "per group (", n_sims, "simulations)...\n")
  
  rejections <- 0
  
  for (sim in 1:n_sims) {
    # Generate data for group 1
    b_1 <- rnorm(n_per_group, 0, sqrt(sigma_i_sq))  # random intercepts
    y_1 <- matrix(NA, n_per_group, m)
    for (i in 1:n_per_group) {
      y_1[i, ] <- b_1[i] + rnorm(m, 0, sqrt(sigma_within_sq))
    }
    avg_1 <- rowMeans(y_1)
    
    # Generate data for group 2
    b_2 <- rnorm(n_per_group, 0, sqrt(sigma_i_sq))  # random intercepts
    y_2 <- matrix(NA, n_per_group, m)
    for (i in 1:n_per_group) {
      y_2[i, ] <- delta + b_2[i] + rnorm(m, 0, sqrt(sigma_within_sq))
    }
    avg_2 <- rowMeans(y_2)
    
    # Pooled two-sample t-test on participant averages
    t_test <- t.test(avg_1, avg_2, var.equal = TRUE)
    
    if (t_test$p.value < alpha) {
      rejections <- rejections + 1
    }
  }
  
  power_mc <- rejections / n_sims
  se_mc <- sqrt(power_mc * (1 - power_mc) / n_sims)
  ci_lower <- power_mc - 1.96 * se_mc
  ci_upper <- power_mc + 1.96 * se_mc
  
  # Analytical power from previous calculation
  sd_avg <- sigma_marginal * sqrt(rho + (1 - rho) / m)
  effective_d <- delta / sd_avg
  
  df <- 2 * n_per_group - 2
  lambda <- effective_d * sqrt(n_per_group / 2)
  t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha / 2, df)
  power_analytical <- pt(-t_crit, df, ncp = lambda, lower.tail = TRUE) +
                      pt(t_crit, df, ncp = lambda, lower.tail = FALSE)
  
  results_mc <- rbind(results_mc, data.frame(
    n_per_group = n_per_group,
    power_mc = power_mc,
    se_mc = se_mc,
    ci_lower = ci_lower,
    ci_upper = ci_upper,
    power_analytical = power_analytical,
    difference = power_mc - power_analytical
  ))
  
  cat(sprintf("  MC power: %.6f (SE: %.6f, 95%% CI: [%.6f, %.6f])\n",
              power_mc, se_mc, ci_lower, ci_upper))
  cat(sprintf("  Analytical: %.6f\n", power_analytical))
  cat(sprintf("  Difference: %.6f\n\n", power_mc - power_analytical))
}

# Summary table
cat("\nSUMMARY: Monte Carlo vs Analytical Power\n")
cat("=========================================\n")
print(results_mc)

# Check calibration
cat("\nCALIBRATION CHECK:\n")
cat("At n=58: MC power", results_mc$power_mc[1], "vs target 0.90 -",
    ifelse(results_mc$ci_lower[1] < 0.90 & results_mc$ci_upper[1] > 0.90,
           "target CONTAINED in CI",
           "target OUTSIDE CI"), "\n")
cat("At n=59: MC power", results_mc$power_mc[2], "vs target 0.90 -",
    ifelse(results_mc$ci_lower[2] < 0.90,
           "target BELOW CI (power confirmed above target)",
           ""), "\n")

# Summary
cat("\nCONCLUSION:\n")
cat("The analytical power calculation is ", 
    if(all(abs(results_mc$difference) < 0.01)) "well-calibrated" else "poorly calibrated",
    " to the Monte Carlo simulation.\n", sep="")
cat("Minimum design n=59 per group has MC power ≈", round(results_mc$power_mc[2], 4),
    "and analytical power =", round(results_mc$power_analytical[2], 4), "\n")

# Check the continuous (non-integer) solution to understand the rounding

rho <- 0.4
delta <- 0.45
alpha <- 0.05
target_power <- 0.90

# Derived quantities
sd_avg <- sigma_marginal * sqrt(rho + (1 - rho) / m)
effective_d <- delta / sd_avg

cat("Continuous Solution Analysis\n")
cat("=============================\n\n")

# For two-sample t-test: power = F(t_crit | ncp, df) where F is survival function of non-central t
# Power as function of n:
# P(n) = P(|t| > t_crit(n) | λ(n)), with t_crit(n) = qt(1-α/2, 2n-2), λ(n) = d*√(n/2)

# Solve numerically for the continuous solution
solve_for_power <- function(target_p, d, alpha_sig) {
  f <- function(n) {
    df <- 2 * n - 2
    lambda <- d * sqrt(n / 2)
    t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha_sig / 2, df)
    power <- pt(-t_crit, df, ncp = lambda, lower.tail = TRUE) +
             pt(t_crit, df, ncp = lambda, lower.tail = FALSE)
    return(power - target_p)
  }
  
  # Use uniroot to find n such that power(n) = target_p
  sol <- uniroot(f, interval = c(1, 200), tol = 1e-8)
  return(sol$root)
}

n_continuous <- solve_for_power(target_power, effective_d, alpha)

cat("Continuous solution: n =", round(n_continuous, 6), "per group\n")
cat("This represents the exact (non-integer) value where power = 0.90\n\n")

  df <- 2 * n - 2

  t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha / 2, df)
  power <- pt(-t_crit, df, ncp = lambda, lower.tail = TRUE) +
           pt(t_crit, df, ncp = lambda, lower.tail = FALSE)
  return(power)
}

alpha <- 0.05

# Safe power computation
compute_power_safe <- function(n) {
  if (n < 2) return(NA)
  df <- 2 * n - 2
  lambda <- effective_d * sqrt(n / 2)
  t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha / 2, df)
  power <- pt(-t_crit, df, ncp = lambda, lower.tail = TRUE) +
           pt(t_crit, df, ncp = lambda, lower.tail = FALSE)
  return(power)
}

cat("Continuous Solution Analysis\n")
cat("=============================\n\n")

# Grid search to find approximate continuous solution
n_grid <- seq(10, 100, by = 0.1)
power_grid <- sapply(n_grid, compute_power_safe)

# Find where power crosses 0.90
idx_cross <- which(power_grid >= target_power)[1]
if (!is.na(idx_cross)) {
  n_approx_cross <- n_grid[max(idx_cross - 1, 1)]
  n_approx_cross_next <- n_grid[idx_cross]
  
  # Linear interpolation to refine
  p1 <- compute_power_safe(n_approx_cross)
  p2 <- compute_power_safe(n_approx_cross_next)
  
  # Interpolate
  if (p1 < target_power & p2 >= target_power) {
    n_continuous <- n_approx_cross + 
                   (target_power - p1) / (p2 - p1) * (n_approx_cross_next - n_approx_cross)
  } else {
    n_continuous <- n_approx_cross_next
  }
}

cat("Continuous (interpolated) solution: n ≈", round(n_continuous, 4), "per group\n")

# Evidence e1; success=true

# Two-group random-intercept Gaussian study
# 4 observations per participant, marginal SD = 1, ICC = 0.4
# Constant mean group difference = 0.45
# Equal allocation, no missing data
# Analyze participant averages with two-sided pooled t-test at alpha = 0.05
# Target: 90% power

# Parameters
m <- 4  # observations per participant
sigma_marginal <- 1  # marginal SD
rho <- 0.4  # intraclass correlation
delta <- 0.45  # group difference
alpha <- 0.05  # significance level
target_power <- 0.90

# Calculate variance components
# From ICC = sigma_i^2 / sigma_marginal^2
sigma_i_sq <- rho * sigma_marginal^2  # between-participant variance
sigma_within_sq <- (1 - rho) * sigma_marginal^2  # within-participant variance

cat("Variance components:\n")
cat("  Between-participant variance (σ²ᵢ):", sigma_i_sq, "\n")
cat("  Within-participant variance (σ²_within):", sigma_within_sq, "\n")
cat("  Marginal variance (σ²_marginal):", sigma_marginal^2, "\n\n")

# SD of participant average
# Var(avg) = Var((y1+y2+y3+y4)/4)
#          = [σ²ᵢ + σ²_within] / 4  (averaging m observations under random intercept model)
# Under random intercept: Var(y_ij) = σ²ᵢ + σ²_within = σ²_marginal
# More precisely: Var(avg_i) = σ²ᵢ + σ²_within/m = σ²_marginal * (ICC + (1-ICC)/m)

sd_avg <- sigma_marginal * sqrt(rho + (1 - rho) / m)

cat("SD of participant average:\n")
cat("  SD_avg = σ_marginal * √(ICC + (1-ICC)/m)\n")
cat("  SD_avg = 1 * √(0.4 + 0.6/4)\n")
cat("  SD_avg = √0.55 =", sd_avg, "\n\n")

# Effective standardized difference (Cohen's d scale)
effective_d <- delta / sd_avg

cat("Effective standardized difference:\n")
cat("  d = Δ / SD_avg =", delta, "/", sd_avg, "=", effective_d, "\n\n")

# For a two-sample t-test with equal allocation (n per group, total N = 2n):
# Non-centrality parameter: λ = d * √(n/2) where n is per group
# df = 2n - 2

# Function to compute power for given n (per group)
compute_power <- function(n_per_group, d, alpha_level) {
  df <- 2 * n_per_group - 2
  lambda <- d * sqrt(n_per_group / 2)
  # Non-central t critical value
  t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha_level / 2, df)
  # Power is P(|t| > t_crit | H1)
  power <- pt(t_crit, df, ncp = lambda, lower.tail = FALSE) +
           pt(-t_crit, df, ncp = lambda, lower.tail = TRUE)
  return(power)
}

# Search for minimum n achieving target power
# Start with a reasonable range
n_candidates <- seq(10, 80, by = 1)
powers <- sapply(n_candidates, function(n) compute_power(n, effective_d, alpha))

# Find minimum n where power >= target_power
min_idx <- which(powers >= target_power)[1]
min_n <- n_candidates[min_idx]
achieved_power <- powers[min_idx]

# Also check the preceding design
if (min_idx > 1) {
  preceding_n <- n_candidates[min_idx - 1]
  preceding_power <- powers[min_idx - 1]
} else {
  preceding_n <- NA
  preceding_power <- NA
}

cat("Power calculation results:\n")
cat("=========================================\n")
cat("Minimum integer n per group:", min_n, "\n")
cat("Achieved power at n =", min_n, ":", achieved_power, "\n")
if (!is.na(preceding_n)) {
  cat("Power at preceding design (n =", preceding_n, "):", preceding_power, "\n")
}
cat("Target power:", target_power, "\n")
cat("Significance level (α):", alpha, "\n\n")

# Show a table around the minimum
n_table <- max(min_n - 3, 1):min(min_n + 3, 80)
power_table <- sapply(n_table, function(n) compute_power(n, effective_d, alpha))

cat("Power curve around minimum:\n")
for (i in seq_along(n_table)) {
  marker <- if (n_table[i] == min_n) " ← SELECTED" else ""
  cat(sprintf("  n = %3d: power = %.6f%s\n", n_table[i], power_table[i], marker))
}

cat("\n")
cat("Study design summary:\n")
cat("=========================================\n")
cat("Sample size: ", min_n, "participants per group\n")
cat("Total participants: ", 2 * min_n, "\n")
cat("Total observations: ", 2 * min_n * m, "\n")
cat("Observations per participant: ", m, "\n")
cat("Marginal SD: ", sigma_marginal, "\n")
cat("ICC: ", rho, "\n")
cat("Group difference: ", delta, "\n")
cat("SD of participant average: ", sd_avg, "\n")
cat("Effective d: ", effective_d, "\n")
cat("Two-sided α: ", alpha, "\n")
cat("Achieved power: ", achieved_power, "\n")


# Evidence e2; success=true

# Final verification and output formatting
# Using the same parameters and rounding convention

m <- 4  # observations per participant
sigma_marginal <- 1
rho <- 0.4
delta <- 0.45
alpha <- 0.05
target_power <- 0.90

# SD of participant average
sd_avg <- sigma_marginal * sqrt(rho + (1 - rho) / m)
effective_d <- delta / sd_avg

# Power computation function
compute_power <- function(n_per_group, d, alpha_level) {
  df <- 2 * n_per_group - 2
  lambda <- d * sqrt(n_per_group / 2)
  t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha_level / 2, df)
  power <- pt(t_crit, df, ncp = lambda, lower.tail = FALSE) +
           pt(-t_crit, df, ncp = lambda, lower.tail = TRUE)
  return(power)
}

# Minimum design meeting target
min_n <- 59
achieved_power_min <- compute_power(min_n, effective_d, alpha)

# Preceding design
preceding_n <- 58
preceding_power <- compute_power(preceding_n, effective_d, alpha)

# Output for structured reporting
cat("STRUCTURED REPORTING OUTPUT\n")
cat("============================\n\n")
cat("Primary metric: sample_size\n")
cat("Unit: participants_per_group\n")
cat("Method identifier: rm_between\n")
cat("Study design: Two-group random-intercept Gaussian\n\n")
cat("Minimum integer sample size:", min_n, "participants per group\n")
cat("Achieved power at selected design:", achieved_power_min, "\n")
cat("Power at preceding admissible design (n=58):", preceding_power, "\n\n")

# Additional design parameters for verification
cat("Design parameters used:\n")
cat("  Number of observations per participant: ", m, "\n")
cat("  Marginal standard deviation: ", sigma_marginal, "\n")
cat("  Intraclass correlation: ", rho, "\n")
cat("  Group difference (Δ): ", delta, "\n")
cat("  SD of participant average: ", round(sd_avg, 10), "\n")
cat("  Effective standardized difference (d): ", round(effective_d, 10), "\n")
cat("  Two-sided significance level (α): ", alpha, "\n")
cat("  Target power: ", target_power, "\n")
cat("  Allocation ratio: 1:1\n\n")

# JSON output
library(jsonlite)
result <- list(
  results = list(
    list(
      metric = "sample_size",
      value = min_n,
      unit = "participants_per_group"
    ),
    list(
      metric = "achieved_power",
      value = round(achieved_power_min, 8),
      unit = "proportion"
    ),
    list(
      metric = "total_participants",
      value = 2 * min_n,
      unit = "participants"
    ),
    list(
      metric = "total_observations",
      value = 2 * min_n * m,
      unit = "count"
    ),
    list(
      metric = "power_at_preceding_design",
      value = round(preceding_power, 8),
      unit = "proportion"
    )
  )
)

cat("JSON OUTPUT:\n")
cat(toJSON(result, auto_unbox = TRUE, pretty = TRUE))

# Assign results for POWER_AGENT_RESULT
POWER_AGENT_RESULT <- list(
  results = list(
    list(
      metric = "sample_size",
      value = min_n,
      unit = "participants_per_group"
    ),
    list(
      metric = "achieved_power",
      value = round(achieved_power_min, 8),
      unit = "proportion"
    ),
    list(
      metric = "total_participants",
      value = 2 * min_n,
      unit = "participants"
    ),
    list(
      metric = "total_observations",
      value = 2 * min_n * m,
      unit = "observations"
    ),
    list(
      metric = "power_at_preceding_design",
      value = round(preceding_power, 8),
      unit = "proportion"
    )
  )
)

cat("\n\nPOWER_AGENT_RESULT=")
cat(toJSON(POWER_AGENT_RESULT, auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15))

# Sample size calculation for two-sample t-test
# Comparing two independent normal means with equal variances, 1:1 allocation
# One-sided pooled t-test at alpha = 0.05, target power = 0.8

library(stats)

# Input parameters
effect_diff <- 4.3        # Expected difference (dBA)
common_sd <- 7.8          # Common standard deviation (dBA)
alpha <- 0.05             # Significance level
target_power <- 0.80      # Target power
allocation_ratio <- 1     # 1:1 allocation

# Calculate standardized effect size (Cohen's d)
cohens_d <- effect_diff / common_sd
cat("Standardized effect size (Cohen's d):", cohens_d, "\n")

# For one-sided test: divide alpha by 2 to get critical value for upper tail
# Critical z value
z_alpha <- qnorm(1 - alpha/2)  # One-sided critical value at alpha=0.05
z_beta <- qnorm(target_power)   # Critical z for power

cat("Critical z (alpha=0.05, one-sided):", z_alpha, "\n")
cat("Critical z (power=0.80):", z_beta, "\n")

# Sample size formula for one-sided t-test (using normal approximation)
# n = (z_alpha + z_beta)^2 * 2 * sigma^2 / delta^2
# For equal variances and 1:1 allocation:
n_continuous <- ((z_alpha + z_beta)^2 * (common_sd^2 + common_sd^2)) / effect_diff^2

cat("\nContinuous solution (per group):", n_continuous, "\n")

# Round up to nearest integer to ensure power target is met
n_per_group <- ceiling(n_continuous)
cat("Rounded sample size (per group):", n_per_group, "\n")

# Verify achieved power at the selected design
# Using non-central t distribution
df <- 2 * n_per_group - 2  # Degrees of freedom for two-sample t-test
ncp <- effect_diff / sqrt(2 * common_sd^2 / n_per_group)  # Non-centrality parameter

# Critical t value (one-sided, alpha=0.05)
t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha/2, df)

# Achieved power (probability that t > t_crit under alternative)
achieved_power <- 1 - pt(t_crit, df, ncp=ncp)

cat("\nVerification at selected design:\n")
cat("Degrees of freedom:", df, "\n")
cat("Non-centrality parameter:", ncp, "\n")
cat("Critical t value (one-sided, alpha=0.05):", t_crit, "\n")
cat("Achieved power at n =", n_per_group, ":", achieved_power, "\n")

# Check power at preceding admissible design (n-1)
if (n_per_group > 1) {
  n_prev <- n_per_group - 1
  df_prev <- 2 * n_prev - 2
  ncp_prev <- effect_diff / sqrt(2 * common_sd^2 / n_prev)
  t_crit_prev <- qt(1 - alpha/2, df_prev)
  power_prev <- 1 - pt(t_crit_prev, df_prev, ncp=ncp_prev)
  
  cat("\nVerification at preceding design (n =", n_prev, "):\n")
  cat("Degrees of freedom:", df_prev, "\n")
  cat("Non-centrality parameter:", ncp_prev, "\n")
  cat("Critical t value:", t_crit_prev, "\n")
  cat("Power at n =", n_prev, ":", power_prev, "\n")
}

# Summary output
cat("\n========== RESULTS ==========\n")
cat("Minimum integer sample size per group:", n_per_group, "\n")
cat("Total sample size (both groups):", 2 * n_per_group, "\n")
cat("Achieved power:", round(achieved_power, 4), "\n")
cat("Target power:", target_power, "\n")
cat("Power criterion satisfied:", achieved_power >= target_power, "\n")

# Find exact minimum sample size meeting 80% power criterion
# by incremental search upward

effect_diff <- 4.3
common_sd <- 7.8
alpha <- 0.05
target_power <- 0.80

# Function to compute achieved power for a given n per group
compute_power <- function(n_per_group, effect_diff, common_sd, alpha) {
  df <- 2 * n_per_group - 2
  ncp <- effect_diff / sqrt(2 * common_sd^2 / n_per_group)
  t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha/2, df)
  power <- 1 - pt(t_crit, df, ncp=ncp)
  return(power)
}

# Start from n=52 and search upward
for (n in 52:60) {
  power <- compute_power(n, effect_diff, common_sd, alpha)
  meets_target <- power >= target_power
  cat(sprintf("n = %2d: power = %.6f, meets 80%% target: %s\n", n, power, meets_target))
  
  if (meets_target) {
    n_selected <- n
    power_selected <- power
    break
  }
}

# Also verify preceding design
n_preceding <- n_selected - 1
power_preceding <- compute_power(n_preceding, effect_diff, common_sd, alpha)

cat("\n========== FINAL RESULT ==========\n")
cat("Minimum sample size per group:", n_selected, "\n")
cat("Achieved power:", round(power_selected, 6), "\n")
cat("Target power:", target_power, "\n")
cat("\nPreceding design (n =", n_preceding, "):\n")
cat("Power:", round(power_preceding, 6), "\n")

# Output in POWER_AGENT_RESULT format
results <- list(
  metric = "sample_size",
  value = n_selected,
  unit = "participants_per_group"
)

cat("\nPOWER_AGENT_RESULT=", jsonlite::toJSON(
  list(
    results = list(results),
    simulation = NULL
  ),
  auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15
), sep = "")

# Evidence e1; success=true

# Sample size calculation for two-sample t-test
# Comparing two independent normal means with equal variances, 1:1 allocation
# One-sided pooled t-test at alpha = 0.05, target power = 0.8

library(stats)

# Input parameters
effect_diff <- 4.3        # Expected difference (dBA)
common_sd <- 7.8          # Common standard deviation (dBA)
alpha <- 0.05             # Significance level
target_power <- 0.80      # Target power
allocation_ratio <- 1     # 1:1 allocation

# Calculate standardized effect size (Cohen's d)
cohens_d <- effect_diff / common_sd
cat("Standardized effect size (Cohen's d):", cohens_d, "\n")

# For one-sided test: divide alpha by 2 to get critical value for upper tail
# Critical z value
z_alpha <- qnorm(1 - alpha/2)  # One-sided critical value at alpha=0.05
z_beta <- qnorm(target_power)   # Critical z for power

cat("Critical z (alpha=0.05, one-sided):", z_alpha, "\n")
cat("Critical z (power=0.80):", z_beta, "\n")

# Sample size formula for one-sided t-test (using normal approximation)
# n = (z_alpha + z_beta)^2 * 2 * sigma^2 / delta^2
# For equal variances and 1:1 allocation:
n_continuous <- ((z_alpha + z_beta)^2 * (common_sd^2 + common_sd^2)) / effect_diff^2

cat("\nContinuous solution (per group):", n_continuous, "\n")

# Round up to nearest integer to ensure power target is met
n_per_group <- ceiling(n_continuous)
cat("Rounded sample size (per group):", n_per_group, "\n")

# Verify achieved power at the selected design
# Using non-central t distribution
df <- 2 * n_per_group - 2  # Degrees of freedom for two-sample t-test
ncp <- effect_diff / sqrt(2 * common_sd^2 / n_per_group)  # Non-centrality parameter

# Critical t value (one-sided, alpha=0.05)
t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha/2, df)

# Achieved power (probability that t > t_crit under alternative)
achieved_power <- 1 - pt(t_crit, df, ncp=ncp)

cat("\nVerification at selected design:\n")
cat("Degrees of freedom:", df, "\n")
cat("Non-centrality parameter:", ncp, "\n")
cat("Critical t value (one-sided, alpha=0.05):", t_crit, "\n")
cat("Achieved power at n =", n_per_group, ":", achieved_power, "\n")

# Check power at preceding admissible design (n-1)
if (n_per_group > 1) {
  n_prev <- n_per_group - 1
  df_prev <- 2 * n_prev - 2
  ncp_prev <- effect_diff / sqrt(2 * common_sd^2 / n_prev)
  t_crit_prev <- qt(1 - alpha/2, df_prev)
  power_prev <- 1 - pt(t_crit_prev, df_prev, ncp=ncp_prev)
  
  cat("\nVerification at preceding design (n =", n_prev, "):\n")
  cat("Degrees of freedom:", df_prev, "\n")
  cat("Non-centrality parameter:", ncp_prev, "\n")
  cat("Critical t value:", t_crit_prev, "\n")
  cat("Power at n =", n_prev, ":", power_prev, "\n")
}

# Summary output
cat("\n========== RESULTS ==========\n")
cat("Minimum integer sample size per group:", n_per_group, "\n")
cat("Total sample size (both groups):", 2 * n_per_group, "\n")
cat("Achieved power:", round(achieved_power, 4), "\n")
cat("Target power:", target_power, "\n")
cat("Power criterion satisfied:", achieved_power >= target_power, "\n")


# Evidence e2; success=true

# Find exact minimum sample size meeting 80% power criterion
# by incremental search upward

effect_diff <- 4.3
common_sd <- 7.8
alpha <- 0.05
target_power <- 0.80

# Function to compute achieved power for a given n per group
compute_power <- function(n_per_group, effect_diff, common_sd, alpha) {
  df <- 2 * n_per_group - 2
  ncp <- effect_diff / sqrt(2 * common_sd^2 / n_per_group)
  t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha/2, df)
  power <- 1 - pt(t_crit, df, ncp=ncp)
  return(power)
}

# Start from n=52 and search upward
for (n in 52:60) {
  power <- compute_power(n, effect_diff, common_sd, alpha)
  meets_target <- power >= target_power
  cat(sprintf("n = %2d: power = %.6f, meets 80%% target: %s\n", n, power, meets_target))
  
  if (meets_target) {
    n_selected <- n
    power_selected <- power
    break
  }
}

# Also verify preceding design
n_preceding <- n_selected - 1
power_preceding <- compute_power(n_preceding, effect_diff, common_sd, alpha)

cat("\n========== FINAL RESULT ==========\n")
cat("Minimum sample size per group:", n_selected, "\n")
cat("Achieved power:", round(power_selected, 6), "\n")
cat("Target power:", target_power, "\n")
cat("\nPreceding design (n =", n_preceding, "):\n")
cat("Power:", round(power_preceding, 6), "\n")

# Output in POWER_AGENT_RESULT format
results <- list(
  metric = "sample_size",
  value = n_selected,
  unit = "participants_per_group"
)

cat("\nPOWER_AGENT_RESULT=", jsonlite::toJSON(
  list(
    results = list(results),
    simulation = NULL
  ),
  auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15
), sep = "")

scientific_notes: Partial eta-squared reflects the proportion of variance explained by the factor, adjusting for other factors in the model

answer.summary: For a balanced 3-by-2 factorial ANOVA with all 6 cells independent, a full interaction model, and common variance, testing the 3-level factor main effect (numerator df = 2) with partial eta-squared = 0.06 and alpha = 0.05, the minimum integer sample size is 27 participants per cell, achieving 80.57% power. At n = 26 participants per cell, power is 78.88%, below the 80% target.
answer.method: Fixed-effects factorial ANOVA power inversion using the noncentral F distribution. The noncentrality parameter λ is derived from partial eta-squared via λ = (partial_η² × df_error) / (1 − partial_η²). For each candidate sample size n, the error degrees of freedom is df_error = 6(n − 1). Power is computed as P(F > F_crit | H₁) where F_crit is the critical F-value at α = 0.05 with df₁ = 2 and df₂ = df_error, under the noncentral F distribution with noncentrality λ.

# Balanced 3-by-2 factorial ANOVA
# Testing the 3-level factor (A) main effect
# Partial eta-squared = 0.06
# Alpha = 0.05
# Target power = 0.80

# Design parameters
alpha <- 0.05
target_power <- 0.80
factor_a_levels <- 3  # 3-level factor (numerator df = 2)
factor_b_levels <- 2  # 2-level factor
total_cells <- factor_a_levels * factor_b_levels  # 6 cells
partial_eta_sq <- 0.06

# Numerator degrees of freedom for testing factor A main effect
df1 <- factor_a_levels - 1  # = 2

# For a balanced design with n participants per cell:
# Total N = n * total_cells = 6n
# df_error = N - total_cells = 6n - 6 = 6(n - 1)

# Conversion from partial eta-squared to noncentrality parameter:
# partial_eta_sq = lambda / (lambda + df_error)
# lambda = partial_eta_sq * df_error / (1 - partial_eta_sq)

# We need to find minimum integer n such that power >= 0.80

library(stats)

# Function to compute power for a given n
compute_power <- function(n) {
  df_error <- 6 * (n - 1)
  lambda <- partial_eta_sq * df_error / (1 - partial_eta_sq)
  
  # Critical F value at alpha = 0.05
  f_crit <- qf(1 - alpha, df1, df_error)
  
  # Power: P(F > f_crit | H1)
  power <- 1 - pf(f_crit, df1, df_error, ncp = lambda)
  
  return(power)
}

# Search for minimum n
n_values <- 1:100
powers <- sapply(n_values, compute_power)

# Find the first n where power >= 0.80
min_n <- n_values[which(powers >= target_power)[1]]

# Compute power at min_n and at min_n - 1 for verification
power_at_min_n <- compute_power(min_n)
power_at_prev_n <- if (min_n > 1) compute_power(min_n - 1) else NA

cat("Design: 3-by-2 factorial ANOVA\n")
cat("Testing factor A (3 levels) main effect\n")
cat("Numerator df:", df1, "\n")
cat("Partial eta-squared:", partial_eta_sq, "\n")
cat("Alpha:", alpha, "\n")
cat("Target power:", target_power, "\n\n")

cat("Results:\n")
cat("Minimum participants per cell:", min_n, "\n")
cat("Achieved power at n =", min_n, ":", round(power_at_min_n, 4), "\n")
if (!is.na(power_at_prev_n)) {
  cat("Power at n =", min_n - 1, ":", round(power_at_prev_n, 4), "\n")
}

# Show the calculation details for the selected design
df_error_min <- 6 * (min_n - 1)
lambda_min <- partial_eta_sq * df_error_min / (1 - partial_eta_sq)
f_crit <- qf(1 - alpha, df1, df_error_min)

cat("\nDetailed calculation for n =", min_n, ":\n")
cat("Total N:", min_n * 6, "participants\n")
cat("Error df:", df_error_min, "\n")
cat("Noncentrality parameter λ:", round(lambda_min, 4), "\n")
cat("Critical F-value (α =", alpha, ", df1 =", df1, ", df2 =", df_error_min, "):", round(f_crit, 4), "\n")

POWER_AGENT_RESULT <- list(
  results = list(
    list(metric = "sample_size", value = min_n, unit = "participants_per_cell"),
    list(metric = "achieved_power", value = round(power_at_min_n, 4), unit = "proportion"),
    list(metric = "power_at_previous_n", value = round(power_at_prev_n, 4), unit = "proportion"),
    list(metric = "total_participants", value = min_n * 6, unit = "participants"),
    list(metric = "error_degrees_of_freedom", value = df_error_min, unit = "df"),
    list(metric = "noncentrality_parameter", value = round(lambda_min, 4), unit = "lambda")
  )
)

cat("\n")
cat(jsonlite::toJSON(POWER_AGENT_RESULT, auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15))

plan.estimand: Main effect of 3-level factor in balanced 3-by-2 factorial ANOVA
plan.hypothesis: H0: The 3-level factor has no main effect (all factor level means equal); H1: At least one factor level mean differs
assumptions: Balanced design: equal sample size n per cell
All 6 cells independent
Full interaction model (main effects and A×B interaction)
Common variance across all cells (homogeneity of variance)
Normal distribution of residuals
Effect size (partial η²) = 0.06 for the 3-level factor main effect
Numerator degrees of freedom = 2 for the tested factor
scientific_notes: Partial eta-squared reflects the proportion of variance explained by the factor, adjusting for other factors in the model
For a 3×2 factorial with full interaction, testing the 3-level factor main effect uses numerator df = 3 - 1 = 2
The noncentrality parameter λ is computed from partial η² and the error degrees of freedom
Power is derived from the noncentral F distribution with df1 = 2, df2 = error df, and noncentrality λ

# Balanced 3-by-2 factorial ANOVA
# Testing the 3-level factor (A) main effect
# Partial eta-squared = 0.06
# Alpha = 0.05
# Target power = 0.80

# Design parameters
alpha <- 0.05
target_power <- 0.80
factor_a_levels <- 3  # 3-level factor (numerator df = 2)
factor_b_levels <- 2  # 2-level factor
total_cells <- factor_a_levels * factor_b_levels  # 6 cells
partial_eta_sq <- 0.06

# Numerator degrees of freedom for testing factor A main effect
df1 <- factor_a_levels - 1  # = 2

# For a balanced design with n participants per cell:
# Total N = n * total_cells = 6n
# df_error = N - total_cells = 6n - 6 = 6(n - 1)

# Conversion from partial eta-squared to noncentrality parameter:
# partial_eta_sq = lambda / (lambda + df_error)
# lambda = partial_eta_sq * df_error / (1 - partial_eta_sq)

# We need to find minimum integer n such that power >= 0.80

library(stats)

# Function to compute power for a given n
compute_power <- function(n) {
  df_error <- 6 * (n - 1)
  lambda <- partial_eta_sq * df_error / (1 - partial_eta_sq)
  
  # Critical F value at alpha = 0.05
  f_crit <- qf(1 - alpha, df1, df_error)
  
  # Power: P(F > f_crit | H1)
  power <- 1 - pf(f_crit, df1, df_error, ncp = lambda)
  
  return(power)
}

# Search for minimum n
n_values <- 1:100
powers <- sapply(n_values, compute_power)

# Find the first n where power >= 0.80
min_n <- n_values[which(powers >= target_power)[1]]

# Compute power at min_n and at min_n - 1 for verification
power_at_min_n <- compute_power(min_n)
power_at_prev_n <- if (min_n > 1) compute_power(min_n - 1) else NA

cat("Design: 3-by-2 factorial ANOVA\n")
cat("Testing factor A (3 levels) main effect\n")
cat("Numerator df:", df1, "\n")
cat("Partial eta-squared:", partial_eta_sq, "\n")
cat("Alpha:", alpha, "\n")
cat("Target power:", target_power, "\n\n")

cat("Results:\n")
cat("Minimum participants per cell:", min_n, "\n")
cat("Achieved power at n =", min_n, ":", round(power_at_min_n, 4), "\n")
if (!is.na(power_at_prev_n)) {
  cat("Power at n =", min_n - 1, ":", round(power_at_prev_n, 4), "\n")
}

# Show the calculation details for the selected design
df_error_min <- 6 * (min_n - 1)
lambda_min <- partial_eta_sq * df_error_min / (1 - partial_eta_sq)
f_crit <- qf(1 - alpha, df1, df_error_min)

cat("\nDetailed calculation for n =", min_n, ":\n")
cat("Total N:", min_n * 6, "participants\n")
cat("Error df:", df_error_min, "\n")
cat("Noncentrality parameter λ:", round(lambda_min, 4), "\n")
cat("Critical F-value (α =", alpha, ", df1 =", df1, ", df2 =", df_error_min, "):", round(f_crit, 4), "\n")

POWER_AGENT_RESULT <- list(
  results = list(
    list(metric = "sample_size", value = min_n, unit = "participants_per_cell"),
    list(metric = "achieved_power", value = round(power_at_min_n, 4), unit = "proportion"),
    list(metric = "power_at_previous_n", value = round(power_at_prev_n, 4), unit = "proportion"),
    list(metric = "total_participants", value = min_n * 6, unit = "participants"),
    list(metric = "error_degrees_of_freedom", value = df_error_min, unit = "df"),
    list(metric = "noncentrality_parameter", value = round(lambda_min, 4), unit = "lambda")
  )
)

cat("\n")
cat(jsonlite::toJSON(POWER_AGENT_RESULT, auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15))

# Sample size for proportion confidence interval precision
# Two-sided 95% CI, half-width 0.03, proportion 0.70
# Using normal approximation with exact z-quantile

# Parameters
p <- 0.70                    # Target proportion
e <- 0.03                    # Desired half-width (margin of error)
alpha <- 0.05                # Significance level for two-sided 95% CI
z_alpha_2 <- qnorm(1 - alpha/2)  # Two-sided 97.5th percentile of standard normal

cat("Parameter Summary:\n")
cat("Target proportion (p):", p, "\n")
cat("Desired CI half-width (E):", e, "\n")
cat("Confidence level:", 1 - alpha, "\n")
cat("Significance level (alpha):", alpha, "\n")
cat("Critical z-value (z_{alpha/2}):", z_alpha_2, "\n")
cat("\n")

# Formula: n = (z_{alpha/2})^2 * p(1-p) / E^2
n_continuous <- (z_alpha_2^2 * p * (1 - p)) / (e^2)

cat("Sample size calculation:\n")
cat("n = (z_{alpha/2})^2 × p(1-p) / E^2\n")
cat("n = (", z_alpha_2, ")^2 × ", p, " × ", 1-p, " / ", e, "^2\n")
cat("n = ", z_alpha_2^2, " × ", p * (1 - p), " / ", e^2, "\n")
cat("n = ", n_continuous, "\n")
cat("\n")

# Round upward to nearest integer
n_rounded <- ceiling(n_continuous)

cat("Rounded sample size (upward):", n_rounded, "participants\n")
cat("\n")

# Verification: compute actual half-width achieved with rounded sample size
actual_se <- sqrt(p * (1 - p) / n_rounded)
actual_half_width <- z_alpha_2 * actual_se
actual_ci_lower <- p - actual_half_width
actual_ci_upper <- p + actual_half_width

cat("Verification with n =", n_rounded, ":\n")
cat("Standard error:", actual_se, "\n")
cat("Actual half-width achieved:", actual_half_width, "\n")
cat("95% CI: [", actual_ci_lower, ", ", actual_ci_upper, "]\n")
cat("Required half-width:", e, "\n")
cat("Actual ≤ Required?", actual_half_width <= e, "\n")

# Output for structured reporting
results <- data.frame(
  metric = "sample_size",
  value = n_rounded,
  unit = "participants_total"
)

library(jsonlite)
cat("\n")
cat("POWER_AGENT_RESULT=")
cat(toJSON(list(results = results), auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15))

library(stats)

# User-specified parameters
mean_reduction <- 3  # kg (effect size: true difference)
sd_baseline <- 5     # kg
sd_followup <- 5.5   # kg
rho <- 0.5           # within-person correlation
alpha <- 0.05        # Type I error
target_power <- 0.80 # 80%
sided <- 1           # one-sided

# Compute the variance of the difference score
# Var(diff) = Var(baseline) + Var(followup) - 2*ρ*SD_baseline*SD_followup
var_diff <- sd_baseline^2 + sd_followup^2 - 2 * rho * sd_baseline * sd_followup
sd_diff <- sqrt(var_diff)

cat("=== Paired t-test Sample Size Calculation ===\n")
cat("Effect parameters:\n")
cat("  Mean weight reduction (δ):", mean_reduction, "kg\n")
cat("  Baseline SD (σ_baseline):", sd_baseline, "kg\n")
cat("  Follow-up SD (σ_followup):", sd_followup, "kg\n")
cat("  Within-person correlation (ρ):", rho, "\n")
cat("  Variance of difference: Var(diff) =", sd_baseline^2, "+", sd_followup^2, "- 2*", rho, "*", sd_baseline, "*", sd_followup, "=", var_diff, "\n")
cat("  SD of difference (σ_diff):", sd_diff, "kg\n")
cat("  Standardized effect (Cohen's d):", mean_reduction / sd_diff, "\n\n")

cat("Test parameters:\n")
cat("  Hypothesis: H0: μ_difference ≤ 0 vs H1: μ_difference > 0\n")
cat("  Sidedness:", sided, "(one-sided)\n")
cat("  Significance level (α):", alpha, "\n")
cat("  Target power:", target_power, "\n\n")

# Critical value for one-sided test (t-distribution with large df approximation)
z_alpha <- qnorm(1 - alpha)  # one-sided critical z
cat("Critical z-value (one-sided, α=0.05):", z_alpha, "\n")

# Power function for paired t-test using approximation and exact calculation
# For a given n, compute power iteratively

power_paired_ttest <- function(n, delta, sd_diff, alpha, sided = 1) {
  # delta: true mean difference
  # sd_diff: SD of the difference scores
  # alpha: Type I error
  # sided: 1 for one-sided, 2 for two-sided
  
  df <- n - 1
  noncentrality <- delta / sd_diff * sqrt(n)
  
  if (sided == 1) {
    # One-sided test: reject if t > t_crit
    t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha, df)
    power <- 1 - pt(t_crit, df, ncp = noncentrality)
  } else {
    # Two-sided test
    t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha/2, df)
    power <- 1 - pt(t_crit, df, ncp = noncentrality) + pt(-t_crit, df, ncp = noncentrality)
  }
  return(power)
}

# Find the minimum sample size satisfying power >= 0.80
n_candidate <- seq(2, 200)
powers <- sapply(n_candidate, function(n) {
  power_paired_ttest(n, mean_reduction, sd_diff, alpha, sided)
})

# Find minimum n with power >= target_power
idx_sufficient <- which(powers >= target_power)
if (length(idx_sufficient) > 0) {
  n_min <- n_candidate[idx_sufficient[1]]
  power_at_min <- powers[idx_sufficient[1]]
  
  # Also report power at n_min - 1 for reference
  if (n_min > 2) {
    n_prev <- n_min - 1
    power_at_prev <- power_paired_ttest(n_prev, mean_reduction, sd_diff, alpha, sided)
  } else {
    n_prev <- NA
    power_at_prev <- NA
  }
} else {
  cat("ERROR: No sample size found meeting the target power\n")
  n_min <- NA
  power_at_min <- NA
}

cat("\n=== Results ===\n")
cat("Minimum sample size (integer):", n_min, "participants\n")
cat("Achieved power at n =", n_min, ":", round(power_at_min, 4), "\n")
if (!is.na(n_prev)) {
  cat("Achieved power at n =", n_prev, "(preceding):", round(power_at_prev, 4), "\n")
}

# Output for POWER_AGENT_RESULT
result_list <- list(
  metric = "sample_size",
  value = n_min,
  unit = "participants_total"
)

cat("\nPOWER_AGENT_RESULT=", jsonlite::toJSON(list(results = list(result_list)), auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15), "\n", sep = "")

cat("         = ", sd_bl^2 + sd_fu^2, " - ", 2*rho*sd_bl*sd_fu, "\n")
cat("         = ", var_diff, "\n")
cat("SD(diff) = √", var_diff, " = ", sd_diff, "\n\n")

# Step 2: Alternative implementation using power.t.test if available
# For paired t-test, we use sd = sd_diff (already pooled in difference)
cat("Step 2: Using stats::power.t.test for paired design\n")

# For paired test: noncentrality = δ * √n / SD_diff

library(stats)

# Search for minimum n with power >= 0.8
min_n_found <- NA
for (n in 2:200) {

  df <- n - 1
  t_crit_one_sided <- qt(1 - alpha, df)  # critical value for one-sided test
  
  # Noncentrality parameter: δ / (SD_diff / √n) = δ * √n / SD_diff
  ncp <- delta / sd_diff * sqrt(n)
  
  # Power = P(t > t_crit | ncp)
  power <- 1 - pt(t_crit_one_sided, df, ncp = ncp)
  
  cat(sprintf("n=%3d: df=%3d, t_crit=%.4f, ncp=%.4f, power=%.6f\n", 
              n, df, t_crit_one_sided, ncp, power))
  
  if (is.na(min_n_found) && power >= power_target) {
    min_n_found <- n
    power_at_min <- power
  }
  
  # Stop when we've found the minimum and gone a few points beyond
  if (!is.na(min_n_found) && n > min_n_found + 3) break
}

cat("Minimum sample size: ", min_n_found, " participants\n")
cat("Power at n = ", min_n_found, ": ", round(power_at_min, 6), "\n")

  df_prev <- n_prev - 1
  ncp_prev <- delta / sd_diff * sqrt(n_prev)
  t_crit_prev <- qt(1 - alpha, df_prev)
  power_prev <- 1 - pt(t_crit_prev, df_prev, ncp = ncp_prev)
  cat("Power at n = ", n_prev, ": ", round(power_prev, 6), "\n")

# Approximate: n ≈ 2 * (z_α + z_β)^2 * σ_diff^2 / δ^2

cat("z_β (power=0.8) = ", z_beta, "\n")
cat("n_approx = 2 * (", z_alpha_one_sided, " + ", z_beta, ")^2 * ", sd_diff^2, " / ", delta^2, "\n")
cat("n_approx = ", n_approx, "\n")
cat("Rounded up: ", ceiling(n_approx), "\n\n")

# Step 4: Cohen's d (standardized effect)
cohens_d <- delta / sd_diff
cat("Cohen's d = δ / σ_diff = ", delta, " / ", sd_diff, " = ", cohens_d, "\n\n")

# Output JSON result
result <- list(
  metric = "sample_size",
  value = min_n_found,
  unit = "participants_total",
  verification_notes = list(
    sd_diff_computed = round(sd_diff, 10),
    cohens_d = round(cohens_d, 10),
    power_at_min_n = round(power_at_min, 6),
    approximate_formula_result = round(n_approx, 2)
  )
)

plan.hypothesis: H0: μ_difference ≤ 0 kg vs H1: μ_difference > 0 kg (one-sided, superiority of 3 kg reduction)
assumptions: Differences in weight (follow-up minus baseline) follow a normal distribution
The within-person correlation of 0.5 applies to weight measurements at baseline and follow-up
Mean difference (effect size) is 3 kg
No attrition or missing data
No multiplicity adjustments
scientific_notes: The paired t-test operates on the difference scores (follow-up minus baseline weight). The variance of the difference is σ²_diff = σ²_baseline + σ²_follow_up - 2·ρ·σ_baseline·σ_follow_up
Given baseline SD = 5 kg, follow-up SD = 5.5 kg, and ρ = 0.5, the difference SD is derived from: Var(diff) = 25 + 30.25 - 2(0.5)(5)(5.5) = 55.25 - 27.5 = 27.75; SD_diff = √27.75 ≈ 5.268 kg
Sample size is computed using the one-sided t-test formula with noncentrality parameter δ = (μ_difference / σ_diff) and critical value from t-distribution with df = n-1
Rounding convention: report the smallest integer n satisfying power ≥ 80% under the specified method
