library(stats)

# User-specified parameters
mean_reduction <- 3  # kg (effect size: true difference)
sd_baseline <- 5     # kg
sd_followup <- 5.5   # kg
rho <- 0.5           # within-person correlation
alpha <- 0.05        # Type I error
target_power <- 0.80 # 80%
sided <- 1           # one-sided

# Compute the variance of the difference score
# Var(diff) = Var(baseline) + Var(followup) - 2*ρ*SD_baseline*SD_followup
var_diff <- sd_baseline^2 + sd_followup^2 - 2 * rho * sd_baseline * sd_followup
sd_diff <- sqrt(var_diff)

cat("=== Paired t-test Sample Size Calculation ===\n")
cat("Effect parameters:\n")
cat("  Mean weight reduction (δ):", mean_reduction, "kg\n")
cat("  Baseline SD (σ_baseline):", sd_baseline, "kg\n")
cat("  Follow-up SD (σ_followup):", sd_followup, "kg\n")
cat("  Within-person correlation (ρ):", rho, "\n")
cat("  Variance of difference: Var(diff) =", sd_baseline^2, "+", sd_followup^2, "- 2*", rho, "*", sd_baseline, "*", sd_followup, "=", var_diff, "\n")
cat("  SD of difference (σ_diff):", sd_diff, "kg\n")
cat("  Standardized effect (Cohen's d):", mean_reduction / sd_diff, "\n\n")

cat("Test parameters:\n")
cat("  Hypothesis: H0: μ_difference ≤ 0 vs H1: μ_difference > 0\n")
cat("  Sidedness:", sided, "(one-sided)\n")
cat("  Significance level (α):", alpha, "\n")
cat("  Target power:", target_power, "\n\n")

# Critical value for one-sided test (t-distribution with large df approximation)
z_alpha <- qnorm(1 - alpha)  # one-sided critical z
cat("Critical z-value (one-sided, α=0.05):", z_alpha, "\n")

# Power function for paired t-test using approximation and exact calculation
# For a given n, compute power iteratively

power_paired_ttest <- function(n, delta, sd_diff, alpha, sided = 1) {
  # delta: true mean difference
  # sd_diff: SD of the difference scores
  # alpha: Type I error
  # sided: 1 for one-sided, 2 for two-sided
  
  df <- n - 1
  noncentrality <- delta / sd_diff * sqrt(n)
  
  if (sided == 1) {
    # One-sided test: reject if t > t_crit
    t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha, df)
    power <- 1 - pt(t_crit, df, ncp = noncentrality)
  } else {
    # Two-sided test
    t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha/2, df)
    power <- 1 - pt(t_crit, df, ncp = noncentrality) + pt(-t_crit, df, ncp = noncentrality)
  }
  return(power)
}

# Find the minimum sample size satisfying power >= 0.80
n_candidate <- seq(2, 200)
powers <- sapply(n_candidate, function(n) {
  power_paired_ttest(n, mean_reduction, sd_diff, alpha, sided)
})

# Find minimum n with power >= target_power
idx_sufficient <- which(powers >= target_power)
if (length(idx_sufficient) > 0) {
  n_min <- n_candidate[idx_sufficient[1]]
  power_at_min <- powers[idx_sufficient[1]]
  
  # Also report power at n_min - 1 for reference
  if (n_min > 2) {
    n_prev <- n_min - 1
    power_at_prev <- power_paired_ttest(n_prev, mean_reduction, sd_diff, alpha, sided)
  } else {
    n_prev <- NA
    power_at_prev <- NA
  }
} else {
  cat("ERROR: No sample size found meeting the target power\n")
  n_min <- NA
  power_at_min <- NA
}

cat("\n=== Results ===\n")
cat("Minimum sample size (integer):", n_min, "participants\n")
cat("Achieved power at n =", n_min, ":", round(power_at_min, 4), "\n")
if (!is.na(n_prev)) {
  cat("Achieved power at n =", n_prev, "(preceding):", round(power_at_prev, 4), "\n")
}

# Output for POWER_AGENT_RESULT
result_list <- list(
  metric = "sample_size",
  value = n_min,
  unit = "participants_total"
)

cat("\nPOWER_AGENT_RESULT=", jsonlite::toJSON(list(results = list(result_list)), auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15), "\n", sep = "")

# Evidence e1; success=true

library(stats)

# User-specified parameters
mean_reduction <- 3  # kg (effect size: true difference)
sd_baseline <- 5     # kg
sd_followup <- 5.5   # kg
rho <- 0.5           # within-person correlation
alpha <- 0.05        # Type I error
target_power <- 0.80 # 80%
sided <- 1           # one-sided

# Compute the variance of the difference score
# Var(diff) = Var(baseline) + Var(followup) - 2*ρ*SD_baseline*SD_followup
var_diff <- sd_baseline^2 + sd_followup^2 - 2 * rho * sd_baseline * sd_followup
sd_diff <- sqrt(var_diff)

cat("=== Paired t-test Sample Size Calculation ===\n")
cat("Effect parameters:\n")
cat("  Mean weight reduction (δ):", mean_reduction, "kg\n")
cat("  Baseline SD (σ_baseline):", sd_baseline, "kg\n")
cat("  Follow-up SD (σ_followup):", sd_followup, "kg\n")
cat("  Within-person correlation (ρ):", rho, "\n")
cat("  Variance of difference: Var(diff) =", sd_baseline^2, "+", sd_followup^2, "- 2*", rho, "*", sd_baseline, "*", sd_followup, "=", var_diff, "\n")
cat("  SD of difference (σ_diff):", sd_diff, "kg\n")
cat("  Standardized effect (Cohen's d):", mean_reduction / sd_diff, "\n\n")

cat("Test parameters:\n")
cat("  Hypothesis: H0: μ_difference ≤ 0 vs H1: μ_difference > 0\n")
cat("  Sidedness:", sided, "(one-sided)\n")
cat("  Significance level (α):", alpha, "\n")
cat("  Target power:", target_power, "\n\n")

# Critical value for one-sided test (t-distribution with large df approximation)
z_alpha <- qnorm(1 - alpha)  # one-sided critical z
cat("Critical z-value (one-sided, α=0.05):", z_alpha, "\n")

# Power function for paired t-test using approximation and exact calculation
# For a given n, compute power iteratively

power_paired_ttest <- function(n, delta, sd_diff, alpha, sided = 1) {
  # delta: true mean difference
  # sd_diff: SD of the difference scores
  # alpha: Type I error
  # sided: 1 for one-sided, 2 for two-sided
  
  df <- n - 1
  noncentrality <- delta / sd_diff * sqrt(n)
  
  if (sided == 1) {
    # One-sided test: reject if t > t_crit
    t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha, df)
    power <- 1 - pt(t_crit, df, ncp = noncentrality)
  } else {
    # Two-sided test
    t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha/2, df)
    power <- 1 - pt(t_crit, df, ncp = noncentrality) + pt(-t_crit, df, ncp = noncentrality)
  }
  return(power)
}

# Find the minimum sample size satisfying power >= 0.80
n_candidate <- seq(2, 200)
powers <- sapply(n_candidate, function(n) {
  power_paired_ttest(n, mean_reduction, sd_diff, alpha, sided)
})

# Find minimum n with power >= target_power
idx_sufficient <- which(powers >= target_power)
if (length(idx_sufficient) > 0) {
  n_min <- n_candidate[idx_sufficient[1]]
  power_at_min <- powers[idx_sufficient[1]]
  
  # Also report power at n_min - 1 for reference
  if (n_min > 2) {
    n_prev <- n_min - 1
    power_at_prev <- power_paired_ttest(n_prev, mean_reduction, sd_diff, alpha, sided)
  } else {
    n_prev <- NA
    power_at_prev <- NA
  }
} else {
  cat("ERROR: No sample size found meeting the target power\n")
  n_min <- NA
  power_at_min <- NA
}

cat("\n=== Results ===\n")
cat("Minimum sample size (integer):", n_min, "participants\n")
cat("Achieved power at n =", n_min, ":", round(power_at_min, 4), "\n")
if (!is.na(n_prev)) {
  cat("Achieved power at n =", n_prev, "(preceding):", round(power_at_prev, 4), "\n")
}

# Output for POWER_AGENT_RESULT
result_list <- list(
  metric = "sample_size",
  value = n_min,
  unit = "participants_total"
)

cat("\nPOWER_AGENT_RESULT=", jsonlite::toJSON(list(results = list(result_list)), auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15), "\n", sep = "")

# Design parameters
alpha <- 0.05
target_power <- 0.90
rho <- 0.30  # anticipated multiple correlation
k <- 3       # number of predictors
p <- k + 1   # degrees of freedom numerator (k predictors)

# For two-sided test, use alpha/2 for each tail in F test
# The F test is inherently one-sided (testing against larger values)
alpha_f <- alpha  # For F-test, we compare to critical value at alpha level

# Noncentrality parameter: lambda = n * rho^2 / (1 - rho^2)
# Effect size: f^2 = rho^2 / (1 - rho^2)
f_squared <- rho^2 / (1 - rho^2)

# Grid search for minimum sample size
sample_sizes <- seq(10, 200, by = 1)
powers <- numeric(length(sample_sizes))

for (i in seq_along(sample_sizes)) {
  n <- sample_sizes[i]
  df1 <- k           # numerator df
  df2 <- n - k - 1   # denominator df
  
  # Noncentrality parameter
  lambda <- n * f_squared
  
  # Critical F value (one-sided test at alpha level)
  f_crit <- qf(1 - alpha_f, df1, df2)
  
  # Power from noncentral F distribution
  power <- 1 - pf(f_crit, df1, df2, lambda)
  powers[i] <- power
}

# Find minimum sample size achieving target power
min_idx <- which(powers >= target_power)[1]
min_sample_size <- sample_sizes[min_idx]
achieved_power <- powers[min_idx]

# Also report the sample size just below minimum for comparison
if (min_idx > 1) {
  prev_sample_size <- sample_sizes[min_idx - 1]
  prev_power <- powers[min_idx - 1]
} else {
  prev_sample_size <- NA
  prev_power <- NA
}

# Display results
cat("=== Linear Regression R² Test Sample Size Calculation ===\n")
cat("Null hypothesis: H₀: ρ² = 0\n")
cat("Alternative hypothesis: H₁: ρ² ≠ 0 (two-sided)\n")
cat("Test: Noncentral F test\n\n")
cat("Design parameters:\n")
cat("  Significance level (α):", alpha, "\n")
cat("  Target power:", target_power, "\n")
cat("  Anticipated multiple correlation (ρ):", rho, "\n")
cat("  Number of predictors (k):", k, "\n")
cat("  Numerator df:", k, "\n")
cat("  Effect size (f² = ρ²/(1-ρ²)):", round(f_squared, 6), "\n\n")

cat("Sample size search:\n")
cat("  Minimum sample size achieving 90% power: N =", min_sample_size, "\n")
cat("  Achieved power at N =", min_sample_size, ":", round(achieved_power, 4), "\n")

if (!is.na(prev_sample_size)) {
  cat("  Power at N =", prev_sample_size, "(preceding design):", round(prev_power, 4), "\n")
}

# Detailed calculation for minimum sample size
n_min <- min_sample_size
df1_min <- k
df2_min <- n_min - k - 1
lambda_min <- n_min * f_squared
f_crit_min <- qf(1 - alpha_f, df1_min, df2_min)
power_min <- 1 - pf(f_crit_min, df1_min, df2_min, lambda_min)

cat("\nDetailed calculation for N =", n_min, ":\n")
cat("  Denominator df: n - k - 1 =", n_min, "-", k, "- 1 =", df2_min, "\n")
cat("  Noncentrality parameter (λ): n × f² =", n_min, "×", round(f_squared, 6), "=", round(lambda_min, 4), "\n")
cat("  Critical F value (F₃,₍ₙ₋₄₎; 1-α):", round(f_crit_min, 4), "\n")
cat("  Power = P(F(3,", df2_min, ", λ=", round(lambda_min, 4), ") > ", round(f_crit_min, 4), ") =", round(power_min, 4), "\n")

# Return structured result
result <- list(
  sample_size = min_sample_size,
  achieved_power = round(achieved_power, 4),
  preceding_sample_size = ifelse(is.na(prev_sample_size), NA, prev_sample_size),
  preceding_power = ifelse(is.na(prev_power), NA, round(prev_power, 4)),
  target_power = target_power,
  alpha = alpha,
  noncentrality_parameter = round(lambda_min, 4),
  critical_f_value = round(f_crit_min, 4)
)

library(jsonlite)
cat("\n\nStructured output:\n")
print(toJSON(result, auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15))

# Design parameters
alpha <- 0.05
target_power <- 0.90
rho <- 0.30  # anticipated multiple correlation
k <- 3       # number of predictors
p <- k + 1   # degrees of freedom numerator (k predictors)

# For two-sided test, use alpha/2 for each tail in F test
# The F test is inherently one-sided (testing against larger values)
alpha_f <- alpha  # For F-test, we compare to critical value at alpha level

# Noncentrality parameter: lambda = n * rho^2 / (1 - rho^2)
# Effect size: f^2 = rho^2 / (1 - rho^2)
f_squared <- rho^2 / (1 - rho^2)

# Grid search for minimum sample size
sample_sizes <- seq(10, 200, by = 1)
powers <- numeric(length(sample_sizes))

for (i in seq_along(sample_sizes)) {
  n <- sample_sizes[i]
  df1 <- k           # numerator df
  df2 <- n - k - 1   # denominator df
  
  # Noncentrality parameter
  lambda <- n * f_squared
  
  # Critical F value (one-sided test at alpha level)
  f_crit <- qf(1 - alpha_f, df1, df2)
  
  # Power from noncentral F distribution
  power <- 1 - pf(f_crit, df1, df2, lambda)
  powers[i] <- power
}

# Find minimum sample size achieving target power
min_idx <- which(powers >= target_power)[1]
min_sample_size <- sample_sizes[min_idx]
achieved_power <- powers[min_idx]

# Also report the sample size just below minimum for comparison
if (min_idx > 1) {
  prev_sample_size <- sample_sizes[min_idx - 1]
  prev_power <- powers[min_idx - 1]
} else {
  prev_sample_size <- NA
  prev_power <- NA
}

# Display results
cat("=== Linear Regression R² Test Sample Size Calculation ===\n")
cat("Null hypothesis: H₀: ρ² = 0\n")
cat("Alternative hypothesis: H₁: ρ² ≠ 0 (two-sided)\n")
cat("Test: Noncentral F test\n\n")
cat("Design parameters:\n")
cat("  Significance level (α):", alpha, "\n")
cat("  Target power:", target_power, "\n")
cat("  Anticipated multiple correlation (ρ):", rho, "\n")
cat("  Number of predictors (k):", k, "\n")
cat("  Numerator df:", k, "\n")
cat("  Effect size (f² = ρ²/(1-ρ²)):", round(f_squared, 6), "\n\n")

cat("Sample size search:\n")
cat("  Minimum sample size achieving 90% power: N =", min_sample_size, "\n")
cat("  Achieved power at N =", min_sample_size, ":", round(achieved_power, 4), "\n")

if (!is.na(prev_sample_size)) {
  cat("  Power at N =", prev_sample_size, "(preceding design):", round(prev_power, 4), "\n")
}

# Detailed calculation for minimum sample size
n_min <- min_sample_size
df1_min <- k
df2_min <- n_min - k - 1
lambda_min <- n_min * f_squared
f_crit_min <- qf(1 - alpha_f, df1_min, df2_min)
power_min <- 1 - pf(f_crit_min, df1_min, df2_min, lambda_min)

cat("\nDetailed calculation for N =", n_min, ":\n")
cat("  Denominator df: n - k - 1 =", n_min, "-", k, "- 1 =", df2_min, "\n")
cat("  Noncentrality parameter (λ): n × f² =", n_min, "×", round(f_squared, 6), "=", round(lambda_min, 4), "\n")
cat("  Critical F value (F₃,₍ₙ₋₄₎; 1-α):", round(f_crit_min, 4), "\n")
cat("  Power = P(F(3,", df2_min, ", λ=", round(lambda_min, 4), ") > ", round(f_crit_min, 4), ") =", round(power_min, 4), "\n")

# Return structured result
result <- list(
  sample_size = min_sample_size,
  achieved_power = round(achieved_power, 4),
  preceding_sample_size = ifelse(is.na(prev_sample_size), NA, prev_sample_size),
  preceding_power = ifelse(is.na(prev_power), NA, round(prev_power, 4)),
  target_power = target_power,
  alpha = alpha,
  noncentrality_parameter = round(lambda_min, 4),
  critical_f_value = round(f_crit_min, 4)
)

library(jsonlite)
cat("\n\nStructured output:\n")
print(toJSON(result, auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15))

plan.estimand: Between-group main effect (group 1 vs group 2) on subject-level average across 3 repeated measurements
plan.hypothesis: H0: μ₁ = μ₂ vs H1: μ₁ ≠ μ₂ where μ₁, μ₂ are population mean averages for groups 1 and 2
assumptions: Multivariate normal observations within each group
Compound symmetry covariance structure across the 3 repeated measurements
Equal correlation ρ = 0.5 between all pairs of occasions
Equal marginal SD = 2.5 at each occasion and across groups
No missing data
No group-by-time interaction (parallel growth curves)
Between-group comparison uses subject-level average (mean across 3 occasions per participant)
Pooled t-test on subject averages (equivalent to between-group F-test in ANOVA)
Equal variances across groups (homogeneity)
scientific_notes: Under compound symmetry with k=3 occasions and correlation ρ=0.5, the variance of the subject-level average is: Var(Ȳᵢ) = σ²/k × [1 + (k-1)ρ] = (2.5)²/3 × [1 + 2(0.5)] = 6.25/3 × 2 = 12.5/3 ≈ 4.167. Standard error of the mean is approximately 1.291.
The effect size (standardized mean difference) is Δ/SD_average = 2/√(4.167) ≈ 0.975, a large effect.
The pooled t-test on subject averages reduces to comparing two independent samples with n participants per group; degrees of freedom = 2n - 2.
This is equivalent to the between-group F-test in a repeated-measures ANOVA (F = t²).
Inversion for target power 0.80 with α=0.05 two-sided will identify the minimum integer n per group.

answer.summary: For a balanced repeated-measures ANOVA with 2 groups and 3 repeated measurements per participant, assuming compound symmetry (ρ = 0.5), marginal SD = 2.5 at each occasion, group means of 51 and 49, no missing data, and no group-by-time interaction, the minimum integer sample size per group to achieve 80% power for the between-group main effect is **18 participants per group** (36 total). This is based on a two-sided pooled t-test on subject-level averages at α = 0.05. The achieved power at n = 18 is 81.47%, exceeding the target. The preceding integer (n = 17) yields 79.10% power, falling short of the target.
answer.method: Two-sample t-test on subject-level averages (independent samples, pooled variance), equivalent to the between-group F-test in repeated-measures ANOVA. The variance of each subject's average across 3 occasions is Var(Ȳᵢ) = σ²/k × [1 + (k-1)ρ] = (2.5)²/3 × [1 + 2(0.5)] = 4.1667, giving SD_average = 2.0412. The effect size is δ = 2 (Group 1 mean − Group 2 mean = 51 − 49), yielding Cohen's d = 2/2.0412 ≈ 0.9798 (large effect). Sample size inversion using R's power.t.test function with two-sided alternative, α = 0.05, and target power 0.80 yields n = 17.3666 continuous; rounded up to n = 18 per group. Verification confirms 81.47% power at n = 18 and 79.10% power at n = 17.
assumptions: Multivariate normal observations within each group across the 3 occasions
Compound symmetry covariance structure: equal variances (2.5² = 6.25) at each occasion and equal correlation ρ = 0.5 between all pairs of occasions
Equal group means under H₁: μ₁ = 51, μ₂ = 49
No missing data across the repeated measurements
No group-by-time interaction (parallel mean trajectories)
Pooled t-test on subject-level averages assumes equal variances across groups
Between-group comparison uses the mean of each participant's 3 measurements as the analysis unit
Significance level α = 0.05 (two-sided)
Balanced design with equal numbers per group
limitations: The design assumes no attrition; if dropout is expected, sample size should be inflated accordingly (not included here)
Compound symmetry is a restrictive assumption; if the true correlation structure deviates substantially, power may differ
The analysis assumes the compound symmetry assumption holds exactly; violation (e.g., autoregressive or heterogeneous correlation) could reduce power
The design does not account for covariates; adjusting for baseline or time-varying covariates could increase efficiency
No provision for multiple comparisons if post-hoc tests beyond the primary group effect are planned

executions.code:
# Repeated-measures ANOVA: Between-group effect with subject-level averages
# Design: 2 groups, k=3 repeated measurements per participant
# Compound symmetry covariance, equal group means under H1

# Parameters
k <- 3  # number of repeated measurements (occasions)
rho <- 0.5  # compound symmetry correlation
sigma_marginal <- 2.5  # marginal SD at each occasion
mu1 <- 51  # Group 1 mean
mu2 <- 49  # Group 2 mean
delta <- mu1 - mu2  # effect size (difference in population means)

# Variance of subject-level average under compound symmetry
# Var(Y_bar_i) = sigma^2 / k * [1 + (k-1)*rho]
var_average <- (sigma_marginal^2 / k) * (1 + (k - 1) * rho)
sd_average <- sqrt(var_average)

cat("Repeated-Measures ANOVA: Between-Group Effect via Subject Averages\n")
cat("================================================================\n")
cat(sprintf("Number of occasions (k): %d\n", k))
cat(sprintf("Compound symmetry correlation (ρ): %.2f\n", rho))
cat(sprintf("Marginal SD at each occasion: %.2f\n", sigma_marginal))
cat(sprintf("Group 1 mean: %.1f\n", mu1))
cat(sprintf("Group 2 mean: %.1f\n", mu2))
cat(sprintf("Effect size (μ₁ - μ₂): %.1f\n", delta))
cat(sprintf("\nVariance of subject-level average: %.4f\n", var_average))
cat(sprintf("SD of subject-level average: %.4f\n", sd_average))

# Standardized effect size (Cohen's d for independent samples t-test)
cohens_d <- delta / sd_average
cat(sprintf("Cohen's d (standardized effect): %.4f\n\n", cohens_d))

# For power analysis: use t-test on independent samples (subject averages)
# H0: μ₁ = μ₂
# H1: μ₁ ≠ μ₂ (two-sided)
# α = 0.05, target power = 0.80

alpha <- 0.05
target_power <- 0.80

# Using power.t.test for two independent samples
# power.t.test expects:
# - n: number of observations per group
# - delta: effect size (difference in means)
# - sd: standard deviation (same for both groups under homogeneity)
# - sig.level: significance level
# - power: target power
# - type: "two.sample" for independent samples t-test
# - alternative: "two.sided"

# Invert for n given target power
result <- power.t.test(
  n = NULL,  # solve for n
  delta = delta,
  sd = sd_average,
  sig.level = alpha,
  power = target_power,
  type = "two.sample",
  alternative = "two.sided"
)

cat("Sample Size Inversion (target power = 0.80)\n")
cat("==========================================\n")
print(result)

n_continuous <- result$n
n_integer <- ceiling(n_continuous)

cat(sprintf("\nContinuous solution: n = %.4f participants per group\n", n_continuous))
cat(sprintf("Rounded-up integer: n = %d participants per group\n", n_integer))

# Verify: compute achieved power at the rounded-up value
power_at_n <- power.t.test(
  n = n_integer,
  delta = delta,
  sd = sd_average,
  sig.level = alpha,
  type = "two.sample",
  alternative = "two.sided"
)$power

cat(sprintf("\nVerification at n = %d per group:\n", n_integer))
cat(sprintf("Achieved power: %.6f (target: 0.80)\n", power_at_n))

# Also check the preceding admissible integer (n-1)
if (n_integer > 1) {
  n_prev <- n_integer - 1
  power_at_prev <- power.t.test(
    n = n_prev,
    delta = delta,
    sd = sd_average,
    sig.level = alpha,
    type = "two.sample",
    alternative = "two.sided"
  )$power
  
  cat(sprintf("\nPrevious integer n = %d per group:\n", n_prev))
  cat(sprintf("Achieved power: %.6f\n", power_at_prev))
}

# Final answer
cat(sprintf("\n\nFINAL ANSWER\n"))
cat(sprintf("============\n"))
cat(sprintf("Minimum integer participants per group: %d\n", n_integer))
cat(sprintf("Achieved power at n = %d: %.4f\n", n_integer, power_at_n))

# Store results for output
results_list <- list(
  sample_size = n_integer,
  achieved_power = power_at_n,
  continuous_n = n_continuous,
  delta = delta,
  sd_average = sd_average,
  cohens_d = cohens_d
)

# Output as JSON
library(jsonlite)
output <- list(
  results = list(
    list(metric = "sample_size", value = n_integer, unit = "participants_per_group"),
    list(metric = "achieved_power", value = round(power_at_n, 6), unit = "proportion"),
    list(metric = "continuous_solution_n", value = round(n_continuous, 4), unit = "participants_per_group"),
    list(metric = "effect_size_cohens_d", value = round(cohens_d, 4), unit = "dimensionless"),
    list(metric = "sd_of_subject_averages", value = round(sd_average, 4), unit = "units")
  )
)

cat("\nPOWER_AGENT_RESULT=")
cat(toJSON(output, auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15))

# Repeated-measures ANOVA: Between-group effect with subject-level averages
# Design: 2 groups, k=3 repeated measurements per participant
# Compound symmetry covariance, equal group means under H1

# Parameters
k <- 3  # number of repeated measurements (occasions)
rho <- 0.5  # compound symmetry correlation
sigma_marginal <- 2.5  # marginal SD at each occasion
mu1 <- 51  # Group 1 mean
mu2 <- 49  # Group 2 mean
delta <- mu1 - mu2  # effect size (difference in population means)

# Variance of subject-level average under compound symmetry
# Var(Y_bar_i) = sigma^2 / k * [1 + (k-1)*rho]
var_average <- (sigma_marginal^2 / k) * (1 + (k - 1) * rho)
sd_average <- sqrt(var_average)

cat("Repeated-Measures ANOVA: Between-Group Effect via Subject Averages\n")
cat("================================================================\n")
cat(sprintf("Number of occasions (k): %d\n", k))
cat(sprintf("Compound symmetry correlation (ρ): %.2f\n", rho))
cat(sprintf("Marginal SD at each occasion: %.2f\n", sigma_marginal))
cat(sprintf("Group 1 mean: %.1f\n", mu1))
cat(sprintf("Group 2 mean: %.1f\n", mu2))
cat(sprintf("Effect size (μ₁ - μ₂): %.1f\n", delta))
cat(sprintf("\nVariance of subject-level average: %.4f\n", var_average))
cat(sprintf("SD of subject-level average: %.4f\n", sd_average))

# Standardized effect size (Cohen's d for independent samples t-test)
cohens_d <- delta / sd_average
cat(sprintf("Cohen's d (standardized effect): %.4f\n\n", cohens_d))

# For power analysis: use t-test on independent samples (subject averages)
# H0: μ₁ = μ₂
# H1: μ₁ ≠ μ₂ (two-sided)
# α = 0.05, target power = 0.80

alpha <- 0.05
target_power <- 0.80

# Using power.t.test for two independent samples
# power.t.test expects:
# - n: number of observations per group
# - delta: effect size (difference in means)
# - sd: standard deviation (same for both groups under homogeneity)
# - sig.level: significance level
# - power: target power
# - type: "two.sample" for independent samples t-test
# - alternative: "two.sided"

# Invert for n given target power
result <- power.t.test(
  n = NULL,  # solve for n
  delta = delta,
  sd = sd_average,
  sig.level = alpha,
  power = target_power,
  type = "two.sample",
  alternative = "two.sided"
)

cat("Sample Size Inversion (target power = 0.80)\n")
cat("==========================================\n")
print(result)

n_continuous <- result$n
n_integer <- ceiling(n_continuous)

cat(sprintf("\nContinuous solution: n = %.4f participants per group\n", n_continuous))
cat(sprintf("Rounded-up integer: n = %d participants per group\n", n_integer))

# Verify: compute achieved power at the rounded-up value
power_at_n <- power.t.test(
  n = n_integer,
  delta = delta,
  sd = sd_average,
  sig.level = alpha,
  type = "two.sample",
  alternative = "two.sided"
)$power

cat(sprintf("\nVerification at n = %d per group:\n", n_integer))
cat(sprintf("Achieved power: %.6f (target: 0.80)\n", power_at_n))

# Also check the preceding admissible integer (n-1)
if (n_integer > 1) {
  n_prev <- n_integer - 1
  power_at_prev <- power.t.test(
    n = n_prev,
    delta = delta,
    sd = sd_average,
    sig.level = alpha,
    type = "two.sample",
    alternative = "two.sided"
  )$power
  
  cat(sprintf("\nPrevious integer n = %d per group:\n", n_prev))
  cat(sprintf("Achieved power: %.6f\n", power_at_prev))
}

# Final answer
cat(sprintf("\n\nFINAL ANSWER\n"))
cat(sprintf("============\n"))
cat(sprintf("Minimum integer participants per group: %d\n", n_integer))
cat(sprintf("Achieved power at n = %d: %.4f\n", n_integer, power_at_n))

# Store results for output
results_list <- list(
  sample_size = n_integer,
  achieved_power = power_at_n,
  continuous_n = n_continuous,
  delta = delta,
  sd_average = sd_average,
  cohens_d = cohens_d
)

# Output as JSON
library(jsonlite)
output <- list(
  results = list(
    list(metric = "sample_size", value = n_integer, unit = "participants_per_group"),
    list(metric = "achieved_power", value = round(power_at_n, 6), unit = "proportion"),
    list(metric = "continuous_solution_n", value = round(n_continuous, 4), unit = "participants_per_group"),
    list(metric = "effect_size_cohens_d", value = round(cohens_d, 4), unit = "dimensionless"),
    list(metric = "sd_of_subject_averages", value = round(sd_average, 4), unit = "units")
  )
)

cat("\nPOWER_AGENT_RESULT=")
cat(toJSON(output, auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15))

# One-sample t-test: minimum sample size for 80% power
# H0: μ = 0 vs H1: μ > 0 (one-sided)
# Effect: mean = 0.2, SD = 0.5, so Cohen's d = 0.2/0.5 = 0.4
# Alpha = 0.05, Target power = 0.80

library(pwr)

# Define effect size
mean_diff <- 0.2
sd <- 0.5
cohens_d <- mean_diff / sd

alpha <- 0.05
target_power <- 0.80

# For one-sided test, we adjust alpha for two-sided equivalent
# pwr package uses two-sided by default, so we use alpha/2 for one-sided
# Actually, for pwr.t.test with one-sided: alternative="greater" uses the full alpha

# Use pwr.t.test for one-sample t-test
# n = NULL to solve for sample size
# d = effect size (Cohen's d)
# sig.level = alpha
# power = target power
# type = "one.sample"
# alternative = "greater" for one-sided

result <- pwr.t.test(
  n = NULL,
  d = cohens_d,
  sig.level = alpha,
  power = target_power,
  type = "one.sample",
  alternative = "greater"
)

print(result)
cat("\n")
cat("Effect size (Cohen's d):", cohens_d, "\n")
cat("Exact sample size needed:", result$n, "\n")
cat("Minimum integer sample size:", ceiling(result$n), "\n")

# Verify power at the rounded sample size
n_min <- ceiling(result$n)
verified_power <- pwr.t.test(
  n = n_min,
  d = cohens_d,
  sig.level = alpha,
  type = "one.sample",
  alternative = "greater"
)

cat("\nVerification at n =", n_min, ":\n")
print(verified_power)
cat("Achieved power:", verified_power$power, "\n")

# Also check power at n-1 to confirm it's below 80%
if (n_min > 1) {
  power_at_prev <- pwr.t.test(
    n = n_min - 1,
    d = cohens_d,
    sig.level = alpha,
    type = "one.sample",
    alternative = "greater"
  )
  cat("\nPower at n =", n_min - 1, ":", power_at_prev$power, "\n")
}

# Prepare final result
POWER_AGENT_RESULT=jsonlite::toJSON(
  list(
    results = list(
      list(metric = "sample_size", value = n_min, unit = "participants_total"),
      list(metric = "achieved_power", value = round(verified_power$power, 6), unit = "proportion"),
      list(metric = "power_at_n_minus_1", value = if(n_min > 1) round(power_at_prev$power, 6) else NA, unit = "proportion"),
      list(metric = "cohens_d", value = cohens_d, unit = "standardized")
    )
  ),
  auto_unbox = TRUE,
  digits = 15
)

# Independent verification using non-centrality parameter approach
# For one-sample t-test with one-sided H1: μ > 0

# Given parameters
mean_diff <- 0.2
sd <- 0.5
cohens_d <- mean_diff / sd  # 0.4
alpha <- 0.05
target_power <- 0.80

# For one-sided test at alpha = 0.05, critical value from standard normal
# (using normal approximation or t-distribution)
# For one-sided t-test: reject H0 if t > t_crit(alpha, df=n-1)

# Non-centrality parameter: lambda = d * sqrt(n)
# Power formula: P(t_{n-1}(lambda) > t_{crit}) = target_power
# where t_{crit} = t_{1-alpha}(n-1)

# We need to solve for n iteratively or use formula

# Analytic approach using t-distribution
# For large n, this approaches normal: Φ(lambda - z_{1-alpha}) ≈ power

# More precisely, for one-sample t-test:
# lambda = d * sqrt(n)
# Power = P(t_{n-1}(lambda) > t_{1-alpha}(n-1))

# Function to compute power given n
compute_power_onesample <- function(n, cohens_d, alpha = 0.05) {
  if (n < 1) return(0)
  df <- n - 1
  lambda <- cohens_d * sqrt(n)
  t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha, df = df)  # critical value for one-sided test
  # Power is P(T > t_crit) where T ~ t_{df}(lambda)
  power <- 1 - pt(t_crit, df = df, ncp = lambda)
  return(power)
}

# Verify at n=41 and n=40
power_40 <- compute_power_onesample(40, cohens_d)
power_41 <- compute_power_onesample(41, cohens_d)

cat("Cohen's d =", cohens_d, "\n")
cat("Alpha = 0.05 (one-sided)\n\n")
cat("Power at n = 40:", format(power_40, digits = 10), "\n")
cat("Power at n = 41:", format(power_41, digits = 10), "\n")

# Verify pwr.t.test behavior for one-sided tests
# The critical question: does pwr.t.test correctly handle alpha for one-sided tests?

library(pwr)

# Test the function with explicit documentation check
cohens_d <- 0.4
alpha <- 0.05

# One-sided test with alternative="greater"
result_one_sided <- pwr.t.test(
  n = NULL,
  d = cohens_d,
  sig.level = alpha,
  power = 0.80,
  type = "one.sample",
  alternative = "greater"
)

# Two-sided test for comparison
result_two_sided <- pwr.t.test(
  n = NULL,
  d = cohens_d,
  sig.level = alpha,
  power = 0.80,
  type = "one.sample",
  alternative = "two.sided"
)

cat("pwr.t.test Alpha Handling Verification:\n\n")
cat("Parameters:\n")
cat("  d = 0.4 (Cohen's d)\n")
cat("  power = 0.80\n")
cat("  sig.level = 0.05\n")
cat("  type = 'one.sample'\n\n")

# One-sample t-test: minimum sample size for 80% power
# H0: μ = 0 vs H1: μ > 0 (one-sided)
# Effect: mean = 0.2, SD = 0.5, so Cohen's d = 0.2/0.5 = 0.4
# Alpha = 0.05, Target power = 0.80

library(pwr)

# Define effect size
mean_diff <- 0.2
sd <- 0.5
cohens_d <- mean_diff / sd

alpha <- 0.05
target_power <- 0.80

# For one-sided test, we adjust alpha for two-sided equivalent
# pwr package uses two-sided by default, so we use alpha/2 for one-sided
# Actually, for pwr.t.test with one-sided: alternative="greater" uses the full alpha

# Use pwr.t.test for one-sample t-test
# n = NULL to solve for sample size
# d = effect size (Cohen's d)
# sig.level = alpha
# power = target power
# type = "one.sample"
# alternative = "greater" for one-sided

result <- pwr.t.test(
  n = NULL,
  d = cohens_d,
  sig.level = alpha,
  power = target_power,
  type = "one.sample",
  alternative = "greater"
)

print(result)
cat("\n")
cat("Effect size (Cohen's d):", cohens_d, "\n")
cat("Exact sample size needed:", result$n, "\n")
cat("Minimum integer sample size:", ceiling(result$n), "\n")

# Verify power at the rounded sample size
n_min <- ceiling(result$n)
verified_power <- pwr.t.test(
  n = n_min,
  d = cohens_d,
  sig.level = alpha,
  type = "one.sample",
  alternative = "greater"
)

cat("\nVerification at n =", n_min, ":\n")
print(verified_power)
cat("Achieved power:", verified_power$power, "\n")

# Also check power at n-1 to confirm it's below 80%
if (n_min > 1) {
  power_at_prev <- pwr.t.test(
    n = n_min - 1,
    d = cohens_d,
    sig.level = alpha,
    type = "one.sample",
    alternative = "greater"
  )
  cat("\nPower at n =", n_min - 1, ":", power_at_prev$power, "\n")
}

# Prepare final result
POWER_AGENT_RESULT=jsonlite::toJSON(
  list(
    results = list(
      list(metric = "sample_size", value = n_min, unit = "participants_total"),
      list(metric = "achieved_power", value = round(verified_power$power, 6), unit = "proportion"),
      list(metric = "power_at_n_minus_1", value = if(n_min > 1) round(power_at_prev$power, 6) else NA, unit = "proportion"),
      list(metric = "cohens_d", value = cohens_d, unit = "standardized")
    )
  ),
  auto_unbox = TRUE,
  digits = 15
)

# Independent verification using non-centrality parameter approach
# For one-sample t-test with one-sided H1: μ > 0

# Given parameters
mean_diff <- 0.2
sd <- 0.5
cohens_d <- mean_diff / sd  # 0.4
alpha <- 0.05
target_power <- 0.80

# For one-sided test at alpha = 0.05, critical value from standard normal
# (using normal approximation or t-distribution)
# For one-sided t-test: reject H0 if t > t_crit(alpha, df=n-1)

# Non-centrality parameter: lambda = d * sqrt(n)
# Power formula: P(t_{n-1}(lambda) > t_{crit}) = target_power
# where t_{crit} = t_{1-alpha}(n-1)

# We need to solve for n iteratively or use formula

# Analytic approach using t-distribution
# For large n, this approaches normal: Φ(lambda - z_{1-alpha}) ≈ power

# More precisely, for one-sample t-test:
# lambda = d * sqrt(n)
# Power = P(t_{n-1}(lambda) > t_{1-alpha}(n-1))

# Function to compute power given n
compute_power_onesample <- function(n, cohens_d, alpha = 0.05) {
  if (n < 1) return(0)
  df <- n - 1
  lambda <- cohens_d * sqrt(n)
  t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha, df = df)  # critical value for one-sided test
  # Power is P(T > t_crit) where T ~ t_{df}(lambda)
  power <- 1 - pt(t_crit, df = df, ncp = lambda)
  return(power)
}

# Verify at n=41 and n=40
power_40 <- compute_power_onesample(40, cohens_d)
power_41 <- compute_power_onesample(41, cohens_d)

cat("Independent verification using analytic t-distribution:\n")
cat("Cohen's d =", cohens_d, "\n")
cat("Alpha = 0.05 (one-sided)\n\n")
cat("Power at n = 40:", format(power_40, digits = 10), "\n")
cat("Power at n = 41:", format(power_41, digits = 10), "\n")
cat("\nCandidate reported:\n")
cat("Power at n = 40: 0.7997377897533268\n")
cat("Power at n = 41: 0.8085822361697333\n")

# Check if they match
tol <- 1e-6
match_40 <- abs(power_40 - 0.7997377897533268) < tol
match_41 <- abs(power_41 - 0.8085822361697333) < tol

cat("\nMatch at n=40:", match_40, "(difference:", abs(power_40 - 0.7997377897533268), ")\n")
cat("Match at n=41:", match_41, "(difference:", abs(power_41 - 0.8085822361697333), ")\n")

# Verify that n=41 is indeed the minimum

meets_target_41 <- power_41 >= 0.80
below_target_40 <- power_40 < 0.80

cat("Power at n=41 >= 0.80:", meets_target_41, "\n")
cat("Power at n=40 < 0.80:", below_target_40, "\n")
cat("n=41 is minimum admissible:", meets_target_41 && below_target_40, "\n")

cat("Mean difference:", mean_diff, "\n")

# => Reject H0 if test statistic > critical value
# => One-sided alpha = 0.05

# The pwr package for one-sample t-test with alternative="greater"
# tests H0: μ = 0 vs H1: μ > 0 at the specified alpha level

# Critical value for one-sided t-test at alpha=0.05, df=40
alpha <- 0.05
df_40 <- 39
df_41 <- 40

t_crit_40 <- qt(1 - alpha, df = df_40)  # one-sided critical value
t_crit_41 <- qt(1 - alpha, df = df_41)

cat("Hypothesis Verification:\n")
cat("H0: μ = 0\n")
cat("H1: μ > 0 (one-sided, right-tailed)\n")
cat("Significance level α = 0.05\n\n")

cat("t_crit(α=0.05, df=40) =", format(t_crit_41, digits=6), "\n\n")

# Check: the test statistic is t = (sample_mean - 0) / SE

cat("λ at n=41: ", cohens_d * sqrt(41), "\n\n")

# The critical question: does pwr.t.test correctly handle alpha for one-sided tests?

library(pwr)

# Test the function with explicit documentation check
cohens_d <- 0.4
alpha <- 0.05

result_one_sided <- pwr.t.test(
  n = NULL,
  d = cohens_d,
  sig.level = alpha,
  power = 0.80,
  type = "one.sample",
  alternative = "greater"
)

# Two-sided test for comparison
result_two_sided <- pwr.t.test(
  n = NULL,
  d = cohens_d,
  sig.level = alpha,
  power = 0.80,
  type = "one.sample",
  alternative = "two.sided"
)

cat("pwr.t.test Alpha Handling Verification:\n\n")
cat("Parameters:\n")
cat("  d = 0.4 (Cohen's d)\n")
cat("  power = 0.80\n")
cat("  sig.level = 0.05\n")
cat("  type = 'one.sample'\n\n")

cat("  Rounded up:", ceiling(result_one_sided$n), "\n\n")

cat("Two-sided test (alternative='two.sided'):\n")
cat("  Required sample size:", result_two_sided$n, "\n")
cat("  Rounded up:", ceiling(result_two_sided$n), "\n\n")

ratio <- result_two_sided$n / result_one_sided$n

# Effect: mean = 0.2, SD = 0.5, so Cohen's d = 0.2/0.5 = 0.4

alpha <- 0.05
target_power <- 0.80

# For one-sided test, we adjust alpha for two-sided equivalent

# Actually, for pwr.t.test with one-sided: alternative="greater" uses the full alpha

result <- pwr.t.test(
  n = NULL,
  d = cohens_d,
  sig.level = alpha,
  power = target_power,
  type = "one.sample",
  alternative = "greater"
)

plan.estimand: omnibus F-statistic difference in population means across 3 independent groups
plan.hypothesis: H₀: μ₁ = μ₂ = μ₃ vs. H₁: at least one mean differs
assumptions: Observations within each group are independent and identically normally distributed
Homogeneity of variance: common population variance σ² across all groups
Fixed effects model: groups are of primary interest (not random sample from population of groups)
Population eta-squared η² = 0.06 represents the true effect size under the alternative hypothesis
scientific_notes: Eta-squared (η²) quantifies proportion of variance in the outcome explained by group membership
Relationship to non-centrality: η² relates to the ANOVA effect size through λ = n·k·η²/(1-η²), where n is per-group sample size and k is number of groups
F-distribution under alternative hypothesis is non-central with df1 = k-1 = 2, df2 = N-k, non-centrality parameter λ
This is a fixed-effects omnibus test at the 0.05 significance level; power calculation assumes effect size is specified under the alternative

answer.summary: For a balanced one-way fixed effects ANOVA with 3 independent groups, common variance, and population eta-squared η² = 0.06, the minimum integer sample size per group yielding at least 80% power at α = 0.05 for the omnibus F test is 52 participants per group. This achieves 80.56% power and requires a total of 156 participants (52 per group × 3 groups). The preceding design (n = 51) yields 79.73% power, confirming that 52 is the smallest admissible integer design meeting the 80% power target.
answer.method: one_way_anova – Power analysis via non-central F distribution using pwr::pwr.anova.test(). Eta-squared η² = 0.06 converted to Cohen's f = √(0.06/0.94) ≈ 0.2526. Sample size inverted to target power 0.80 at α = 0.05 with k = 3 groups, yielding continuous solution n ≈ 51.33 participants per group. Integer rounding ceiling(51.33) = 52 participants per group. Power verified at integer designs: n = 52 achieves 0.8056 power; n = 51 achieves 0.7973 power.
assumptions: Observations within each group are independent and identically normally distributed with a common population variance σ²
Fixed effects model: the 3 groups are of primary interest (not a random sample from a larger population of groups)
Population eta-squared η² = 0.06 represents the true effect size under the alternative hypothesis H₁
Balanced design: equal sample size per group
Omnibus F test: H₀: μ₁ = μ₂ = μ₃ vs. H₁: at least one mean differs
limitations: Sample size calculation assumes the population effect size η² = 0.06 is known and fixed; actual power depends on the true effect size
Calculation applies to the omnibus F test only; if follow-up pairwise comparisons are planned, additional multiplicity adjustment (e.g., Bonferroni) may reduce power
Non-centrality parameter and power assume normality and homogeneity of variance; sensitivity to violations is not assessed
Design is balanced; unequal group sizes would require recalculation

# Load required package
library(pwr)

# Define parameters
k <- 3                    # number of groups
eta_squared <- 0.06       # population eta-squared
alpha <- 0.05             # significance level
target_power <- 0.8       # target power

# Convert eta-squared to Cohen's f effect size
# Relationship: f = sqrt(eta_squared / (1 - eta_squared))
f_effect <- sqrt(eta_squared / (1 - eta_squared))

cat("Effect size parameters:\n")
cat("  Eta-squared (η²):", eta_squared, "\n")
cat("  Cohen's f:", f_effect, "\n\n")

# Calculate sample size per group using pwr.anova.test()
# This returns the per-group sample size for a balanced design
result <- pwr.anova.test(
  k = k,
  f = f_effect,
  sig.level = alpha,
  power = target_power
)

cat("Power analysis result:\n")
cat("  Number of groups (k):", result$k, "\n")
cat("  Cohen's f:", result$f, "\n")
cat("  Significance level (α):", result$sig.level, "\n")
cat("  Target power:", result$power, "\n")
cat("  Sample size per group (continuous):", result$n, "\n\n")

# Round up to nearest integer (standard practice)
n_integer <- ceiling(result$n)
cat("Minimum integer sample size per group:", n_integer, "\n\n")

# Verify power at the rounded sample size
verified_power <- pwr.anova.test(
  k = k,
  f = f_effect,
  sig.level = alpha,
  n = n_integer
)

cat("Verified power at n =", n_integer, "per group:", verified_power$power, "\n\n")

# Also check power at n-1 to confirm n_integer is the minimum
power_at_prev <- pwr.anova.test(
  k = k,
  f = f_effect,
  sig.level = alpha,
  n = n_integer - 1
)

cat("Power at n =", n_integer - 1, "per group:", power_at_prev$power, "\n\n")

# Calculate total sample size
N_total <- k * n_integer
cat("Total sample size (across all groups):", N_total, "\n")
cat("Degrees of freedom (between groups):", k - 1, "\n")
cat("Degrees of freedom (within groups):", N_total - k, "\n\n")

# Compute non-centrality parameter for verification
ncp <- sqrt(n_integer * k * f_effect^2)
cat("Non-centrality parameter (λ):", ncp, "\n")

# Critical F value
f_crit <- qf(1 - alpha, df1 = k - 1, df2 = N_total - k)
cat("Critical F value at α = 0.05:", f_crit, "\n")

# Return results
POWER_AGENT_RESULT <- list(
  results = list(
    list(metric = "sample_size", value = n_integer, unit = "participants_per_group"),
    list(metric = "achieved_power", value = round(verified_power$power, 4), unit = "probability"),
    list(metric = "power_at_preceding_design", value = round(power_at_prev$power, 4), unit = "probability"),
    list(metric = "total_sample_size", value = N_total, unit = "participants"),
    list(metric = "cohens_f", value = round(f_effect, 4), unit = "effect_size")
  )
)

cat("\n=== FINAL RESULTS ===\n")
cat("Minimum sample size per group (n):", n_integer, "participants_per_group\n")
cat("Achieved power at n =", n_integer, ":", round(verified_power$power, 4), "\n")

plan.estimand: omnibus F-statistic difference in population means across 3 independent groups
plan.hypothesis: H₀: μ₁ = μ₂ = μ₃ vs. H₁: at least one mean differs
assumptions: Observations within each group are independent and identically normally distributed
Homogeneity of variance: common population variance σ² across all groups
Fixed effects model: groups are of primary interest (not random sample from population of groups)
Population eta-squared η² = 0.06 represents the true effect size under the alternative hypothesis
scientific_notes: Eta-squared (η²) quantifies proportion of variance in the outcome explained by group membership
Relationship to non-centrality: η² relates to the ANOVA effect size through λ = n·k·η²/(1-η²), where n is per-group sample size and k is number of groups
F-distribution under alternative hypothesis is non-central with df1 = k-1 = 2, df2 = N-k, non-centrality parameter λ
This is a fixed-effects omnibus test at the 0.05 significance level; power calculation assumes effect size is specified under the alternative

# Load required package
library(pwr)

# Define parameters
k <- 3                    # number of groups
eta_squared <- 0.06       # population eta-squared
alpha <- 0.05             # significance level
target_power <- 0.8       # target power

# Convert eta-squared to Cohen's f effect size
# Relationship: f = sqrt(eta_squared / (1 - eta_squared))
f_effect <- sqrt(eta_squared / (1 - eta_squared))

cat("Effect size parameters:\n")
cat("  Eta-squared (η²):", eta_squared, "\n")
cat("  Cohen's f:", f_effect, "\n\n")

# Calculate sample size per group using pwr.anova.test()
# This returns the per-group sample size for a balanced design
result <- pwr.anova.test(
  k = k,
  f = f_effect,
  sig.level = alpha,
  power = target_power
)

cat("Power analysis result:\n")
cat("  Number of groups (k):", result$k, "\n")
cat("  Cohen's f:", result$f, "\n")
cat("  Significance level (α):", result$sig.level, "\n")
cat("  Target power:", result$power, "\n")
cat("  Sample size per group (continuous):", result$n, "\n\n")

# Round up to nearest integer (standard practice)
n_integer <- ceiling(result$n)
cat("Minimum integer sample size per group:", n_integer, "\n\n")

# Verify power at the rounded sample size
verified_power <- pwr.anova.test(
  k = k,
  f = f_effect,
  sig.level = alpha,
  n = n_integer
)

cat("Verified power at n =", n_integer, "per group:", verified_power$power, "\n\n")

# Also check power at n-1 to confirm n_integer is the minimum
power_at_prev <- pwr.anova.test(
  k = k,
  f = f_effect,
  sig.level = alpha,
  n = n_integer - 1
)

cat("Power at n =", n_integer - 1, "per group:", power_at_prev$power, "\n\n")

# Calculate total sample size
N_total <- k * n_integer
cat("Total sample size (across all groups):", N_total, "\n")
cat("Degrees of freedom (between groups):", k - 1, "\n")
cat("Degrees of freedom (within groups):", N_total - k, "\n\n")

# Compute non-centrality parameter for verification
ncp <- sqrt(n_integer * k * f_effect^2)
cat("Non-centrality parameter (λ):", ncp, "\n")

# Critical F value
f_crit <- qf(1 - alpha, df1 = k - 1, df2 = N_total - k)
cat("Critical F value at α = 0.05:", f_crit, "\n")

# Return results
POWER_AGENT_RESULT <- list(
  results = list(
    list(metric = "sample_size", value = n_integer, unit = "participants_per_group"),
    list(metric = "achieved_power", value = round(verified_power$power, 4), unit = "probability"),
    list(metric = "power_at_preceding_design", value = round(power_at_prev$power, 4), unit = "probability"),
    list(metric = "total_sample_size", value = N_total, unit = "participants"),
    list(metric = "cohens_f", value = round(f_effect, 4), unit = "effect_size")
  )
)

cat("\n=== FINAL RESULTS ===\n")
cat("Minimum sample size per group (n):", n_integer, "participants_per_group\n")
cat("Achieved power at n =", n_integer, ":", round(verified_power$power, 4), "\n")
cat("Power at n =", n_integer - 1, ":", round(power_at_prev$power, 4), "\n")

jsonlite::toJSON(POWER_AGENT_RESULT, auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15)

plan.estimand: difference in means between two independent normal populations
plan.hypothesis: true mean difference = 4.3 dBA (treatment group mean minus control group mean)
assumptions: Both groups follow independent normal distributions
Equal variances across groups (homogeneity of variance)
No attrition or missing data

# Power calculation for two-sample pooled t-test
# Comparing two independent normal means with equal variances

# Study parameters
n_per_group <- 32
mean_diff <- 4.3  # expected difference (dBA)
common_sd <- 7.8  # common standard deviation (dBA)
alpha <- 0.05
sidedness <- "one-sided"

# Calculate standard error
# SE = sqrt(SD^2 * (1/n1 + 1/n2)) = SD * sqrt(2/n) for equal-sized groups
se <- common_sd * sqrt(2 / n_per_group)

# Calculate noncentrality parameter
# λ = mean_diff / SE
noncentrality <- mean_diff / se

# Degrees of freedom
df <- n_per_group + n_per_group - 2

# For one-sided test at alpha 0.05, find critical t-value
# H0: μ1 - μ2 = 0 vs H1: μ1 - μ2 > 0 (one-sided, upper tail)
critical_t <- qt(1 - alpha, df)

# Power = P(t > critical_t | H1 is true)
# = 1 - P(t ≤ critical_t | λ)
# Using non-central t-distribution
power <- 1 - pt(critical_t, df = df, ncp = noncentrality)

# Summary of calculations
cat("Two-Sample Pooled t-Test: Power Calculation\n")
cat("===========================================\n")
cat("Study Design:\n")
cat(sprintf("  Sample size per group: %d participants\n", n_per_group))
cat(sprintf("  Total sample size: %d participants\n", 2 * n_per_group))
cat(sprintf("  Expected mean difference: %.1f dBA\n", mean_diff))
cat(sprintf("  Common standard deviation: %.1f dBA\n", common_sd))
cat(sprintf("  Significance level (α): %.4f\n", alpha))
cat(sprintf("  Test: One-sided (H1: μ1 > μ2)\n\n"))

cat("Statistical Calculations:\n")
cat(sprintf("  Standard error (SE): %.6f dBA\n", se))
cat(sprintf("  Noncentrality parameter (λ): %.6f\n", noncentrality))
cat(sprintf("  Degrees of freedom: %d\n", df))
cat(sprintf("  Critical t-value: %.6f\n", critical_t))
cat(sprintf("  Power: %.6f\n", power))

# Output for structured reporting
results <- data.frame(
  metric = "power",
  value = power,
  unit = "probability"
)

cat("\n\nStructured Result:\n")
print(results)

# Emit the result for POWER_AGENT_RESULT
POWER_AGENT_RESULT <- jsonlite::toJSON(
  list(results = results),
  auto_unbox = TRUE,
  digits = 15
)
cat("\nPOWER_AGENT_RESULT=", POWER_AGENT_RESULT, "\n")

# Power calculation for two-sample pooled t-test
# Comparing two independent normal means with equal variances

# Study parameters
n_per_group <- 32
mean_diff <- 4.3  # expected difference (dBA)
common_sd <- 7.8  # common standard deviation (dBA)
alpha <- 0.05
sidedness <- "one-sided"

# Calculate standard error
# SE = sqrt(SD^2 * (1/n1 + 1/n2)) = SD * sqrt(2/n) for equal-sized groups
se <- common_sd * sqrt(2 / n_per_group)

# Calculate noncentrality parameter
# λ = mean_diff / SE
noncentrality <- mean_diff / se

# Degrees of freedom
df <- n_per_group + n_per_group - 2

# For one-sided test at alpha 0.05, find critical t-value
# H0: μ1 - μ2 = 0 vs H1: μ1 - μ2 > 0 (one-sided, upper tail)
critical_t <- qt(1 - alpha, df)

# Power = P(t > critical_t | H1 is true)
# = 1 - P(t ≤ critical_t | λ)
# Using non-central t-distribution
power <- 1 - pt(critical_t, df = df, ncp = noncentrality)

# Summary of calculations
cat("Two-Sample Pooled t-Test: Power Calculation\n")
cat("===========================================\n")
cat("Study Design:\n")
cat(sprintf("  Sample size per group: %d participants\n", n_per_group))
cat(sprintf("  Total sample size: %d participants\n", 2 * n_per_group))
cat(sprintf("  Expected mean difference: %.1f dBA\n", mean_diff))
cat(sprintf("  Common standard deviation: %.1f dBA\n", common_sd))
cat(sprintf("  Significance level (α): %.4f\n", alpha))
cat(sprintf("  Test: One-sided (H1: μ1 > μ2)\n\n"))

cat("Statistical Calculations:\n")
cat(sprintf("  Standard error (SE): %.6f dBA\n", se))
cat(sprintf("  Noncentrality parameter (λ): %.6f\n", noncentrality))
cat(sprintf("  Degrees of freedom: %d\n", df))
cat(sprintf("  Critical t-value: %.6f\n", critical_t))
cat(sprintf("  Power: %.6f\n", power))

# Output for structured reporting
results <- data.frame(
  metric = "power",
  value = power,
  unit = "probability"
)

cat("\n\nStructured Result:\n")
print(results)

# Emit the result for POWER_AGENT_RESULT
POWER_AGENT_RESULT <- jsonlite::toJSON(
  list(results = results),
  auto_unbox = TRUE,
  digits = 15
)
cat("\nPOWER_AGENT_RESULT=", POWER_AGENT_RESULT, "\n")

lambda <- mean_diff / se_computed

cat("================================\n")

# Evidence e1; success=true

# Power calculation for two-sample pooled t-test
# Comparing two independent normal means with equal variances

# Study parameters
n_per_group <- 32
mean_diff <- 4.3  # expected difference (dBA)
common_sd <- 7.8  # common standard deviation (dBA)
alpha <- 0.05
sidedness <- "one-sided"

# Calculate standard error
# SE = sqrt(SD^2 * (1/n1 + 1/n2)) = SD * sqrt(2/n) for equal-sized groups
se <- common_sd * sqrt(2 / n_per_group)

# Calculate noncentrality parameter
# λ = mean_diff / SE
noncentrality <- mean_diff / se

# Degrees of freedom
df <- n_per_group + n_per_group - 2

# For one-sided test at alpha 0.05, find critical t-value
# H0: μ1 - μ2 = 0 vs H1: μ1 - μ2 > 0 (one-sided, upper tail)
critical_t <- qt(1 - alpha, df)

# Power = P(t > critical_t | H1 is true)
# = 1 - P(t ≤ critical_t | λ)
# Using non-central t-distribution
power <- 1 - pt(critical_t, df = df, ncp = noncentrality)

# Summary of calculations
cat("Two-Sample Pooled t-Test: Power Calculation\n")
cat("===========================================\n")
cat("Study Design:\n")
cat(sprintf("  Sample size per group: %d participants\n", n_per_group))
cat(sprintf("  Total sample size: %d participants\n", 2 * n_per_group))
cat(sprintf("  Expected mean difference: %.1f dBA\n", mean_diff))
cat(sprintf("  Common standard deviation: %.1f dBA\n", common_sd))
cat(sprintf("  Significance level (α): %.4f\n", alpha))
cat(sprintf("  Test: One-sided (H1: μ1 > μ2)\n\n"))

cat("Statistical Calculations:\n")
cat(sprintf("  Standard error (SE): %.6f dBA\n", se))
cat(sprintf("  Noncentrality parameter (λ): %.6f\n", noncentrality))
cat(sprintf("  Degrees of freedom: %d\n", df))
cat(sprintf("  Critical t-value: %.6f\n", critical_t))
cat(sprintf("  Power: %.6f\n", power))

# Output for structured reporting
results <- data.frame(
  metric = "power",
  value = power,
  unit = "probability"
)

)

# Sample size calculation for proportion confidence interval
# Using normal approximation with exact standard normal quantile

# Parameters
p <- 0.70  # target proportion
z_alpha_2 <- 1.959964  # exact standard normal 97.5th percentile (two-sided alpha=0.05)
ME <- 0.03  # margin of error (half-width)

# Formula: n = z^2 * p(1-p) / ME^2
n_continuous <- (z_alpha_2^2 * p * (1 - p)) / (ME^2)

# Round upward to nearest integer
n_rounded <- ceiling(n_continuous)

cat("Proportion confidence interval sample size calculation\n")
cat("=====================================================\n")
cat(sprintf("Target proportion (p): %.2f\n", p))
cat(sprintf("Standard normal 97.5th percentile (z): %.6f\n", z_alpha_2))
cat(sprintf("Margin of error / half-width (ME): %.2f\n", ME))
cat(sprintf("\nFormula: n = z² × p(1-p) / ME²\n"))
cat(sprintf("Continuous solution: n = (%.6f)² × %.2f × %.2f / (%.2f)²\n", 
            z_alpha_2, p, 1-p, ME))
cat(sprintf("Continuous solution: n = %.4f\n", n_continuous))
cat(sprintf("\nRounded upward: n = %d participants\n", n_rounded))

# Verify: check the actual half-width achieved with n_rounded
half_width_achieved <- z_alpha_2 * sqrt(p * (1 - p) / n_rounded)
cat(sprintf("\nVerification:\n")
cat(sprintf("Half-width achieved with n=%d: %.6f\n", n_rounded, half_width_achieved))
cat(sprintf("Meets requirement (≤ %.2f)? %s\n", ME, 
            if (half_width_achieved <= ME) "YES" else "NO"))

# Store results for output
results <- data.frame(
  metric = "sample_size",
  value = n_rounded,
  unit = "participants_total"
)

# Output JSON for POWER_AGENT_RESULT
library(jsonlite)
output_list <- list(
  results = list(
    list(metric = "sample_size", value = n_rounded, unit = "participants_total")
  )
)

cat("\n")
cat(toJSON(output_list, auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15))

# Sample size calculation for proportion confidence interval
# Using normal approximation with exact standard normal quantile

# Parameters
p <- 0.70  # target proportion
z_alpha_2 <- 1.959964  # exact standard normal 97.5th percentile (two-sided alpha=0.05)
ME <- 0.03  # margin of error (half-width)

# Formula: n = z^2 * p(1-p) / ME^2
n_continuous <- (z_alpha_2^2 * p * (1 - p)) / (ME^2)

# Round upward to nearest integer
n_rounded <- ceiling(n_continuous)

cat("Proportion confidence interval sample size calculation\n")
cat("=====================================================\n")
cat(sprintf("Target proportion (p): %.2f\n", p))
cat(sprintf("Standard normal 97.5th percentile (z): %.6f\n", z_alpha_2))
cat(sprintf("Margin of error / half-width (ME): %.2f\n", ME))
cat(sprintf("\nFormula: n = z² × p(1-p) / ME²\n"))
cat(sprintf("Continuous solution: n = (%.6f)² × %.2f × %.2f / (%.2f)²\n", 
            z_alpha_2, p, 1-p, ME))
cat(sprintf("Continuous solution: n = %.4f\n", n_continuous))
cat(sprintf("\nRounded upward: n = %d participants\n", n_rounded))

# Verify: check the actual half-width achieved with n_rounded
half_width_achieved <- z_alpha_2 * sqrt(p * (1 - p) / n_rounded)
cat(sprintf("\nVerification:\n")
cat(sprintf("Half-width achieved with n=%d: %.6f\n", n_rounded, half_width_achieved))
cat(sprintf("Meets requirement (≤ %.2f)? %s\n", ME, 
            if (half_width_achieved <= ME) "YES" else "NO"))

# Store results for output
results <- data.frame(
  metric = "sample_size",
  value = n_rounded,
  unit = "participants_total"
)

# Output JSON for POWER_AGENT_RESULT
library(jsonlite)
output_list <- list(
  results = list(
    list(metric = "sample_size", value = n_rounded, unit = "participants_total")
  )
)

cat("\n")
cat(toJSON(output_list, auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15))

Power = P(T > 1.7109 | H₁) = 1 − Pr(T ≤ 1.7109; df=24, ncp=2.0) = 0.6173. Calculated and verified using pwr::pwr.t.test.

# One-sample t-test power calculation
# H0: mu <= 0 vs H1: mu > 0 (one-sided, right-tailed)
# H0: mu = 0 under null
# HA: mu = 0.2 under alternative

n <- 25
alpha <- 0.05
mean_diff <- 0.2
sd <- 0.5
df <- n - 1

# Effect size (Cohen's d)
cohens_d <- mean_diff / sd
cat("Cohen's d =", cohens_d, "\n")

# Non-centrality parameter
ncp <- cohens_d * sqrt(n)
cat("Non-centrality parameter =", ncp, "\n")

# Critical value for one-sided test
# For one-sided, we use the upper quantile at alpha level
t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha, df)
cat("Critical t-value (one-sided, alpha=0.05, df=24) =", t_crit, "\n")

# Power = P(T > t_crit | H1 true)
# When H1 is true, the test statistic follows non-central t distribution
# with ncp = 2.0 and df = 24
power <- 1 - pt(t_crit, df, ncp = ncp)

cat("\nPower calculation:\n")
cat("Power = P(T >", t_crit, "| H1 true)\n")
cat("Power =", power, "\n")

# Verification using power.t.test (which uses same approach for one-sample)
library_check <- requireNamespace("stats", quietly = TRUE)
ptt <- power.t.test(n = n, delta = mean_diff, sd = sd, 
                     sig.level = alpha, type = "one.sample",
                     alternative = "one.sided")
cat("\nVerification with power.t.test:\n")
cat("Power =", ptt$power, "\n")

# Final result
cat("\n=== RESULT ===\n")
cat("Power (probability) =", power, "\n")

# Output in required format
result <- list(
  metric = "power",
  value = power,
  unit = "probability"
)
cat("\nPOWER_AGENT_RESULT=", jsonlite::toJSON(list(results = list(result)), auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15), "\n", sep = "")

# One-sample t-test power calculation
# H0: mu <= 0 vs H1: mu > 0 (one-sided, right-tailed)
# H0: mu = 0 under null
# HA: mu = 0.2 under alternative

n <- 25
alpha <- 0.05
mean_diff <- 0.2
sd <- 0.5
df <- n - 1

# Effect size (Cohen's d)
cohens_d <- mean_diff / sd
cat("Cohen's d =", cohens_d, "\n")

# Non-centrality parameter
ncp <- cohens_d * sqrt(n)
cat("Non-centrality parameter =", ncp, "\n")

# Critical value for one-sided test
# For one-sided, we use the upper quantile at alpha level
t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha, df)
cat("Critical t-value (one-sided, alpha=0.05, df=24) =", t_crit, "\n")

# When H1 is true, the test statistic follows non-central t distribution
# with ncp = 2.0 and df = 24

plan.estimand: Mean difference between groups on participant-level averages: constant difference of 0.45
plan.hypothesis: Two-group comparison of mean participant averages, testing H0: μ_treatment = μ_control vs. H1: μ_treatment ≠ μ_control
assumptions: Random-intercept model: two groups with fixed group mean difference and random intercepts (random effect variance implies ICC)
Marginal variance structure: within-group SD = 1 applies to individual observations
Intraclass correlation ρ = 0.4 across n = 4 observations per participant
Analysis performed on participant-level averages (summary scores)
Averages are approximately normal; t-test with pooled variance is appropriate
Constant group difference (no group × time interaction); identical ICC in both groups
Equal allocation (1:1 ratio) and zero missing data
scientific_notes: The study collects repeated measurements within participants but analyzes participant-level summaries (averages), reducing the design to a two-sample t-test on aggregated data.
With n observations per participant and ICC = ρ, the variance of a participant average Y_avg = (1/n)ΣY_ij is: Var(Y_avg) = σ²[1 + (n−1)ρ]/n where σ² = 1 is the marginal observation-level variance.
The effective effect size for the two-sample t-test is Δ/SD_avg = 0.45/√0.4 ≈ 0.711, a medium effect.
Power calculation uses two-sample t-test (equal variance, df = 2N−2) with this reduced SD.

answer.summary: For a two-group random-intercept Gaussian study with 4 observations per participant, marginal SD = 1, ICC = 0.4, mean group difference = 0.45, equal allocation, and two-sided pooled t-test at α = 0.05, the minimum integer sample size to achieve 90% power is **20 participants per group** (40 total participants, 160 total observations). This design achieves 92.85% power; the preceding design with n = 19 per group achieves 88.89% power.
answer.method: Two-sample t-test on participant-level averages with noncentrality parameter inversion. Under the random-intercept model, the variance of a participant average is Var(Ȳ) = σ²[1 + (n−1)ρ]/n = 1·[1 + 3·0.4]/4 = 0.55, yielding SD(Ȳ) ≈ 0.7416. The group difference (0.45) on the average scale produces Cohen's d ≈ 0.6068. Power is computed using the noncentral t-distribution with df = 2n − 2 and noncentrality parameter ncp = d·√(n/2). The minimum integer sample size equals ceiling(19.278) = 20 per group.
assumptions: Random-intercept model with fixed group mean difference (0.45) and random intercepts that induce ICC = 0.4 across 4 observations per participant
Marginal variance (observation level) is σ² = 1
Participant-level averages are approximately normally distributed; two-sample pooled t-test with equal variances is appropriate
No group-by-time interaction; constant treatment effect across observations
Complete data with zero missing; no attrition
Equal allocation (1:1 ratio) between groups
Analysis uses participant average as the comparison unit, reducing the design to a standard two-sample problem
limitations: Calculation assumes the random-intercept model holds exactly. Real data may violate normality of averages, especially with small numbers of observations per participant
Power is conditional on the specified ICC and marginal SD; variation in either parameter changes the sample size requirement
No inflation for interim analyses, dropout, or protocol modifications
The pooled t-test assumes equal variances; Welch correction would produce slightly different power
Rounding to ceiling(19.278) = 20 follows the standard integer convention; custom rounding rules were not specified

target_power <- 0.9  # target power

# For random-intercept model with ICC:
# Var(Y_ij) = σ² (marginal)
# Var(Y_bar_i) = σ²[1 + (n-1)ρ]/n where ρ is ICC
var_avg <- marginal_sd^2 * (1 + (n_obs - 1) * icc) / n_obs
sd_avg <- sqrt(var_avg)

cat(sprintf("Marginal SD (observation level): %.4f\n", marginal_sd))
cat(sprintf("Intraclass correlation: %.4f\n", icc))
cat(sprintf("Observations per participant: %d\n", n_obs))
cat(sprintf("Variance of average: %.4f\n", var_avg))
cat(sprintf("SD of average: %.6f\n", sd_avg))

# Standardized effect size (Cohen's d on participant averages)
cohens_d <- mean_diff / sd_avg
cat(sprintf("\n=== Effect Size ===\n"))
cat(sprintf("Unstandardized group difference: %.2f\n", mean_diff))
cat(sprintf("Cohen's d (on averages): %.6f\n", cohens_d))

# For two-sample t-test, we need n per group such that:
# power = P(|t| > t_{α/2, 2n-2}) where t ~ t_{2n-2}(ncp)
# and noncentrality parameter ncp = d * sqrt(n/2)

# We'll use the ncp approach with qt and pt to find minimum n
source_vals <- list(
  n_obs = n_obs,
  marginal_sd = marginal_sd,
  icc = icc,
  mean_diff = mean_diff,
  alpha = alpha,
  target_power = target_power,
  var_avg = var_avg,
  sd_avg = sd_avg,
  cohens_d = cohens_d
)

# Binary search for minimum sample size per group
power_at_n <- function(n_per_group, d, alpha = 0.05) {
  # For two-sided t-test with equal allocation (n per group, total 2n)
  df <- 2 * n_per_group - 2
  ncp <- d * sqrt(n_per_group / 2)  # noncentrality
  t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha / 2, df)
  
  # Power = P(T > t_crit) + P(T < -t_crit) with noncentral t
  power <- 2 * (1 - pt(t_crit, df, ncp = ncp))
  return(power)
}

cat("\n=== Power Search (Continuous then Integer) ===\n")

# Try a grid to find approximate region
grid <- seq(10, 150, by = 1)
powers_grid <- sapply(grid, function(n) power_at_n(n, cohens_d, alpha))

idx_exceed <- min(which(powers_grid >= target_power))
approx_n <- grid[idx_exceed]

cat(sprintf("Power at n=%d: %.6f\n", approx_n, powers_grid[idx_exceed]))

# Refine with binary search for exact continuous solution
left <- 1
right <- 200

for (iter in 1:50) {
  mid <- (left + right) / 2
  p_mid <- power_at_n(mid, cohens_d, alpha)
  if (p_mid < target_power) {
    left <- mid
  } else {
    right <- mid
  }
}

n_continuous <- (left + right) / 2
power_continuous <- power_at_n(n_continuous, cohens_d, alpha)

cat(sprintf("\nContinuous solution: n = %.3f participants per group\n", n_continuous))
cat(sprintf("Power at continuous n: %.6f\n", power_continuous))

power_integer <- power_at_n(n_integer, cohens_d, alpha)

    ),

    )

)

# Linear regression sample size calculation for test of overall model significance
# H0: ρ² = 0 vs H1: ρ² ≠ 0
# Test: F = [R²/k] / [(1-R²)/(n-k-1)]
# Noncentrality parameter: λ = R²(n-k-1) / (1-R²)

library(stats)

# Parameters
r_squared <- 0.30          # Population R-squared (anticipated multiple correlation)
k <- 3                      # Number of predictors
alpha <- 0.05              # Significance level (two-sided)
target_power <- 0.90       # Target power

# Critical value for two-sided test at alpha = 0.05
# For overall F test: df1 = k, df2 = n - k - 1
# Critical value depends on n, so we'll iterate

# Function to calculate power for a given sample size n
calculate_power_linear <- function(n, r_sq, k, alpha) {
  if (n <= k) return(0)  # Invalid design
  
  df1 <- k                    # numerator df
  df2 <- n - k - 1            # denominator df
  
  # Critical value for two-sided test
  f_crit <- qf(1 - alpha/2, df1, df2)
  
  # Noncentrality parameter
  lambda <- r_sq * (n - k - 1) / (1 - r_sq)
  
  # Power = P(F > f_crit | lambda)
  power <- 1 - pf(f_crit, df1, df2, ncp = lambda)
  
  return(power)
}

# Search for minimum sample size giving power >= 0.90
# Start with a reasonable range
n_search <- seq(10, 200, by = 1)
powers <- sapply(n_search, function(n) calculate_power_linear(n, r_squared, k, alpha))

# Find minimum n where power >= target
idx_sufficient <- which(powers >= target_power)

if (length(idx_sufficient) > 0) {
  n_min <- n_search[idx_sufficient[1]]
  power_achieved <- powers[idx_sufficient[1]]
  
  # Also report power at the preceding sample size
  if (n_min > 10) {
    n_preceding <- n_min - 1
    power_preceding <- calculate_power_linear(n_preceding, r_squared, k, alpha)
  } else {
    n_preceding <- NA
    power_preceding <- NA
  }
} else {
  n_min <- NA
  power_achieved <- NA
  n_preceding <- NA
  power_preceding <- NA
}

# Detailed calculation for minimum sample size
cat("=== Linear Regression Power Analysis ===\n")
cat("Hypothesis: H₀: ρ² = 0 vs. H₁: ρ² ≠ 0\n")
cat("Test: Noncentral F distribution\n")
cat("Alpha (two-sided):", alpha, "\n")
cat("Number of predictors (k):", k, "\n")
cat("Anticipated R-squared:", r_squared, "\n")
cat("Target power:", target_power, "\n\n")

cat("Results:\n")
cat("Minimum total sample size:", n_min, "participants\n")
cat("Achieved power at n =", n_min, ":", sprintf("%.6f", power_achieved), "\n")
if (!is.na(n_preceding)) {
  cat("Power at n =", n_preceding, ":", sprintf("%.6f", power_preceding), "\n")
}

# Verify the calculation step-by-step for n_min
if (!is.na(n_min)) {
  cat("\n=== Verification for n =", n_min, "===\n")
  df1 <- k
  df2 <- n_min - k - 1
  f_crit <- qf(1 - alpha/2, df1, df2)
  lambda <- r_squared * (n_min - k - 1) / (1 - r_squared)
  power_check <- 1 - pf(f_crit, df1, df2, ncp = lambda)
  
  cat("Numerator df (df1):", df1, "\n")
  cat("Denominator df (df2):", df2, "\n")
  cat("Critical F-value:", sprintf("%.6f", f_crit), "\n")
  cat("Noncentrality parameter (λ):", sprintf("%.6f", lambda), "\n")
  cat("Power (verification):", sprintf("%.6f", power_check), "\n")
}

# Return final results
result <- list(
  sample_size = n_min,
  power_achieved = power_achieved,
  sample_size_preceding = n_preceding,
  power_preceding = power_preceding
)

cat("\n")
cat(jsonlite::toJSON(list(results = list(
  list(metric = "sample_size", value = n_min, unit = "participants_total"),
  list(metric = "power_achieved", value = round(power_achieved, 6), unit = "probability"),
  list(metric = "sample_size_preceding", value = if(is.na(n_preceding)) NULL else n_preceding, unit = "participants_total"),
  list(metric = "power_preceding", value = if(is.na(power_preceding)) NULL else round(power_preceding, 6), unit = "probability")
)), auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15))

cat("Under H₀: ρ² = 0, power should equal α = ", alpha, "\n\n")

df1 <- k
df2 <- n - k - 1

# Critical value
f_crit <- qf(1 - alpha/2, df1, df2)

# Under null (λ = 0)
power_null <- 1 - pf(f_crit, df1, df2, ncp = 0)

# The effect size in terms of f (Cohen's f) relates to ρ² as:
# f = sqrt(ρ² / (1 - ρ²))
# And λ = f² * (n - k - 1) = [ρ² / (1 - ρ²)] * (n - k - 1)

cohen_f <- sqrt(r_squared / (1 - r_squared))

# The critical value qf(1 - α/2, df1, df2) with α/2 = 0.025 gives the UPPER critical value
# for a TWO-SIDED test on R² (rejecting both ρ² = 0 and ρ² = 1 scenarios, though the latter is unnatural)

# However, for a test of overall model significance, we only care about detecting
# ρ² > 0, so it's essentially ONE-TAILED (upper tail).
# The "two-sided" language may refer to the fact that we test whether ρ² differs from 0.

# Let's clarify: for Type I error calibration under H₀: ρ² = 0
# Under null with λ = 0, F ~ F(k, n-k-1)
# We reject if F > f_crit, where f_crit is the upper α quantile
# So P(F > f_crit | H₀) should equal α, not α/2

alpha <- 0.05
n <- 47

df2 <- n - k - 1

# Linear regression sample size calculation for test of overall model significance
# H0: ρ² = 0 vs H1: ρ² ≠ 0
# Test: F = [R²/k] / [(1-R²)/(n-k-1)]
# Noncentrality parameter: λ = R²(n-k-1) / (1-R²)

library(stats)

# Parameters
r_squared <- 0.30          # Population R-squared (anticipated multiple correlation)
k <- 3                      # Number of predictors
alpha <- 0.05              # Significance level (two-sided)
target_power <- 0.90       # Target power

# Critical value for two-sided test at alpha = 0.05
# For overall F test: df1 = k, df2 = n - k - 1
# Critical value depends on n, so we'll iterate

# Function to calculate power for a given sample size n
calculate_power_linear <- function(n, r_sq, k, alpha) {
  if (n <= k) return(0)  # Invalid design
  
  df1 <- k                    # numerator df
  df2 <- n - k - 1            # denominator df
  
  # Critical value for two-sided test
  f_crit <- qf(1 - alpha/2, df1, df2)
  
  # Noncentrality parameter
  lambda <- r_sq * (n - k - 1) / (1 - r_sq)
  
  # Power = P(F > f_crit | lambda)
  power <- 1 - pf(f_crit, df1, df2, ncp = lambda)
  
  return(power)
}

# Search for minimum sample size giving power >= 0.90
# Start with a reasonable range
n_search <- seq(10, 200, by = 1)
powers <- sapply(n_search, function(n) calculate_power_linear(n, r_squared, k, alpha))

# Find minimum n where power >= target
idx_sufficient <- which(powers >= target_power)

if (length(idx_sufficient) > 0) {
  n_min <- n_search[idx_sufficient[1]]
  power_achieved <- powers[idx_sufficient[1]]
  
  # Also report power at the preceding sample size
  if (n_min > 10) {
    n_preceding <- n_min - 1
    power_preceding <- calculate_power_linear(n_preceding, r_squared, k, alpha)
  } else {
    n_preceding <- NA
    power_preceding <- NA
  }
} else {
  n_min <- NA
  power_achieved <- NA
  n_preceding <- NA
  power_preceding <- NA
}

# Detailed calculation for minimum sample size
cat("=== Linear Regression Power Analysis ===\n")
cat("Hypothesis: H₀: ρ² = 0 vs. H₁: ρ² ≠ 0\n")
cat("Test: Noncentral F distribution\n")
cat("Alpha (two-sided):", alpha, "\n")
cat("Number of predictors (k):", k, "\n")
cat("Anticipated R-squared:", r_squared, "\n")
cat("Target power:", target_power, "\n\n")

cat("Results:\n")
cat("Minimum total sample size:", n_min, "participants\n")
cat("Achieved power at n =", n_min, ":", sprintf("%.6f", power_achieved), "\n")
if (!is.na(n_preceding)) {
  cat("Power at n =", n_preceding, ":", sprintf("%.6f", power_preceding), "\n")
}

# Verify the calculation step-by-step for n_min
if (!is.na(n_min)) {
  cat("\n=== Verification for n =", n_min, "===\n")
  df1 <- k
  df2 <- n_min - k - 1
  f_crit <- qf(1 - alpha/2, df1, df2)
  lambda <- r_squared * (n_min - k - 1) / (1 - r_squared)
  power_check <- 1 - pf(f_crit, df1, df2, ncp = lambda)
  
  cat("Numerator df (df1):", df1, "\n")
  cat("Denominator df (df2):", df2, "\n")
  cat("Critical F-value:", sprintf("%.6f", f_crit), "\n")
  cat("Noncentrality parameter (λ):", sprintf("%.6f", lambda), "\n")
  cat("Power (verification):", sprintf("%.6f", power_check), "\n")
}

# Return final results
result <- list(
  sample_size = n_min,
  power_achieved = power_achieved,
  sample_size_preceding = n_preceding,
  power_preceding = power_preceding
)

cat("\n")
cat(jsonlite::toJSON(list(results = list(
  list(metric = "sample_size", value = n_min, unit = "participants_total"),
  list(metric = "power_achieved", value = round(power_achieved, 6), unit = "probability"),
  list(metric = "sample_size_preceding", value = if(is.na(n_preceding)) NULL else n_preceding, unit = "participants_total"),
  list(metric = "power_preceding", value = if(is.na(power_preceding)) NULL else round(power_preceding, 6), unit = "probability")
)), auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15))

# Additional validation: check formula correctness and null-case calibration
library(stats)

# Parameters
r_squared <- 0.30
k <- 3
alpha <- 0.05
n <- 47

# The test statistic under the null hypothesis H₀: ρ² = 0 should have F(k, n-k-1) distribution
# Let's verify null-case calibration: with ρ² = 0, power should be α

cat("=== NULL CASE CALIBRATION CHECK ===\n")
cat("Under H₀: ρ² = 0, power should equal α = ", alpha, "\n\n")

df1 <- k
df2 <- n - k - 1

# Critical value
f_crit <- qf(1 - alpha/2, df1, df2)

# Under null (λ = 0)
power_null <- 1 - pf(f_crit, df1, df2, ncp = 0)

cat("F-critical (", 1-alpha/2, " quantile) =", f_crit, "\n")
cat("Power under H₀ (λ = 0) = P(F > f_crit) =", power_null, "\n")
cat("Expected:", alpha, "\n")
cat("Match? ", abs(power_null - alpha) < 1e-6, "\n\n")

# Alternative formula check: verify noncentrality parameter calculation
# The effect size in terms of f (Cohen's f) relates to ρ² as:
# f = sqrt(ρ² / (1 - ρ²))
# And λ = f² * (n - k - 1) = [ρ² / (1 - ρ²)] * (n - k - 1)

cohen_f <- sqrt(r_squared / (1 - r_squared))
lambda_from_f <- cohen_f^2 * df2

lambda_direct <- r_squared * df2 / (1 - r_squared)

cat("=== NONCENTRALITY PARAMETER VERIFICATION ===\n")
cat("Cohen's f = sqrt(ρ²/(1-ρ²)) = sqrt(", r_squared, "/", 1-r_squared, ") =", cohen_f, "\n")
cat("λ from f: f² × df2 = ", cohen_f^2, "×", df2, "=", lambda_from_f, "\n")
cat("λ direct: ρ² × df2 / (1-ρ²) =", r_squared, "×", df2, "/", 1-r_squared, "=", lambda_direct, "\n")

# CLARIFICATION: The "power under null" calculation I just did was incorrect.
# The test statistic for the F test is:
# F = [R² / k] / [(1 - R²) / (n - k - 1)]
# This is a ONE-TAILED test in the standard sense: we reject H₀ if F > f_crit (upper tail)
# The critical value qf(1 - α/2, df1, df2) with α/2 = 0.025 gives the UPPER critical value
# for a TWO-SIDED test on R² (rejecting both ρ² = 0 and ρ² = 1 scenarios, though the latter is unnatural)

# However, for a test of overall model significance, we only care about detecting
# ρ² > 0, so it's essentially ONE-TAILED (upper tail).
# The "two-sided" language may refer to the fact that we test whether ρ² differs from 0.

# Let's clarify: for Type I error calibration under H₀: ρ² = 0
# Under null with λ = 0, F ~ F(k, n-k-1)
# We reject if F > f_crit, where f_crit is the upper α quantile
# So P(F > f_crit | H₀) should equal α, not α/2

library(stats)

k <- 3
alpha <- 0.05
n <- 47

df1 <- k
df2 <- n - k - 1

# For UPPER-TAIL test (one-sided):
f_crit_upper <- qf(1 - alpha, df1, df2)  # α quantile (upper tail)

# Evidence e1; success=true

# Linear regression sample size calculation for test of overall model significance
# H0: ρ² = 0 vs H1: ρ² ≠ 0
# Test: F = [R²/k] / [(1-R²)/(n-k-1)]
# Noncentrality parameter: λ = R²(n-k-1) / (1-R²)

library(stats)

# Parameters
r_squared <- 0.30          # Population R-squared (anticipated multiple correlation)
k <- 3                      # Number of predictors
alpha <- 0.05              # Significance level (two-sided)
target_power <- 0.90       # Target power

# Critical value for two-sided test at alpha = 0.05
# For overall F test: df1 = k, df2 = n - k - 1
# Critical value depends on n, so we'll iterate

# Function to calculate power for a given sample size n
calculate_power_linear <- function(n, r_sq, k, alpha) {
  if (n <= k) return(0)  # Invalid design
  
  df1 <- k                    # numerator df
  df2 <- n - k - 1            # denominator df
  
  # Critical value for two-sided test
  f_crit <- qf(1 - alpha/2, df1, df2)
  
  # Noncentrality parameter
  lambda <- r_sq * (n - k - 1) / (1 - r_sq)
  
  # Power = P(F > f_crit | lambda)
  power <- 1 - pf(f_crit, df1, df2, ncp = lambda)
  
  return(power)
}

Standard statistical interpretation:

2. Since R² ≥ 0 by definition, 'differs from zero' means ρ² > 0 (one-sided in practice)
3. The F test is inherently UPPER-TAILED: reject H₀ if F > f_crit
4. Type I error probability = α (e.g., 0.05) for upper tail

- 'Two-sided test at α = 0.05' could mean:
  (a) Allocate α/2 = 0.025 to each tail (but only upper tail is used) → f_crit = qf(0.975, k, df2)
  (b) Use α = 0.05 for the effective one-sided upper tail → f_crit = qf(0.95, k, df2)
